optionsEn: That counts as Tamattu' requiring Hady
According to the majority of jurists, because the Umrah was completed in Ramadan (before the Hajj months begin in Shawwal), they are NOT a Mutamatti' and do not owe Tamattu' Hady
They must repeat Umrah five times
explanationEn: Qur'an 2:196 specifies 'Whoever enjoys [Tamattu'] by performing Umrah BEFORE Hajj [in the Hajj months]'; since Ramadan precedes Shawwal, an Umrah in Ramadan does not constitute Hajj al-Tamattu'.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ mean when he told the people during the Farewell Hajj: 'Umrah has entered into Hajj until the Day of Judgment'?
optionsEn: That Hajj is only 7 laps around Safa
That performing Umrah during the Hajj season (as in Tamattu' and Qiran) is permanently lawful, overturning the pre-Islamic taboo against Umrah during Hajj months
That no one may visit Makkah in Ramadan
explanationEn: In pre-Islamic times, Arabs considered performing Umrah during the months of Hajj one of the gravest sins; the Prophet ﷺ interlocked his fingers to show Umrah is permanently lawful alongside Hajj.

questionEn: What did pre-Islamic Arabs say when refusing Umrah during the months of Hajj—a superstition abolished by the Prophet ﷺ?
optionsEn: 'When the wounds of the camels heal, the traces are erased, and Safar passes, then Umrah is lawful for whoever performs it'
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) narrated this exact pre-Islamic superstition that barred Umrah until Safar; Islam abolished it by validating Umrah year-round and in Hajj months.

questionEn: If a pilgrim is in a hurry or arrives late in Makkah on the morning of the 8th of Dhul-Hijjah, which Nusuk is easiest to adopt if they go straight to Mina?
optionsEn: Hajj al-Ifrad (or Qiran if intending both), heading straight to Mina without needing to complete a separate Umrah before the 8th
explanationEn: When time does not allow completing Umrah before departing for Mina/Arafah, entering Ihram for Hajj al-Ifrad (or Qiran) ensures the pilgrim reaches Arafah calmly on schedule.

questionEn: Which Miqat is located closest to Makkah among the five prophetic Mawaqit?
optionsEn: Qarn al-Manazil (~75–90 km east of Makkah)
explanationEn: Qarn al-Manazil (Al-Sayl al-Kabir) is the nearest of the five prophetic Mawaqit to Makkah, whereas Dhul-Hulayfah near Madinah is the farthest.
reference: Atlas of the Hajj Routes; Sahih al-Bukhari 1524

questionEn: What is the name of the mosque at Dhul-Hulayfah where pilgrims from Madinah wash, pray, and enter Ihram?
optionsEn: Masjid al-Shajarah (or Masjid al-Miqat at Abyar Ali)
explanationEn: Because the Prophet ﷺ rested under an acacia tree there before entering Ihram, the historic mosque at Dhul-Hulayfah is famously known as Masjid al-Shajarah.

questionEn: Which type of Ihram does NOT require a pilgrim who entered Makkah before the 8th to stay in Ihram on the 5th, 6th, and 7th of Dhul-Hijjah?
optionsEn: Hajj al-Tamattu' (once Umrah is completed on arrival, they remain out of Ihram until the 8th)
explanationEn: This relief between Umrah and the 8th of Dhul-Hijjah is one of the greatest practical mercies of Hajj al-Tamattu' for pilgrims arriving days or weeks early.

questionEn: If a pilgrim in Hajj al-Ifrad wishes to change into Tamattu' AFTER having already performed Tawaf al-Qudum and Sa'i, what happens?
optionsEn: If they did not bring a Hady, Hanbali jurists allow converting it to Umrah (Tamattu') by trimming hair and exiting Ihram, just as the Companions did on the Prophet's ﷺ order after Tawaf and Sa'i
It is strictly impossible in every school
explanationEn: The Companions had already done Tawaf and Sa'i in Makkah when the Prophet ﷺ ordered those without Hady to cut their hair and turn it into Umrah—demonstrating the ease of Tamattu'.

questionEn: What is the ruling on performing Tawaf al-Qudum (Arrival Tawaf) for a pilgrim performing Hajj al-Tamattu'?
optionsEn: They must perform Tawaf al-Qudum separately in addition to Umrah Tawaf
They do NOT perform a separate Tawaf al-Qudum; their Tawaf of Umrah upon arriving in Makkah fulfills their arrival greeting of the Kaaba
They perform Tawaf al-Qudum at Mina
They skip Tawaf completely until the 13th
explanationEn: Tawaf al-Qudum is a Sunnah specifically for the Mufrid and Qarin upon entering Makkah; the Mutamatti' performs Umrah Tawaf directly upon arrival.

questionEn: When a pilgrim performing Hajj al-Tamattu' puts on Ihram for Hajj on the 8th of Dhul-Hijjah in Makkah, should they perform a Tawaf before going to Mina?
optionsEn: Yes, it is an obligatory pillar
No, there is no Tawaf required when entering Hajj Ihram on the 8th in Tamattu'—they head directly to Mina
Only if they travel by camel
explanationEn: Jabir (RA) narrated that when the Companions re-entered Ihram for Hajj on Yawm al-Tarwiyah from Al-Abtah, they headed straight to Mina without performing an extra Tawaf first.

questionEn: What is the ruling on 'Idtiba' (exposing the right shoulder under the Rida) during Salah?
optionsEn: Obligatory in all five daily prayers
Not Sunnah during Salah—men should cover both shoulders when praying the two rakaat after Tawaf or any daily prayer
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ forbade praying with one shoulder uncovered when a garment is large enough to cover both (Sahih al-Bukhari 359); thus men pull the Rida over both shoulders right after finishing Tawaf.

questionEn: If a pilgrim lives in Jeddah and goes to Makkah intending Hajj al-Tamattu' (doing Umrah first in Dhul-Hijjah and then Hajj), does he owe the Tamattu' Hady sacrifice?
optionsEn: Yes, according to the majority of scholars, because Jeddah lies outside the Haram boundary (not 'Ahl al-Masjid al-Haram')
No, Jeddah is inside the Kaaba courtyard
Only if he stays in Mina
explanationEn: Most jurists interpret 'him whose family is not in the area of Al-Masjid al-Haram' (2:196) as residents of the Makkah Haram sanctuary (or within Qasr distance); Jeddah residents outside the Haram owe Hady for Tamattu'.

questionEn: What should a pilgrim do if they enter Ihram for Hajj from Makkah on the 8th of Dhul-Hijjah—should they make Ghusl first?
optionsEn: Yes, taking Ghusl, trimming nails if needed, and wearing clean Ihram sheets before Niyyah on the 8th is recommended Sunnah
Only if they didn't bathe in Ramadan
explanationEn: Just as at the Miqat, bathing and freshening up before assuming Hajj Ihram on Yawm al-Tarwiyah follows the Prophetic Sunnah of purity.

questionEn: Which group of travelers passing by sea through the Red Sea on a ship toward Jeddah used to enter Ihram when aligned with Al-Juhfah or Yalamlam?
optionsEn: Pilgrims arriving by sea from Egypt/North Africa (Al-Juhfah) or from Yemen/South Asia (Yalamlam)
explanationEn: Maritime pilgrims historically used the ship captain's navigation alignment with Al-Juhfah (northwest) or Yalamlam (south) to enter Ihram before docking at Jeddah.

questionEn: Can a man tie a knot in his Rida (upper Ihram sheet) at the chest or neck so it doesn't slip off?
optionsEn: Yes, tying the Rida is fine
Many scholars advise against tying or fastening the Rida in a knot around the neck (except securing the lower Izar with a belt/pin); tucking or folding it neatly over the shoulders is Sunnah
explanationEn: Scholars distinguish securing the lower Izar (necessary for modesty) from knotting/pinning the upper Rida like a sewn cloak; simply draping and folding the Rida neatly suffices.

questionEn: What is the linguistic meaning of 'Ihram' from the Arabic root h-r-m?
optionsEn: Entering a state of sacred inviolability in which previously lawful acts (like tailored dress, perfume, hunting) become prohibited
explanationEn: Ihram shares the root of 'Haram' (sacred/forbidden): by intending Hajj, the pilgrim places themselves inside a sacred boundary of heightened reverence.

questionEn: If a pilgrim is in Makkah for Umrah and decides AFTER finishing Umrah to stay for Hajj, what kind of Hajj are they performing?
optionsEn: Hajj al-Tamattu' (since they completed Umrah in the Hajj months and then perform Hajj in the same season)
explanationEn: Even if someone initially came only for Umrah in Shawwal or Dhul-Qi'dah and later stayed for Hajj, completing both in the same Hajj months places them in Tamattu'.

questionEn: What if a person passes the Miqat with NO intention of Hajj or Umrah (e.g., visiting relatives in Jeddah or business in Makkah), and later decides to perform Hajj?
optionsEn: They owe a sheep for crossing the Miqat
They must leave Saudi Arabia first
They owe no penalty at all and enter Ihram from wherever they are when they make the intention
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ specified the Mawaqit 'for them and for whoever passes them intending Hajj or Umrah'; one traveling without pilgrimage intent incurs no Miqat penalty.

questionEn: Which two phrases in the Talbiyah directly declare that all praise, blessings, and sovereignty belong exclusively to Allah?
explanationEn: Reciting 'Innal-hamda wan-ni'mata laka wal-mulk' reminds the pilgrim that their health, wealth, travel safety, and very opportunity to answer Allah's call are sheer gifts from Him.

questionEn: Should a pilgrim wear underwear (briefs/boxers) underneath the lower Izar while in Ihram (for men)?
optionsEn: No, stitched undergarments are prohibited for men in Ihram unless there is genuine medical necessity (in which case Fidyah applies)
explanationEn: Male pilgrims wear only the unstitched Izar below; stitched trousers or underwear are forbidden unless no Izar exists or medical necessity requires it.

questionEn: Can a woman wear stitched undergarments and ordinary modest clothing under her abaya/jilbab while in Ihram?
optionsEn: No, women also avoid all stitched clothes
Yes, women are permitted all normal stitched modest garments except the fitted niqab and gloves
Only white cotton is valid for women
explanationEn: Ibn Umar (RA) and scholarly consensus affirm that the prohibition of tailored/stitched clothes applies solely to men, not women.

questionEn: What is 'Raml' during Tawaf al-Qudum for men in Hajj al-Ifrad or Hajj al-Qiran?
optionsEn: Brisk walking with short, confident steps in the first three circuits around the Kaaba while keeping the right shoulder uncovered (Idtiba)
explanationEn: Raml is performed by men during the first 3 circuits of Tawaf al-Qudum (or Umrah Tawaf), followed by normal walking in the remaining 4 circuits.

questionEn: If a pilgrim is unable to perform Raml due to severe crowding or age/illness during Tawaf al-Qudum, what is the ruling?
optionsEn: They must repeat Tawaf at midnight
Their Tawaf is completely valid with zero penalty, as Raml is a Sunnah tied to ability and avoiding harm to others
explanationEn: Raml and Idtiba are Sunnah acts; if crowding prevents brisk walking without jostling or harming fellow pilgrims, walking calmly is strictly preferred.

questionEn: Which of the following is strictly prohibited for BOTH men and women while in the state of Ihram?
optionsEn: Applying perfume or scented oils to body or clothes
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ forbade pilgrims in Ihram from wearing any garment touched by saffron or wars perfume, and jurists agree applying fragrance after entering Ihram is prohibited for both genders.

questionEn: What is the Fidyah (expiation) prescribed in Surah Al-Baqarah 2:196 for a pilgrim in Ihram who must shave their head early due to illness or lice/scalp injury?
optionsEn: A choice of fasting 3 days, feeding 6 poor persons, or sacrificing a sheep (Fidyah al-Adha)
explanationEn: When Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah (RA) suffered from lice on his head during Hudaybiyyah, Allah revealed 2:196 allowing him to shave and pay Fidyah: fasting 3 days, feeding 6 needy people (half a sa' each), or offering a sheep.

questionEn: Which Companion's severe scalp ailment at Hudaybiyyah became the direct occasion for the revelation of the Fidyah options in Qur'an 2:196?
explanationEn: Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah (RA) came to the Prophet ﷺ with lice falling onto his face; the Prophet ﷺ ordered him to shave his head and explained the three equal choices of Fidyah.

questionEn: How much food per needy person is given if a pilgrim chooses the 'feeding six poor persons' option of Fidyah al-Adha?
optionsEn: Half a sa' (~1.5 kg) of staple grain/food per person (3 sa' total for 6 people)
explanationEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari 1815, the Prophet ﷺ told Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah (RA): 'Fast three days, or feed six poor people—half a sa' of food for each poor person—or slaughter a sheep.'

questionEn: What is the ruling on a male pilgrim wearing a hat, cap, turban, or pulling his Ihram sheet over his head while awake or asleep in Ihram?
optionsEn: Prohibited for men to cover the head directly with anything attached/resting on it, though shading from a distance (like an umbrella or tent roof) is fully permitted
explanationEn: When a man in Ihram died, the Prophet ﷺ instructed: 'Do not cover his head' (Sahih al-Bukhari 1265), while Umm al-Husayn (RA) saw Bilal and Usamah shading the Prophet ﷺ with a raised garment during Hajj.

questionEn: Is carrying an umbrella or riding inside a roofed bus/car permitted for a pilgrim in Ihram?
optionsEn: No, every vehicle roof violates Ihram
Yes, because the shade does not sit directly upon or adhere to the head
explanationEn: Authentic Sunnah shows Companions held a cloth aloft to shade the Prophet ﷺ as he moved toward Jamrat al-Aqabah; umbrellas, tents, and vehicle roofs are completely allowed.

questionEn: What is the ruling on clipping fingernails or toenails intentionally while in the state of Ihram?
optionsEn: Prohibited in Ihram (unless a nail breaks painfully, in which case trimming only the broken painful piece incurs no penalty)
explanationEn: Jurists agree trimming healthy nails in Ihram is prohibited (incurring Fidyah), whereas removing only a torn, painful jagged portion of a broken nail is excused without penalty.

questionEn: If a pilgrim in Ihram gently scratches their head or beard and a few loose hairs fall out unintentionally, do they owe a penalty?
optionsEn: No penalty—scholars including Ibn Taymiyyah and the majority agree unintentional falling of dead/loose hair carries no Fidyah
explanationEn: Aisha (RA) ruled that a pilgrim in Ihram may scratch their head gently; only deliberate cutting, shaving, or plucking of hair triggers Fidyah.

questionEn: What is the ruling on marriage proposals or conducting a marriage contract (Nikah) while in Ihram?
optionsEn: Invalid/prohibited—a person in Ihram may neither marry, give someone in marriage, nor propose marriage
Permitted if no perfume is used
explanationEn: Uthman ibn Affan (RA) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: 'A person in Ihram does not marry, nor give in marriage, nor propose.'

questionEn: What happens to a pilgrim's Hajj if spouses engage in marital intercourse BEFORE the first release from Ihram (Tahallul al-Awwal) on the 10th?
optionsEn: It corrupts (invalidates) that Hajj, yet they MUST still complete all remaining rites, slaughter a camel/badanah, and make up the Hajj the next year
They immediately go home without finishing
explanationEn: The Companions (Umar, Ali, Abu Hurayrah, Ibn Abbas) unanimously ruled that intercourse prior to Arafah/first Tahallul spoils the Hajj, obligates completing all remaining rituals, offering a Badanah (camel), and performing Qada Hajj the following year.

questionEn: What if marital intercourse occurs AFTER the first partial Tahallul (after stoning Aqabah and shaving on the 10th) but BEFORE Tawaf al-Ifadah?
optionsEn: Hajj is completely void and must be redone next year
The Hajj remains valid (does NOT become void), though the act is sinful and requires a compensatory Dam (a sheep; Hanafis say Badanah if before Ifadah) and renewing Ihram from Tan'im in some schools
explanationEn: Because the major pillar of Arafah and first Tahallul have already passed, jurists agree the Hajj is NOT invalidated after first Tahallul, though a Dam is owed for violating the remaining restriction.

questionEn: Which verse of Surah Al-Ma'idah strictly prohibits killing wild land game while in the state of Ihram?
explanationEn: Qur'an 5:95 warns: 'O you who believe, do not kill game while you are in the state of Ihram. And whoever among you kills it intentionally—the penalty is an equivalent from sacrificial animals...'

questionEn: Which type of hunting/fishing IS explicitly permitted for a pilgrim in Ihram according to Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:96?
optionsEn: Sea game (fish and marine catch) and its food
explanationEn: Qur'an 5:96 states: 'Lawful to you is game from the sea and its food as provision for you and the travelers, but forbidden to you is game from the land as long as you are in Ihram.'

questionEn: If a non-pilgrim hunts a wild animal and gifts its meat to a pilgrim in Ihram, may the pilgrim eat it?
optionsEn: Yes, provided the pilgrim did NOT hunt it, point to it, instruct it to be hunted, nor was it hunted specifically for them
explanationEn: When Abu Qatadah (RA)—who was NOT in Ihram—hunted a wild donkey and brought meat to his companions in Ihram, the Prophet ﷺ asked if any of them signaled or helped; when they said no, he told them: 'Eat what remains of it.'

questionEn: When Al-Sa'b ibn Jaththamah (RA) gifted a wild donkey he had hunted specifically for the Prophet ﷺ while the Prophet ﷺ was in Ihram, why did the Prophet ﷺ politely return it?
optionsEn: Because it was hunted specifically for him while he was in Ihram ('We are returning it only because we are in Ihram')
explanationEn: Distinguishing the Abu Qatadah case from Al-Sa'b's gift, jurists note game hunted specifically on behalf of a Muhrim is unlawful for the Muhrim to consume.

questionEn: Which five harmful creatures (Fawasiq) did the Prophet ﷺ permit a pilgrim to kill even inside the Haram sanctuary and while in Ihram?
optionsEn: Gazelle, pigeon, fox, hare, and sparrow
Camel, sheep, goat, cow, and horse
Eagle, deer, ostrich, hedgehog, and lizard
The crow, kite (bird of prey), scorpion, mouse/rat, and rabid/biting dog (plus venomous snakes)
explanationEn: Aisha and Ibn Umar (RA) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ named five harmful pests (fawasiq) that may be killed both outside and inside the Haram/Ihram to protect life and property.

questionEn: What is the penalty (Jaza' al-Sayd) in Qur'an 5:95 for a pilgrim in Ihram who intentionally kills a wild land animal like a gazelle or ostrich?
optionsEn: An equivalent domestic livestock animal judged by two just persons (e.g., camel for ostrich, goat for gazelle), or feeding the poor with its value, or fasting an equivalent number of days
explanationEn: Qur'an 5:95 sets out three graduated options determined by two upright judges: an equivalent livestock sacrifice delivered to the Kaaba's poor, feeding needy people, or fasting equivalent days.

questionEn: What is the ruling on a pilgrim in Ihram killing mosquitoes, ants, or flies that bite or land on them?
optionsEn: Insects that are not game animals may be brushed off or killed if harmful without Ihram hunting penalty (though avoiding unnecessary harm to harmless creatures in the Haram is good etiquette)
explanationEn: The prohibition of 'Sayd' applies to wild edible/hunted land animals, not biting insects or fleas—though scholars advise gently brushing away harmless ants rather than needlessly crushing them.

questionEn: Can a pilgrim in Ihram use unscented soap, unscented deodorant, or a toothbrush/miswak?
optionsEn: Yes—unscented hygiene products, brushing teeth, and using miswak are completely permitted in Ihram
explanationEn: Keeping clean and fresh without added perfume preserves health and dignity during crowded Hajj days; scented soaps/lotions should be avoided.

questionEn: What if a pilgrim in Ihram unintentionally puts on a shirt or uses perfumed soap out of forgetfulness or ignorance?
optionsEn: They must fly back to Miqat

According to many scholars (including Shafi'i, Hanbali, and Ibn Baz/Ibn Uthaymeen based on Qur'an 2:286), there is no sin and no Fidyah for genuine forgetfulness or ignorance, provided they remove it as soon as they remember
explanationEn: Allah forgives mistakes and forgetfulness (Qur'an 2:286; 33:5); upon realizing, the pilgrim immediately removes the shirt or washes off the scent without delay.

questionEn: What is the ruling on a pilgrim eating food naturally flavored with aromatic spices like cardamom, saffron, or cinnamon while in Ihram?
optionsEn: Cooked food flavored with spices loses its perfume-application status and is generally permitted (though avoiding raw/strong un-cooked saffron rubbed on hands is safer)
All spices are banned in Ihram
explanationEn: Classical jurists permit eating cooked food containing spices, though Hanafis note caution if uncooked aromatic saffron imparts clear scent/color—normal cooked meals are completely lawful.

questionEn: Why is uprooting wild trees, cutting natural green grass, or picking up lost valuables (other than to announce and return them) prohibited inside the Haram boundaries of Makkah—for BOTH pilgrims in Ihram and non-pilgrims?
optionsEn: Because the Prophet ﷺ declared Makkah permanently sacred (Haram) on the day of its Conquest until the Day of Judgment
Only during the month of Dhul-Hijjah
explanationEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari 1834, the Prophet ﷺ proclaimed: 'Allah made Makkah sacred the day He created the heavens and earth... its thorns are not cut, its game is not chased, and its lost property is not picked up except by one announcing it.'

questionEn: Which single sweet-smelling desert plant inside Makkah's Haram did Al-Abbas (RA) ask the Prophet ﷺ to exempt from the plant-cutting ban for use by blacksmiths and in homes?
explanationEn: Al-Abbas (RA) said: 'O Messenger of Allah, except Al-Idhkhir, for it is used by our blacksmiths and in our graves/houses.' The Prophet ﷺ immediately granted the exception: 'Except Al-Idhkhir.'

questionEn: Does touching the Kiswah (cloth covering of the Kaaba) or Maqam Ibrahim when heavily perfumed by mosque attendants cause a problem for a pilgrim in Ihram?
optionsEn: No problem, they should rub perfume all over their Ihram
Pilgrims in Ihram should avoid deliberately touching freshly perfumed spots of the Kaaba/Hajar al-Aswad so perfume does not transfer onto their hands and Ihram
explanationEn: Scholars remind pilgrims in Ihram to be mindful during Tawaf: if wet perfume has just been applied to the Black Stone or Kaaba corner, touching it deliberately transfers fragrance, so gesturing from afar ('Allahu Akbar') is safer and avoids crowding.

questionEn: Is a pilgrim in Ihram permitted to wear medical compression socks or normal tailored bandages if injured on the foot?
optionsEn: If medically necessary, wearing a bandage/splint is completely permitted; if a full tailored garment must be worn out of medical necessity, Fidyah al-Adha applies without sin
No medical care is allowed until the 13th
explanationEn: Islam prioritizes health and ease: wound dressings/bandages incur no Fidyah, and necessary fitted medical garments are permitted with Fidyah al-Adha (fast 3 days, feed 6, or sheep).

questionEn: Can a pilgrim in Ihram undergo cupping (Hijama) or have a necessary blood test/injection?
optionsEn: Yes, medical injections, blood draws, and Hijama are permitted in Ihram—so long as no hair is shaved unnecessarily without Fidyah
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ himself underwent Hijama while in Ihram at Lahy Jamal.

questionEn: What is the ruling on combing one's hair or beard vigorously while in Ihram?
optionsEn: Disliked/avoided if it risks pulling out hair, as pulling hair intentionally is prohibited in Ihram
explanationEn: Jurists advise running fingers gently if needed and avoiding tight-toothed combing that tugs and uproots hair during Ihram.

questionEn: When a pilgrim covers their sleeping body with a regular stitched blanket or duvet in a hotel or Mina tent, does that violate the rule against tailored clothing for men?
optionsEn: Yes, blankets are banned in Ihram
Yes, unless the blanket is torn
No, covering the torso and legs with a blanket while sleeping is permissible for men as long as the head remains uncovered
explanationEn: Tailored clothing prohibition applies to wearing clothes shaped for limbs (shirts/pants), not laying a blanket over the torso/legs while sleeping—so long as the male pilgrim keeps his head uncovered.

questionEn: May a male pilgrim in Ihram cover his FACE while sleeping (without covering the scalp/head), or what is the scholarly view?
optionsEn: The majority (Shafi'i, Hanbali) permit covering the face for men because the Prophetic prohibition specifies 'do not cover his head'; Hanafis and Malikis prohibit covering the face as well
Both head and face must be tightly wrapped
explanationEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari 1265, the Prophet ﷺ said regarding the deceased Muhrim: 'Do not cover his head' (some narrations in Muslim say 'nor his face', which is why Hanafis/Malikis prohibit both while Shafi'is/Hanbalis restrict it to the head).

questionEn: What is the ruling on a pilgrim looking in a mirror or using eye drops while in Ihram?
optionsEn: Both looking in a mirror and using unscented medical eye drops are completely permissible
Mirrors are only allowed after Mina
explanationEn: No authentic prohibition exists against mirrors or non-perfumed medical drops in Ihram.

questionEn: If a pilgrim is in Hajj al-Qiran or Hajj al-Ifrad and arrives in Makkah days before the 8th of Dhul-Hijjah, what is the Sunnah Tawaf upon entering Masjid al-Haram?
optionsEn: Tawaf al-Qudum (Arrival Tawaf), which is a Sunnah greeting to the Kaaba
explanationEn: Upon entering Makkah in Ifrad or Qiran, the pilgrim greets the Sacred House with Tawaf al-Qudum (7 circuits with Idtiba and Raml in the first 3 circuits for men).

questionEn: Can a pilgrim performing Hajj al-Ifrad or Hajj al-Qiran perform their Hajj Sa'i immediately AFTER Tawaf al-Qudum so they don't have to do Sa'i on the crowded 10th of Dhul-Hijjah?
optionsEn: No, Sa'i is never valid before Arafah
Yes, according to the majority (Shafi'i, Maliki, Hanbali), a Mufrid or Qarin may bring forward their Hajj Sa'i right after Tawaf al-Qudum—just as the Prophet ﷺ did
explanationEn: Because the Prophet ﷺ performed Qiran and did Tawaf al-Qudum followed by Sa'i upon reaching Makkah, he did NOT repeat Sa'i after Tawaf al-Ifadah on the 10th.

questionEn: Does performing Sa'i after Tawaf al-Qudum release a Mufrid or Qarin from Ihram before going to Arafah?
optionsEn: No! They do NOT cut hair and remain in Ihram until Yawm al-Nahr (10th Dhul-Hijjah)
Only if they give a sheep
explanationEn: Only the Mutamatti' cuts hair and exits Ihram after Umrah Sa'i; a Qarin or Mufrid who advances Sa'i after Tawaf al-Qudum stays in Ihram until stoning and shaving on the 10th.

questionEn: What is the ruling on performing a voluntary (Nafl) Tawaf while waiting in Makkah before the 8th of Dhul-Hijjah for a Mutamatti' who has already exited Ihram?
optionsEn: Highly recommended—and performed in regular clothes without Idtiba or Raml
explanationEn: A Mutamatti' out of Ihram may perform as many voluntary Tawafs in regular garments as they wish, praying two rakaat after each 7-circuit Tawaf.

questionEn: If a pilgrim violates a single Ihram prohibition multiple times (e.g., applying perfume three times on the same day before paying expiation) of the SAME type, how many Fidyahs are owed according to the Hanbali/majority reasoning?
optionsEn: One Fidyah covers repeated acts of the exact same category before expiation, whereas different categories (e.g., wearing a shirt AND clipping nails) incur separate Fidyahs
explanationEn: Jurists explain that repeated minor violations of one kind before expiation merge into a single Fidyah, while distinct violations (like shaving head + wearing sewn shirt) require separate Fidyahs.

questionEn: Where should a Fidyah sacrifice (Dam) for an Ihram violation or missed Wajib be slaughtered and distributed?
optionsEn: In the pilgrim's home country after returning
Anywhere in the world by telephone
Within the Haram sanctuary of Makkah (including Mina), distributed to the poor of the Haram
explanationEn: Qur'an 2:196 and 22:33 indicate that Hady and Dam sacrifices are brought to the Ancient House (within the Haram boundary) so the poor of Makkah benefit; whereas Fidyah al-Adha (fasting/feeding) may be done there or elsewhere (some schools require feeding in Haram).

questionEn: Can a pilgrim eat from a penalty sacrifice (Dam for a missed Wajib or Ihram violation), or is it strictly for the poor?
optionsEn: Unlike voluntary/Tamattu' Hady (from which eating is Sunnah), jurists rule a compensatory penalty Dam (for missed Wajib/violation) must go entirely to the poor—the pilgrim does NOT eat from it
The pilgrim must eat all of it alone
explanationEn: Scholars distinguish Hady al-Nusuk (Tamattu'/Qiran gratitude sacrifice, from which eating is Sunnah per 22:28) from Dam al-Jubran (expiation/penalty), which belongs wholly to the needy.

questionEn: What is the ruling on using a walking stick, wheelchair, or motorized scooter during Tawaf and Sa'i if one has difficulty walking?
optionsEn: Completely permissible and valid—the Prophet ﷺ himself performed Tawaf riding his camel so people could see and ask him questions
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) reported the Prophet ﷺ performed Tawaf riding a camel (Sahih al-Bukhari 1612) and Sa'i riding when crowds pressed; thus wheelchairs and mobility scooters are fully valid.

questionEn: During Tawaf al-Qudum, what must a pilgrim avoid touching or kissing if it is freshly perfumed with musk/oud?
optionsEn: The Black Stone (Al-Hajar al-Aswad) or Kaaba Kiswah if visibly wet with fragrance
explanationEn: Touching freshly perfumed stone/cloth transfers fragrance onto the pilgrim in Ihram; pointing with the hand while saying 'Allahu Akbar' fulfills the Sunnah gracefully without transferring perfume.

questionEn: What is the ruling on talking with companions or answering a phone call briefly while in Ihram?
optionsEn: Ihram requires total silence like a monk
Ordinary wholesome conversation is completely permissible, though avoiding idle chatter and quarreling (Jidal) is strongly commanded
explanationEn: Islam has no silent-vow restriction in Ihram; rather, speech should be truthful, gentle, and rich in dhikr, free of obscenity and angry arguments (Qur'an 2:197).

questionEn: May a pilgrim in Ihram wear a surgical face mask or medical respirator to protect against dust and respiratory illness in dense crowds?
optionsEn: Women should avoid fitted masks touching like a niqab unless medically needed (some scholars allow surgical masks for health necessity without penalty or with minimal concern, and men are permitted by the majority to cover mouth/nose for health)
All masks are strictly banned even in epidemics
explanationEn: Contemporary juristic councils permit hygienic/medical masks during Hajj to prevent contagion and respiratory harm, noting a surgical mask is not the prohibited tailored niqab meant for adornment/veil.
reference: International Islamic Fiqh Academy Resolutions; Fatawa Ibn Baz

questionEn: If a pilgrim wears tailored clothing (like pants or a shirt) ONLY for a few minutes and removes it immediately upon realizing they are in Ihram, do they owe a Dam?
optionsEn: No penalty if done out of forgetfulness or ignorance and removed immediately upon remembering
Yes, they must return to Miqat
explanationEn: Based on Qur'an 2:286 and Ya'la ibn Umayyah's narration of the man wearing a perfumed jubbah, the Prophet ﷺ told him to wash the perfume and take off the jubbah without imposing a Fidyah on the ignorant questioner.

questionEn: In the famous Hadith of Ya'la ibn Umayyah (RA), a bedouin came to the Prophet ﷺ at Al-Ji'ranah wearing a jubbah (cloak) stained with khaluq perfume—what did the Prophet ﷺ command him?
optionsEn: 'Wash off the trace of perfume thrice, take off your jubbah, and do in your Umrah as you do in your Hajj'
Keep the cloak on for seven days
explanationEn: This classic Hadith teaches both that tailored cloaks and perfume are forbidden in Ihram AND how mercifully the Prophet ﷺ corrected an earnest newcomer.

questionEn: During Hajj al-Qiran or Hajj al-Ifrad, if a pilgrim performs an optional Tawaf al-Qudum upon arriving in Makkah, when should they perform the Hajj Sa'i between Safa and Marwah?
optionsEn: Either immediately after Tawaf al-Qudum or after Tawaf al-Ifadah on the 10th of Dhul-Hijjah (performing it only once)
Mandatory twice: once after Tawaf al-Qudum and a second time after Tawaf al-Ifadah
Only on the 8th of Dhul-Hijjah in Mina before departing for Arafah
Only after Tawaf al-Wada immediately prior to leaving Makkah
explanationEn: A pilgrim performing Qiran or Ifrad needs only one Sa'i for their Hajj; they may advance it right after Tawaf al-Qudum (as the Prophet ﷺ and his companions who brought sacrificial animals did) or perform it after Tawaf al-Ifadah.

questionEn: What is the ruling on a pilgrim in Ihram getting a tooth extracted or a wound stitched if medically urgent?
optionsEn: Permissible with zero Fidyah, because medical necessity removes harm and dental work is not shaving head hair
Strictly forbidden until Dhul-Qi'dah next year
explanationEn: Urgent dental or surgical treatment (with unscented antiseptics) is fully allowed in Ihram and carries no penalty.

questionEn: If a pilgrim experiences a wet dream (nocturnal emission) while asleep in Ihram, does that invalidate their Hajj or require a Fidyah?
optionsEn: No—an involuntary dream carries zero sin, zero Fidyah, and does NOT spoil Ihram; the pilgrim simply performs Ghusl for major ritual purity
explanationEn: The pen is lifted from the sleeper; Ibn Abbas (RA) explicitly ruled that a nocturnal emission in Ihram only requires Ghusl before prayer/Tawaf, with no penalty.

questionEn: If a pilgrim is waiting in Mina or Arafah and needs to repair a torn sandal strap or sew a tear in their tent, does sewing violate Ihram?
optionsEn: Yes, touching a needle is forbidden
No—the ban is on wearing tailored garments shaped to body limbs, NOT on holding a needle to mend a bag, tent, or sandal strap
explanationEn: Many people confuse 'ghayr makhit' (untailored) with any act of sewing; mending a bag or belt does not violate Ihram at all.

questionEn: Is a pilgrim in Ihram allowed to carry a backpack with shoulder straps or a crossbody sling bag?
optionsEn: Only if made of palm leaves
Yes, carrying bags, satchels, or backpacks for water, Qur'an, and sandals is completely permissible
explanationEn: A backpack or waist bag is luggage, not a garment worn to cover the body, so it is universally permitted in Ihram.

questionEn: What is the ruling on a pilgrim in Ihram deliberately smelling strong perfume bottles or burning fragrant incense (bukhoor) directly to inhale its scent?
optionsEn: They should avoid deliberately inhaling concentrated perfume or applying bukhoor to their clothes/body; passing briefly by incidental scent in public is forgiven
explanationEn: While accidental whiffs of scent in crowds or mosques incur nothing, deliberately perfuming oneself or seeking out bukhoor smoke to fragrance one's garments violates Ihram etiquette.

questionEn: What if a pilgrim in Hajj al-Tamattu' forgets and leaves Makkah for Mina on the 8th STILL wearing normal stitched clothes without having re-entered Ihram?
optionsEn: They never need Ihram for Hajj
They must immediately return or stop, bathe/change into Ihram garments, and make the intention for Hajj Ihram right away (before Arafah passes)
explanationEn: Since Tamattu' exited the first Ihram after Umrah, entering Hajj requires a new Ihram intention; realizing it early allows immediate Ihram entry without missing Arafah.

questionEn: What is the ruling on 'Jidal' (angry arguing and disputing) during Hajj according to Qur'an 2:197?
optionsEn: Explicitly forbidden ('fa la rafatha wa la fusuqa wa la jidala fil-Hajj')—pilgrims must guard their tongues and show forbearance
explanationEn: Crowds, heat, and bus delays test every pilgrim's patience; remembering Allah's prohibition of jidal transforms friction into humility and forgiveness.

questionEn: In Tawaf al-Qudum, what must a pilgrim's state of ritual purity (Taharah) be according to the majority of jurists?
optionsEn: Wudu is never needed for Tawaf
Being free of major and minor ritual impurity (having Wudu), just like Salah—except without prohibition on speaking
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ told Aisha (RA): 'Do everything a pilgrim does except perform Tawaf around the House until you become pure,' and in another hadith compared Tawaf to prayer except Allah permitted speech in it.

questionEn: Which corner of the Kaaba marks BOTH the beginning and the end of every single circuit in Tawaf?
explanationEn: Every circuit of Tawaf starts in line with the Black Stone, keeps the Kaaba on the pilgrim's left, and concludes back at the Black Stone line.

questionEn: When passing the Black Stone during crowded Hajj days, what is the best Prophetic practice if kissing or touching it would require pushing or harming others?
optionsEn: Shove people aside to kiss it
Face it briefly, raise the right hand in gesture (Istilam from afar), and say 'Bismillahi Allahu Akbar' without harming anyone
Touch it with the left foot
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ advised Umar (RA): 'O Umar, you are a strong man; do not crowd around the Stone lest you harm the weak. If you find an opening, touch it; otherwise face it, say Takbir, and move on.'

questionEn: What special supplication did the Prophet ﷺ consistently recite between Al-Rukn al-Yamani (the Yemeni Corner) and Al-Hajar al-Aswad during every circuit of Tawaf?
optionsEn: 'Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanatan wa fil-akhirati hasanatan wa qina 'adhaban-nar' (Qur'an 2:201)
explanationEn: Abdullah ibn al-Sa'ib (RA) heard the Prophet ﷺ recite this comprehensive Qur'anic dua between the two southern corners in every circuit.

questionEn: Why must a pilgrim walk OUTSIDE the curved semicircular wall of Al-Hijr (Hateem / Hijr Isma'il) during every circuit of Tawaf?
optionsEn: Because the floor inside is slippery
Because it is a resting lounge
Because roughly six cubits of Al-Hijr were originally part of the Kaaba's foundations built by Ibrahim (AS); walking inside it misses part of the Kaaba
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ informed Aisha (RA) that Quraysh ran short of lawful funds when rebuilding the Kaaba, leaving part of its original footprint inside Al-Hijr; therefore Tawaf must circle outside it.

questionEn: What is the rule regarding touching Al-Rukn al-Shami and Al-Rukn al-Iraqi (the two northern corners of the Kaaba) during Tawaf?
optionsEn: We do NOT touch or kiss them—the Prophet ﷺ only touched/kissed Al-Hajar al-Aswad and touched Al-Rukn al-Yamani (because those two stand on the original foundations of Ibrahim AS)
They must be kissed seven times
They are patted with both feet
explanationEn: Ibn Umar (RA) explicitly observed that the Prophet ﷺ touched only the two Yemeni corners (Black Stone & Rukn al-Yamani), omitting the Iraqi and Syrian corners.

questionEn: After completing seven circuits of Tawaf, what Sunnah prayer does a pilgrim perform behind Maqam Ibrahim (or anywhere in Masjid al-Haram if crowded)?
optionsEn: Two rakaat reciting Surah Al-Kafirun in the first and Surah Al-Ikhlas in the second
explanationEn: Jabir (RA) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ recited 'Wattakhidhu min Maqami Ibrahima musalla' (2:125), prayed two light rakaat behind the Maqam, and read Qul ya ayyuhal-kafirun and Qul Huwallahu Ahad.

questionEn: What if the space directly behind Maqam Ibrahim is packed with Tawaf crowds—may a pilgrim pray the two Tawaf rakaat farther back in Masjid al-Haram?
optionsEn: No, it is only valid within 2 meters
They must push through the Mataf
Yes! Praying anywhere in Masjid al-Haram (keeping Maqam Ibrahim between you and the Kaaba if easy, or anywhere in the Haram) is completely valid and avoids blocking Tawaf
explanationEn: Blocking the active Tawaf path harms fellow worshippers; scholars emphasize stepping well clear of the Mataf flow to pray the two rakaat peacefully.

questionEn: If a pilgrim is in doubt during Tawaf whether they completed 5 or 6 circuits, what is the juristic rule?
optionsEn: Build upon the lower, certain number (5) and complete the remaining circuits
explanationEn: Just as in Salah, certainty is not overridden by doubt: one counts the lower assured number and completes to 7.

questionEn: What happens if an obligatory Fard prayer (Jama'ah) begins while a pilgrim is in the middle of Tawaf?
optionsEn: They stop Tawaf, pray in congregation with the Imam, and afterward resume Tawaf from the exact circuit/spot where they paused
They keep walking through the prayer rows
Their entire Tawaf is canceled and must restart from circuit 1
explanationEn: Stopping briefly for congregational Salah or renewing Wudu does not break Tawaf continuity according to the majority (Shafi'i, Hanafi, Hanbali); one resumes from where one stopped.

questionEn: Is Sa'i between Al-Safa and Al-Marwah 7 round-trips (14 legs) or 7 single lengths?
optionsEn: 7 single lengths: Safa→Marwah (1), Marwah→Safa (2), ..., ending at Marwah on lap 7
explanationEn: Going from Safa to Marwah is lap 1, returning Marwah to Safa is lap 2, and lap 7 concludes at Marwah (~450m per lap, ~3.15 km total).

questionEn: Which hill did the Prophet ﷺ climb first when beginning Sa'i, saying 'Abda'u bima bada'Allahu bih' (I begin with what Allah began with)?
explanationEn: Because Qur'an 2:158 mentions Al-Safa before Al-Marwah, the Prophet ﷺ ascended Al-Safa first, faced the Kaaba, proclaimed Tawhid and Takbir three times, and made long dua.

questionEn: What do the green fluorescent lights between Al-Safa and Al-Marwah mark today?
optionsEn: The valley bed (Batn al-Wadi) where Hajar (AS) hurried to keep sight of baby Isma'il, and where male pilgrims jog briskly (Sa'y al-Khabab)
explanationEn: Men jog briskly between the two green markers in every lap of Sa'i while women walk at a normal modest pace throughout.

questionEn: What is the ruling on having Wudu during Sa'i between Safa and Marwah?
optionsEn: Recommended (Mustahabb) for reward, though Sa'i remains valid even without Wudu (and even for a menstruating woman once her Tawaf was already completed)
explanationEn: Unlike Tawaf around the Kaaba, the Prophet ﷺ told Aisha (RA) when she menstruated to perform everything except Tawaf; scholars agree Wudu is Sunnah—not a validity condition—for Sa'i.

questionEn: Can a pilgrim in Ihram use a pain-relief balm or cream?
optionsEn: Yes, provided the cream/ointment is completely fragrance-free
explanationEn: Unscented medical ointments, petroleum jelly, or anti-chafing creams are widely allowed in Ihram to prevent blisters and heat rash.

questionEn: What is the ruling on taking medicine to temporarily delay menstruation so a female pilgrim can complete Tawaf al-Ifadah cleanly before her group's flight?
optionsEn: Permissible with medical consultation, provided it does not harm the woman's health
explanationEn: Classical and contemporary scholars permit safe medical delay of menses when needed to finish Tawaf before scheduled departure, provided a doctor confirms no harm.
reference: Fatawa Ibn Baz; Fatawa Ibn Uthaymeen

questionEn: If a pilgrim is in Ihram and passes through a public hall where incense or perfume lingers in the air, does that break their Ihram?
optionsEn: They must hold their breath for an hour
No, passive exposure to ambient scent carries zero penalty
explanationEn: Only intentional application or direct consumption/use of perfume as fragrance triggers Fidyah; smelling ambient scent while walking by incurs nothing.

questionEn: What is the ruling on a pilgrim in Ihram trimming a hangnail or peeling dead skin around a blister?
optionsEn: Removing loose dead skin or a painfully torn nail tip that causes harm is permissible with no penalty
explanationEn: Removing harm (daf' al-darar) is a core legal maxim in Islam; only cutting healthy nails or hair intentionally is barred.

questionEn: Why does the Shariah prohibit hunting and cutting wild vegetation in the Makkah Haram Sanctuary?
optionsEn: Because animals belonged to Quraysh kings
To make Makkah an ultimate sanctuary of peace and safety for humans, birds, beasts, and plants alike
explanationEn: Allah honored Makkah as 'Al-Balad al-Amin' (the Secure Sanctuary); extending protection even to doves, gazelles, and acacia trees teaches deep reverence for life.

questionEn: If a person inside the Makkah Haram accidentally kills a wild Haram pigeon, what did the majority of classical jurists (including Umar and Uthman RA) rule?
optionsEn: Compensatory charity (a sheep or its food value for the poor of the Haram) still applies to protect the sanctuary's wildlife
No charity may ever be given
explanationEn: Classical jurists treat harming Haram wildlife analogously to property liability: Umar, Uthman, and Ibn Abbas (RA) ruled that even unintentional killing of a Haram pigeon requires giving a sheep or its value to the poor.

questionEn: According to Ibn Abbas (RA) and classical jurists, what is the compensation (Jaza') historically ruled for killing a pigeon of the Makkah Haram sanctuary?
optionsEn: One sheep (or its charitable equivalent to the poor of the Haram)
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas, Uthman, and Umar (RA) ruled a sheep as the equivalent compensation for a pigeon of the Haram sanctuary.

questionEn: May a pilgrim in Ihram pluck gray hairs from their beard or trim their mustache while in Ihram?
optionsEn: Yes, mustache trimming is Sunnah in Ihram
No, removing any hair from head, beard, mustache, or body intentionally is prohibited in Ihram until Tahallul
Only gray hairs may be plucked
explanationEn: The prohibition on removing hair covers all body and facial hair equally during Ihram.

questionEn: How many hairs pulled or shaved deliberately trigger the full Fidyah al-Adha according to Hanbali/Shafi'i jurists?
optionsEn: Only if the entire head is bald
Three or more hairs (in Shafi'i/Hanbali fiqh; 1–2 hairs incur a smaller charity such as a mudd of food)
explanationEn: Shafi'i and Hanbali manuals specify 3 hairs (or 3 nails) trigger the full Fidyah al-Adha, whereas removing 1–2 incurs a smaller food charity (sadaqah).

questionEn: What is the ruling on a pilgrim in Ihram wearing a wedding ring, wristwatch, or medical ID bracelet?
optionsEn: Permissible—rings and watches are ornaments/instruments, not stitched clothing covering body parts
Allowed only on the right hand
explanationEn: Wearing a silver ring, watch, or Hajj ID wristband does not violate Ihram in any school.

questionEn: When a woman in Ihram washes her face or wipes her hair during Wudu, must she be careful not to pull out strands deliberately?
optionsEn: She cannot make Wudu with water
Yes, she wipes gently; if a stray strand falls naturally without intent to pluck, there is no sin or penalty
She owes a sheep for every drop
explanationEn: Aisha (RA) taught women to wash and comb gently if needed when pure, and unintentional shedding during Wudu or Ghusl carries zero blame.

questionEn: If a pilgrim performing Hajj al-Tamattu' forgot to cut or shave their hair after Umrah Sa'i and put on normal clothes, realizing it a day later, what should they do?
optionsEn: Immediately remove stitched clothes, cut/shave their hair to properly exit Umrah Ihram (with no penalty if out of ignorance/forgetfulness, or Fidyah per Hanafis)
explanationEn: Because exiting Umrah Ihram requires Halq or Taqsir, the pilgrim completes that step as soon as they remember, after which they are cleanly out of Umrah Ihram.

questionEn: What is the ruling on performing Tawaf on the upper floors or rooftop of Masjid al-Haram during peak Hajj seasons?
optionsEn: Invalid because it is above the Kaaba roof
Counts only as half a Tawaf
Completely valid—the entire vertical column of air above the Masjid al-Haram courtyard shares the ruling of the mosque
explanationEn: Scholarly consensus confirms Tawaf and Sa'i on the first, second, or rooftop floors of Masjid al-Haram are completely valid, easing congestion safely.

questionEn: When performing Tawaf al-Qudum, can a pilgrim recite the Qur'an silently or aloud softly, or only fixed booklets of dua?
optionsEn: Pilgrims may make any heartfelt dua, dhikr, or recite Qur'an; no specific rigid dua is mandated per circuit (aside from Sunnah 'Rabbana atina...' between Yemeni corner and Black Stone)
Qur'an recitation is banned in Tawaf
Only Arabic speakers may make dua
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ did not assign seven fixed duas for the seven circuits; praying from the heart in any language draws the pilgrim closest to Allah.

questionEn: What is the difference between 'Dam' (compensatory animal) and 'Hady' (pilgrimage sacrifice)?
optionsEn: Hady is the grateful Nusuk sacrifice offered in Tamattu', Qiran, or voluntarily (from which eating is Sunnah); Dam is a compensatory sacrifice required for missing a Wajib or violating an Ihram rule
Dam is only for Eid al-Fitr
explanationEn: Understanding the distinction helps pilgrims know when they may eat from the meat (Hady of Tamattu'/Qiran) versus when all meat goes to the poor (penalty Dam).

questionEn: If a pilgrim is in Ihram and uses a perfume-free sunscreen lotion in the desert sun of Arafah, is it permissible?
optionsEn: Yes, fragrance-free sunscreen is completely permissible and protects skin health
explanationEn: The Ihram restriction targets fragrance (teeb), not medical or protective unscented skin lotions.

questionEn: What should a male pilgrim do if his lower Izar (waist cloth) accidentally slips loose during a crowded Tawaf?
optionsEn: Quickly fasten or re-wrap it modestly right away; brief accidental exposure does not invalidate Tawaf if corrected immediately
explanationEn: Securing the Izar firmly with a belt prevents exposure; if it momentarily slips and is fixed immediately, the Tawaf continues validly.

questionEn: Can a pilgrim in Ihram wear prescription sunglasses?
optionsEn: Yes, sunglasses and prescription glasses are fully permitted for both men and women in Ihram
No, glasses count as covering the head
explanationEn: Glasses sit on the nose/ears without covering the scalp or functioning as a face-veil, so wearing them in bright sunlight is fully permitted.

questionEn: What is the ruling on a pilgrim in Ihram sleeping inside an air-conditioned tent or hotel room?
optionsEn: Completely permissible—seeking lawful shelter and comfort from extreme heat is not prohibited in Ihram
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ himself used a leather tent pitched for him at Namirah on the Day of Arafah and stayed in tents in Mina; modern cooled tents fulfill the same purpose safely.

questionEn: If a pilgrim is in Ihram and uses a scented wet wipe mistakenly to clean their hands, what should they do?
optionsEn: Keep wiping their face with it
Wash the scented area promptly with water upon realizing and switch to unscented wipes
explanationEn: Washing off inadvertent perfume immediately follows the Prophet's ﷺ guidance to the man at Al-Ji'ranah.

questionEn: Which of the following acts is NOT an Ihram prohibition?
optionsEn: Changing into a freshly washed pair of white Ihram sheets
explanationEn: Replacing dusty Ihram sheets with clean ones is fully lawful and encourages personal hygiene.

questionEn: What is the ruling on kissing or hugging one's spouse with desire while in the state of Ihram before Tahallul?
optionsEn: Prohibited as part of 'Rafath' (2:197) and foreplay leading to intimacy; if it occurs without emission/intercourse it is sinful and requires repentance (and Dam in some schools), though Hajj is not voided unless intercourse occurs
explanationEn: Qur'an 2:197 forbids 'Rafath', encompassing sexual talk and physical foreplay; spouses maintain affectionate respect without sensual intimacy until after exiting Ihram.

questionEn: If a pilgrim breaks Wudu during Tawaf al-Qudum, what must they do according to the majority of jurists?
optionsEn: Stop Tawaf, go renew Wudu, and return to complete Tawaf (either resuming from the interrupted circuit in Hanbali/Hanafi views or restarting circuits depending on school)
explanationEn: Most jurists require Wudu for Tawaf; renewing Wudu immediately preserves validity, with Hanafis/Hanbalis permitting resumption from where one stopped (while Shafi'is also have a view on restarting).

questionEn: During Tawaf, why must the pilgrim keep the Kaaba on their LEFT side?
optionsEn: It is optional; clockwise is equally valid
Because counter-clockwise with the Kaaba on the left is the unbroken Sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ ('Take your rituals from me') and prerequisite for Tawaf validity
explanationEn: Jabir (RA) described the Prophet's ﷺ Tawaf starting at the Black Stone with the House on his left; circling with the House on the right renders Tawaf invalid.

questionEn: What is the 'Multazam' near the Kaaba where pilgrims often supplicate after Tawaf?
optionsEn: The roughly two-meter wall space of the Kaaba between the Black Stone and the Kaaba's door
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas and Amr ibn al-'As (RA) reported standing at Al-Multazam—between the Black Stone and the Kaaba's door—clinging humbly in dua; during dense crowds, making dua facing it from afar avoids crushing others.

questionEn: What does 'Istilam' mean during Tawaf around the Kaaba?
optionsEn: Greeting/touching or kissing the Black Stone (or gesturing toward it with the right hand saying 'Allahu Akbar' when crowded) and touching Al-Rukn al-Yamani
explanationEn: Istilam denotes honoring the Black Stone at the start of each circuit—kissing it if clear, touching with the hand/staff, or simply pointing from a distance without pushing.

questionEn: What is the Sunnah action if a pilgrim is able to reach Al-Rukn al-Yamani easily without crowding?
optionsEn: Touch it gently with the right hand without kissing it and without gesturing from afar if unreachable
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ touched Al-Rukn al-Yamani with his hand without kissing it; if crowded, scholars advise passing smoothly while continuing 'Rabbana atina...' without pointing at it.

questionEn: Why did Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) address the Black Stone directly when kissing it during his caliphate?
optionsEn: He believed the stone answered prayers
To teach the Ummah pure Tawhid: 'I know you are only a stone that can neither harm nor benefit; had I not seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ kiss you, I would not have kissed you'
explanationEn: Umar's (RA) famous declaration preserves Tawaf as pure obedience to Allah and His Messenger ﷺ, free of any stone-worship superstition.

questionEn: Are women recommended to perform Raml (brisk jogging) in Tawaf or jogging between the green lights in Sa'i?
optionsEn: No—Ibn Umar (RA) and scholarly consensus affirm women walk at their normal dignified pace throughout both Tawaf and Sa'i, and keep both shoulders fully covered
explanationEn: Neither Idtiba nor Raml nor jogging between green markers applies to women, preserving modesty and ease.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about the virtue of Zamzam water when drunk after Tawaf?
optionsEn: 'The water of Zamzam is for whatever purpose it is drunk for'—blessed food that nourishes and heals with sincere dua
'It may only be drunk once a decade'
explanationEn: Jabir (RA) narrated the Prophet's ﷺ saying 'Ma'u Zamzama lima shuriba lah' (Zamzam water is for whatever it is drunk for), and Abu Dharr (RA) survived 30 days on Zamzam alone.

questionEn: What happens if a pilgrim in Hajj al-Qiran performs Umrah Tawaf and Sa'i on arrival—must they perform ANOTHER Tawaf (Tawaf al-Ifadah) on or after the 10th of Dhul-Hijjah?
optionsEn: No, arrival Tawaf suffices for Hajj
Yes! Tawaf al-Qudum does NOT replace Tawaf al-Ifadah; Tawaf al-Ifadah after standing at Arafah is an indispensable Rukn (pillar) of Hajj
Only if they stayed in Madinah
explanationEn: Every pilgrim—Mufrid, Qarin, and Mutamatti'—must perform Tawaf al-Ifadah on or after Yawm al-Nahr; arrival Tawaf cannot substitute for it.

questionEn: Is it permissible for a pilgrim in Ihram to swim or immerse themselves in water to cool down (without diving to hunt or using scented bath products)?
optionsEn: Yes, Ibn Umar (RA) and Companions permitted bathing or immersing in water while in Ihram, taking care not to scrub hair aggressively
explanationEn: Immersing in water or showering with unscented water is lawful in Ihram, as confirmed by Companions' narrations in Sahih al-Bukhari.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ originally command Raml (brisk striding in the first 3 circuits) during Umrat al-Qada in 7 AH, and why did it remain Sunnah?
optionsEn: To display the Muslims' vigor and resilience before onlookers of Quraysh who claimed Madinah's fever had weakened them; Umar (RA) affirmed we preserve this Sunnah even after Islam prevailed
explanationEn: Umar (RA) asked why we still perform Raml after Quraysh perished, then concluded: 'It is a Sunnah the Messenger of Allah ﷺ established, and we will never abandon it.'

questionEn: If a pilgrim is in Makkah before the 8th of Dhul-Hijjah and wants to make the best use of their days while staying out of Ihram (in Tamattu'), what worship is most meritorious?
optionsEn: Praying all five daily prayers in congregation in Masjid al-Haram (each worth 100,000 prayers), reciting Qur'an, Tawaf, and resting well for the intense 5 days ahead
Exhausting oneself with 15 extra Umrahs in 3 days
explanationEn: Scholars encourage praying in Masjid al-Haram, performing voluntary Tawaf (which is unique to Makkah), and conserving physical strength for Mina, Arafah, and Muzdalifah.

questionEn: Before heading out to Mina on the 8th of Dhul-Hijjah, why is planning hydration, light footwear, and patience essential alongside spiritual preparation?
optionsEn: Because water is prohibited in Mina
Because Hajj blends physical endurance with intense worship; caring for one's body as an Amanah helps the pilgrim focus on dhikr, dua, and serving fellow pilgrims
explanationEn: Prophetic wisdom balances devotion and bodily care ('Your body has a right over you'); staying hydrated and calm prevents heat exhaustion and helps maintain humility.

questionEn: Why is the 8th day of Dhul-Hijjah historically named 'Yawm al-Tarwiyah'?
optionsEn: Because pilgrims stayed up telling stories
Because pilgrims watered their mounts and filled water skins in Makkah before setting out to Mina and Arafah where water was once scarce
Because camels were sold on that day
explanationEn: Tarwiyah comes from riyy (quenching thirst / drawing water); in ancient times Mina and Arafah lacked abundant wells, so pilgrims prepared water supplies on the 8th.
reference: Fath al-Bari by Ibn Hajar; Lisan al-Arab

questionEn: On the 8th of Dhul-Hijjah, which pilgrims must newly put on Ihram garments and declare the intention for Hajj?
optionsEn: Tamattu' pilgrims (who exited Ihram after completing their Umrah) and residents of Makkah intending Hajj
explanationEn: Mufrids and Qarins are already in Ihram continuously from their Miqat; Tamattu' pilgrims and Makkah residents enter Ihram for Hajj on the morning of the 8th.

questionEn: At what time of day on the 8th of Dhul-Hijjah did the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions depart from Makkah toward Mina?
optionsEn: In the morning (Duha time, after sunrise) so they reached Mina before Dhuhr
explanationEn: Jabir (RA) narrated that on Yawm al-Tarwiyah the Companions headed out to Mina in the forenoon (Duha), entering Hajj Ihram and praying Dhuhr in Mina.

questionEn: What is the exact sequence of five daily prayers that the Prophet ﷺ led in Mina on the 8th of Dhul-Hijjah and dawn of the 9th?
optionsEn: Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha (of the 8th) and Fajr (of the 9th)
Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, and Isha of the 8th
explanationEn: Anas and Jabir (RA) reported the Prophet ﷺ arrived in Mina before Dhuhr on the 8th and prayed Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha, and Fajr of Arafah morning there before departing after sunrise.

questionEn: How are the four-rakaat prayers (Dhuhr, Asr, and Isha) performed by pilgrims in Mina on the 8th of Dhul-Hijjah?
optionsEn: Shortened to 2 rakaat AND combined together
Shortened to 2 rakaat (Qasr), prayed each in its own prescribed time WITHOUT combining them
Prayed in full 4 rakaat and combined
explanationEn: Unlike Arafah (Dhuhr+Asr combined) and Muzdalifah (Maghrib+Isha combined), in Mina the Sunnah is Qasr (shortening 4-rakaat prayers to 2) without Jam' (combining)—each prayer offered in its own time.

questionEn: How many rakaat are Maghrib and Fajr prayed in Mina?
optionsEn: Maghrib remains 3 rakaat and Fajr remains 2 rakaat (since Qasr applies only to 4-rakaat prayers)
explanationEn: In Islamic law, travel shortening applies strictly to four-rakaat prayers (Dhuhr, Asr, Isha); Maghrib (3) and Fajr (2) are never shortened.

questionEn: Do permanent residents of Makkah also shorten their prayers (Qasr) in Mina, Arafah, and Muzdalifah according to the Prophet's ﷺ practice?
optionsEn: No, Makkah residents pray 4 rakaat everywhere
Only if they travel to Madinah first

Opinions differ: Hanbalis/some scholars hold Makkah residents pray Qasr behind the Imam because Qasr in Hajj is a Nusuk sunnah (or follow the Imam), while Shafi'is/Hanafis view Makkah residents inside Mina/Makkah limits as non-travelers who complete 4 rakaat after the Imam's salam
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ led everyone—including Makkah residents—in 2 rakaat at Mina and Arafah without telling Makkans to stand and complete 4 (though Shafi'is/Hanafis deduce they complete 4 based on travel rules, while Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah held Qasr in Hajj applies to all pilgrims).

questionEn: What is the juristic status of staying in Mina on the 8th of Dhul-Hijjah and sleeping there on the night before Arafah?
optionsEn: A strongly emphasized Sunnah (not a pillar or Wajib according to the vast majority, though following it earns great reward and aligns with the Prophet's ﷺ example)
The supreme pillar of Hajj without which Hajj is void
explanationEn: Staying in Mina on the 8th (Yawm al-Tarwiyah) and its night is a stressed Sunnah; if a tour group moves directly to Arafah early due to logistics, the Hajj remains completely valid with zero Dam.

questionEn: Where geographically is the valley of Mina situated relative to Masjid al-Haram and Muzdalifah?
optionsEn: East of Makkah, lying inside the Haram boundary between Makkah (Jamrat al-Aqabah) and Muzdalifah (Wadi Muhassir)
explanationEn: Mina is a narrow valley roughly 5–7 km east of Masjid al-Haram, bounded on the Makkah side by Jamrat al-Aqabah and on the east by Wadi Muhassir.

questionEn: Why must pilgrims verify the official boundary signs of Mina before pitching or settling into tents for the Tashreeq nights?
optionsEn: Because outside Mina belongs to Yemen
Because due to overcrowding some modern camps spill over into Muzdalifah (e.g., Wadi Muhassir); only tents inside Mina's legal borders fulfill the Mina Mabit
Because Mina has no boundary markers
explanationEn: Scholars clarify that if Mina's tent capacity is completely full and authorities assign camps extending into Muzdalifah, the pilgrim tries to stay within Mina if possible, and if no space remains in Mina, staying in the adjacent assigned camp carries no sin or Dam.

questionEn: Which famous mosque stands in the valley of Mina near the base of the southern mountain?
explanationEn: Masjid al-Khayf (meaning the slope of a mountain above a valley) is where the Prophet ﷺ camped and led prayers in Mina.

questionEn: What is the linguistic meaning of 'Al-Khayf' in 'Masjid al-Khayf'?
optionsEn: The gently sloping ground descending from a mountain above the floodbed of a valley
explanationEn: In Arabic, 'khayf' refers to the elevated slope at the foot of a mountain rising safely above the valley torrent—exactly where Masjid al-Khayf stands in Mina.

questionEn: What is the Sunnah regarding reciting Takbir ('Allahu Akbar') alongside the Talbiyah on the morning of the 9th of Dhul-Hijjah when moving from Mina toward Arafah?
optionsEn: Both Talbiyah and Takbir are forbidden
Companions recited both Talbiyah and Takbir openly without anyone objecting to the other
explanationEn: Anas (RA) narrated: 'We set out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from Mina to Arafah; some of us were reciting the Talbiyah and some of us were saying Takbir, and none objected to the other.'

questionEn: When did the Prophet ﷺ depart from Mina for Arafah on the morning of the 9th of Dhul-Hijjah?
optionsEn: After praying Fajr at Mina and waiting until the sun had risen cleanly above the horizon
explanationEn: Jabir (RA) narrated: 'He remained in Mina until the sun rose, then proceeded toward Arafah.'

questionEn: If a pilgrim is resting inside Mina on the 8th of Dhul-Hijjah, should they spend the time exclusively sleeping or engage in worship?
optionsEn: Spend the entire night standing without sleeping at all
Balance quiet rest for Arafah's endurance with Talbiyah, Qur'an recitation, dhikr, dua, and serving tent-mates kindly
explanationEn: Yawm al-Tarwiyah prepares both body and soul for the great standing at Arafah; adequate sleep alongside dhikr and camaraderie prevents exhaustion on the 9th.

questionEn: Which two forms of worship are the primary Sunnah prayers maintained in Mina alongside the shortened Fard prayers?
optionsEn: The Sunnah of Fajr (2 rakaat before Fajr) and Witr at night (as the Prophet ﷺ never left them even while traveling)
All twelve Rawatib Sunnahs after Dhuhr, Maghrib, and Isha
explanationEn: While traveling, the Prophet ﷺ regularly omitted the post-Dhuhr/Maghrib/Isha Rawatib Sunnahs, yet consistently prayed the 2 Sunnah rakaat of Fajr and Witr (plus Duha when appropriate).

questionEn: What is the linguistic origin of the name 'Mina' according to classical Arabic historians?
optionsEn: From 'tamanna' (wishing/hoping for Allah's mercy) or from 'mana' (where sacrificial blood is poured on Yawm al-Nahr)
From a Roman governor named Mina
explanationEn: Historians mention two roots: because Adam (AS) wished for Paradise there, or because sacrificial animals (hady) are shed there in devotion to Allah.

questionEn: If a pilgrim is already staying in Mina on the 8th of Dhul-Hijjah, are they permitted to leave Mina briefly for an urgent need before returning, or is the 8th flexible?
optionsEn: Leaving for one minute voids Hajj
Since staying in Mina on the 8th is a Sunnah rather than a Wajib, attending to a genuine necessity carries no penalty at all
explanationEn: Even during the Wajib nights of Tashreeq (11th–12th), leaving temporarily for a necessity before returning is allowed; on the Sunnah 8th day there is certainly no penalty.

questionEn: When a Tamattu' pilgrim enters Ihram for Hajj in their Makkah hotel on the morning of the 8th, which phrase of intention/Talbiyah do they utter?
explanationEn: Having already completed Umrah earlier, on the 8th the Mutamatti' enters Ihram strictly for Hajj with 'Labbayka Hajjan.'

questionEn: What special care should a Tamattu' pilgrim take regarding personal grooming on the morning of the 8th BEFORE saying 'Labbayka Hajjan'?
optionsEn: Clip nails, trim excess hair, bathe, and apply perfume to the body BEFORE putting on Ihram intention, because all Ihram prohibitions immediately resume once Niyyah is made
Pour perfume onto the white sheets
explanationEn: Taking advantage of the final hour before Hajj Ihram to freshen up, bathe, and trim nails avoids accidental violations in Mina and Arafah.

questionEn: What is the ruling on performing Hajj Ihram on the night of the 7th of Dhul-Hijjah (a few hours early) for Tamattu' pilgrims whose buses depart late at night toward Mina?
optionsEn: Completely valid and permissible, as the entire month of Dhul-Hijjah up to the 9th is within the Hajj Ihram window
explanationEn: Because modern transport often moves pilgrims into Mina tents on the night of the 7th–8th, entering Hajj Ihram before boarding the bus is completely valid.

questionEn: If a pilgrim is in Mina on the 8th of Dhul-Hijjah and is not feeling well, may they skip walking to Masjid al-Khayf and pray in their tent?
optionsEn: No, prayers inside tents are invalid
They must walk even if fainting
Yes! Praying in congregation inside one's Mina camp is completely valid and protects health for Arafah
Only Fajr can be prayed in a tent
explanationEn: All of Mina is inside the Haram sanctuary; praying in one's tent with fellow pilgrims protects weak or distant pilgrims from heat stroke or getting lost.

questionEn: During the 8th of Dhul-Hijjah in Mina, why did the Companions and later righteous scholars encourage sharing food and tent space cheerfully?
optionsEn: Because restaurants are closed by law
Because Mina's cramped quarters are a real-life workshop in brotherhood, humility, and patience ('feeding food and gentle speech')
explanationEn: Tight quarters test patience; sharing water, space, and smiles embodies the Prophetic definition of Hajj Mabrur.

questionEn: Which mountain overlooks Masjid al-Khayf in Mina, where revelation of Surah Al-Mursalat occurred during one of the Prophet's ﷺ journeys?
optionsEn: A cave in Mina near Mount Thabir / Masjid al-Khayf (narrated by Ibn Mas'ud RA: 'While we were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in a cave at Mina, Al-Mursalat was revealed to him')
explanationEn: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (RA) famously recounted receiving Surah Al-Mursalat directly from the Prophet's ﷺ lips while sheltered in a cave at Mina.

questionEn: Why is it important NOT to combine Dhuhr and Asr, or Maghrib and Isha, while resting in Mina on the 8th of Dhul-Hijjah?
optionsEn: Combining is banned for travelers everywhere
Because the Prophet ﷺ remained settled in his Mina camp all day on the 8th and prayed every prayer shortened at its individual time—reserving combining for the travel push at Arafah and Muzdalifah
Because there is no Adhan in Mina
explanationEn: Following the Prophet's ﷺ exact distinction—Qasr without Jam' while stationary in Mina, versus Qasr with Jam' at Arafah and Muzdalifah—preserves the Sunnah of Yawm al-Tarwiyah.

questionEn: Which two Prophets' legacy is deeply tied to Mina's valleys and hills?
optionsEn: Ibrahim and Isma'il (AS), through Ibrahim's readiness to sacrifice and his rejection of Shaytan's temptations along Mina
explanationEn: Mina stands as the living monument to Prophet Ibrahim's (AS) total submission to Allah's command and his family's steadfast faith.

questionEn: What is the rule if a pilgrim decides to spend the 8th of Dhul-Hijjah in Makkah (due to medical disability or group schedule) and travels straight to Arafah on the morning of the 9th?
optionsEn: Their Hajj is completely valid with zero penalty, though they missed the Sunnah virtue of Yawm al-Tarwiyah in Mina
explanationEn: Jurists agree that staying in Mina on the 8th is Sunnah Mu'akkadah (not Wajib); going directly to Arafah for valid reasons leaves Hajj intact without Dam.

questionEn: Which Surah's opening verses about 'the ten nights' (Wal-Fajr, wa layalin 'ashr) do Ibn Abbas and the majority of commentators identify with the first ten days/nights of Dhul-Hijjah?
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Ibn Kathir explain 'wa layalin 'ashr' in Surah Al-Fajr refers to the blessed first ten nights of Dhul-Hijjah culminating in Arafah and Eid.

questionEn: What special Takbir (Takbir al-Muqayyad) is traditionally recommended to begin at Fajr of the Day of Arafah (9th Dhul-Hijjah) for non-pilgrims, and after Dhuhr of Yawm al-Nahr for pilgrims?
optionsEn: Takbir al-Tashreeq after obligatory prayers ('Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, la ilaha illallah...')
explanationEn: Pilgrims continue reciting the Talbiyah until stoning Jamrat al-Aqabah on the 10th, after which their post-prayer Takbirat al-Tashreeq continue through Asr of the 13th.

questionEn: Is there any restriction on walking versus riding from Makkah to Mina on the 8th of Dhul-Hijjah?
optionsEn: Both walking and riding (bus, train, car) are fully permissible; the Prophet ﷺ rode his she-camel Al-Qaswa'
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ rode Al-Qaswa' throughout Mina, Arafah, and Muzdalifah so crowds could see him and conserve energy for worship.

questionEn: What was the name of the Prophet's ﷺ faithful she-camel that he rode during the Farewell Hajj?
explanationEn: Al-Qaswa' carried the Prophet ﷺ during the Hijrah, the Conquest, and throughout the Farewell Hajj—including while he delivered the Arafah Khutbah.

questionEn: During the 8th of Dhul-Hijjah in Mina, can a pilgrim perform Qiyam al-Layl (night prayer) and Witr inside their tent?
optionsEn: Yes, Qiyam and Witr at night in Mina are blessed Sunnahs, provided the pilgrim also gets sufficient sleep to stay alert on the Day of Arafah
Night prayer is prohibited in Mina
Only Maghrib is prayed at night
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ never abandoned Witr even while traveling; balancing modest night prayer with restful sleep prepares the heart for Arafah.

questionEn: Which direction do pilgrims travel when leaving Makkah on the morning of the 8th toward Mina, Arafah, and Muzdalifah?
optionsEn: East/Southeast along the sacred mountain corridor (Makkah → Mina → Muzdalifah → Arafah)
explanationEn: Mina (~6 km east), Muzdalifah (~10 km east), and Arafah (~20 km east-southeast of Makkah) form a straight eastern spiritual corridor.

questionEn: If a pilgrim is in Mina on the 8th of Dhul-Hijjah and accidentally drinks water containing a tiny mint leaf or lemon slice, does that violate Ihram?
optionsEn: Yes, mint is a perfume requiring a sheep
No, edible flavorings in food and drink (like mint, lemon, or tea) are completely lawful and are not prohibited fragrances
explanationEn: Mint tea, lemon water, and normal food ingredients are nutrition, not perfume applied to body or garments.

questionEn: What should a pilgrim do with their personal luggage and extra stitched clothes when heading to Mina on the 8th?
optionsEn: Leave everything uncovered on the street
Leave heavy bags safely in Makkah storage/hotel and carry only a light daypack with essentials (ID, water, umbrella, sandals, spare Ihram, snacks, medications)
explanationEn: Practical preparation prevents lost belongings and unnecessary strain when moving in huge crowds between Mina, Arafah, and Muzdalifah.

questionEn: How many days in total do the core Hajj rites in Mina, Arafah, and Muzdalifah span?
optionsEn: Five to six days (8th through 12th or 13th of Dhul-Hijjah)
explanationEn: From 8th Dhul-Hijjah (Tarwiyah) to 12th (Nafar Awwal) or 13th (Nafar Thani) spans 5 or 6 sacred days.

questionEn: What does the unified sea of white tents in Mina symbolize spiritually for the global Ummah?
optionsEn: A single egalitarian camp where millions from every race, language, and economic status dwell side-by-side under Allah's hospitality
explanationEn: Mina strips away palaces and class barriers so kings and laborers share simple tents as equal guests of Al-Rahman.

questionEn: If a pilgrim is praying inside Mina on the 8th and misses the tent's congregational Dhuhr prayer due to arriving late, how should they pray?
optionsEn: Pray Dhuhr shortened to 2 rakaat (with companions if available or individually) within its time before Asr
explanationEn: Every traveler in Mina still prays Dhuhr shortened to 2 rakaat even if praying later in a smaller group before Asr enters.

questionEn: Does a resident of Mina itself (if someone happened to reside permanently in Mina) shorten prayers during Hajj, or how do scholars address 'Qasr as a ritual of Hajj'?
optionsEn: Nobody ever shortens prayers in Mina

Hanafi, Shafi'i, and Maliki schools tie Qasr to travel distance (excluding local Makkans), while many Hanbalis and Ibn Taymiyyah treat Qasr in Mina/Arafah/Muzdalifah as a rite of Hajj for all pilgrims
explanationEn: Ibn Umar (RA) reported the Prophet ﷺ shortened at Mina, Abu Bakr shortened, Umar shortened, and Uthman shortened early in his caliphate before praying 4 later when residents settled—reflecting the classic juristic discussion.

questionEn: What did Uthman ibn Affan (RA) explain when questioned why he prayed 4 rakaat in Mina later in his caliphate instead of 2?
optionsEn: He had married in Makkah (or considered himself a resident / wanted newly arrived bedouins not to think Dhuhr was permanently 2 rakaat), while Ibn Mas'ud (RA) still preferred praying 2 following the Prophet ﷺ
explanationEn: Sahih al-Bukhari and Muslim record Ibn Mas'ud's famous saying 'I prayed two rakaat with the Prophet ﷺ, Abu Bakr, and Umar' while respectfully praying four behind Caliph Uthman to preserve unity ('Disagreement is evil').

questionEn: What profound lesson in Muslim unity did Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (RA) demonstrate when he prayed 4 rakaat behind Caliph Uthman (RA) in Mina despite believing 2 rakaat was Sunnah?
optionsEn: That preserving unity behind the Imam ('Al-khilafu sharr' — division is evil) outweighs insisting on personal preference in secondary matters
That Uthman never met the Prophet
explanationEn: Ibn Mas'ud's (RA) humility—following the Imam even when holding another juristic opinion—remains a timeless model for pilgrims in crowded Hajj camps.

questionEn: If a pilgrim is in Mina on the 8th of Dhul-Hijjah and hears the Adhan of Maghrib, should they combine Maghrib and Isha right then?
optionsEn: No—on the 8th in Mina, pray Maghrib (3 rakaat) at Maghrib time and Isha (2 rakaat) at Isha time separately
explanationEn: Combining Maghrib and Isha applies specifically on the night of the 9th–10th in Muzdalifah, not on the 8th in Mina.

questionEn: Which two Companions did the Prophet ﷺ send ahead or assign roles to during the departure to Mina and Arafah?
optionsEn: Companions like Bilal and Usamah ibn Zayd (RA) who walked beside his camel shading him, and Al-Fadl ibn Abbas (RA) riding behind him from Muzdalifah
explanationEn: Younger Companions like Usamah and Al-Fadl ibn Abbas (RA) served closely beside the Prophet ﷺ throughout the Hajj stations, transmitting priceless eyewitness details.

questionEn: Can a pilgrim who has an elderly or frail companion stay in Makkah on the night of the 8th and join them at Arafah on the morning of the 9th?
optionsEn: Yes, caring for the weak and avoiding unnecessary crowd stress before Arafah is wise and incurs zero penalty
No, it voids both pilgrims' Hajj
explanationEn: Because the 8th in Mina is a Sunnah and Arafah on the 9th is the supreme pillar ('Al-Hajju Arafah'), preserving strength for Arafah takes clear priority when needed.

questionEn: When leaving Mina after Fajr on the 9th of Dhul-Hijjah, what should be on the pilgrim's tongue as they head toward Arafah?
optionsEn: Continuous Talbiyah, Takbir, Tahlil, and heartfelt supplication asking Allah for acceptance at Arafah
explanationEn: Buses and walking paths to Arafah can take hours; turning transit delays into Talbiyah and Takbir mirrors the Companions' joyful march.

questionEn: Where did the Prophet ﷺ pitch his wool/leather tent on the 9th of Dhul-Hijjah BEFORE noon (Zawal) while waiting to enter Arafah?
optionsEn: At Namirah (just outside the western boundary of Arafah)
explanationEn: Jabir (RA) narrated: 'He found the dome-tent pitched for him at Namirah, so he alighted there until the sun passed its zenith (Zawal).'

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ rest at Namirah until Zawal (noon) on the 9th before moving into the valley of Uranah and then Arafah?
optionsEn: Because Arafah was closed until midnight
To wait for the time of Dhuhr and the formal commencement of the Day of Arafah standing after Zawal
explanationEn: Resting calmly in the shade at Namirah until midday preserved energy so he could deliver the Arafah Khutbah, lead Dhuhr and Asr combined, and then stand in uninterrupted dua until sunset.
