optionsEn: Right before the sun rose (after bright dawn glowed), differing deliberately from the pagans who used to wait until the sun shone on Mount Thabir
explanationEn: In pre-Islamic times, polytheists shouted 'Ashriq Thabir kayma nughir!' and refused to leave until sunrise; the Prophet ﷺ departed BEFORE sunrise to distinguish Islamic worship from pagan custom.

questionEn: What was the pre-Islamic pagan slogan at Muzdalifah—'Ashriq Thabir kayma nughir'—that the Prophet ﷺ deliberately opposed by departing before sunrise?
optionsEn: 'Shine upon Mount Thabir (so we may rush onward)!'
explanationEn: Umar (RA) recalled that pagans waited until sunlight struck Mount Thabir before moving; the Prophet ﷺ deliberately left Muzdalifah before sunrise.

questionEn: What is the prescribed size of each pebble used for stoning the Jamarat (Hasa al-Khadhf)?
optionsEn: The size of a human fist
Small, roughly the size of a chickpea or fava bean / hazelnut (slightly larger than a lentil, able to be flicked between thumb and forefinger)
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) collected pebbles for the Prophet ﷺ; holding them in his palm, the Prophet ﷺ said: 'With the likes of these throw! And beware of extremism (ghuluww) in religion, for those before you were destroyed by extremism.'

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ warn 'Beware of extremism (ghuluww) in religion' specifically when holding the tiny Jamarat pebbles?
optionsEn: Because some people imagine larger rocks, shoes, or angry shouting make stoning 'stronger' against Shaytan—whereas true devotion is humble obedience to exact Prophetic limits
Because he wanted people to throw boulders
explanationEn: Throwing huge stones or shoes violates the Sunnah and endangers fellow pilgrims; small chickpea-sized pebbles affirm disciplined submission.

questionEn: Is it Sunnah or required to wash the Jamarat pebbles in water or Zamzam before throwing them?
optionsEn: Obligatory to wash them seven times
Neither required nor Sunnah—ordinary clean dry pebbles picked from the ground are used directly without washing
explanationEn: Neither the Prophet ﷺ nor his Companions ever washed pebbles before Rami; if a pebble has visible filth, simply pick a clean pebble.

questionEn: How many pebbles does a pilgrim need specifically for Yawm al-Nahr (10th Dhul-Hijjah) alone, vs for the entire Hajj?
optionsEn: 7 pebbles on the 10th (for Jamrat al-Aqabah), and either 49 total (for Nafar Awwal leaving on 12th) or 70 total (staying through 13th)—plus a few extra spares in case one drops
explanationEn: Keeping 7 pebbles ready for Eid morning—or gathering 49/70 plus a handful of spares in Muzdalifah—keeps you prepared (any extra pebbles may be picked later in Mina too).

questionEn: Must ALL 49 or 70 pebbles be collected strictly in Muzdalifah, or is collecting only the first 7 (or picking later pebbles in Mina) also valid?
optionsEn: Only Muzdalifah pebbles work; Mina pebbles are void
They must be imported from Madinah
Pebbles must be picked while fasting
Collecting all pebbles from Muzdalifah OR picking only 7 in Muzdalifah and the rest in Mina is completely valid—the Prophet ﷺ only asked Ibn Abbas for 7 pebbles in the morning near Aqabah/Muzdalifah
explanationEn: The Prophet's ﷺ own 7 pebbles for Eid morning were gathered by Ibn Abbas (RA) around Muzdalifah/on the route ('Pick up pebbles for me'); any clean pebbles outside the Jamarat basin are valid.

questionEn: Why do scholars advise NOT picking up previously thrown pebbles from inside the Jamarat basin itself?
optionsEn: To avoid dangerous crowding inside the basin area, and because jurists (such as Hanbalis) consider pebbles already used in an obligatory rite unsuitable to reuse (while clean ground pebbles elsewhere in Mina/Muzdalifah are clean and abundant)
Because basin stones turn into glass
Because they are guarded by angels
explanationEn: Reaching into the stone basin risks injury and reuses cast stones; collecting fresh pebbles in Muzdalifah or clean roadside gravel in Mina is safe and sound.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ do when passing through the valley of Wadi Muhassir between Muzdalifah and Mina on the morning of the 10th?
optionsEn: He stopped to sleep there for 3 hours
He urged his mount to move briskly across Wadi Muhassir because it was the place where Allah punished Abraha's army of the Elephant
explanationEn: Just as the Prophet ﷺ hurried past Al-Hijr (Thamud's ruins) out of awe of Allah's punishment, he quickened his pace through Wadi Muhassir.

questionEn: Which two Companions rode behind the Prophet ﷺ at different legs of the journey—one from Arafah to Muzdalifah, the other from Muzdalifah to Mina?
optionsEn: Usamah ibn Zayd (Arafah → Muzdalifah) and Al-Fadl ibn Abbas (Muzdalifah → Mina)
explanationEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari, Usamah (RA) narrated the Arafah-to-Muzdalifah ride, while Al-Fadl ibn Abbas (RA) narrated the Muzdalifah-to-Mina ride when a woman from Khath'am asked about Hajj for her elderly father.

questionEn: What touching pastoral moment occurred while Al-Fadl ibn Abbas (RA) was riding behind the Prophet ﷺ from Muzdalifah to Mina?
optionsEn: When a young woman from Khath'am asked about proxy Hajj for her father and Al-Fadl looked at her, the Prophet ﷺ gently turned Al-Fadl's chin away twice with his hand to protect modesty while patiently answering her question
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ combined protective modesty—gently turning his young cousin's gaze away without harsh shaming—with clear juristic guidance for the earnest daughter.

questionEn: If a pilgrim is in traffic leaving Arafah and does NOT arrive in Muzdalifah until 2:30 AM (after midnight, but before Fajr), how do they pray Maghrib and Isha?
optionsEn: Pray Maghrib (3) and shortened Isha (2) immediately upon arrival (or earlier on the road if Fajr threatens to enter before reaching Muzdalifah!), never letting Isha pass past Fajr
Combine them with Fajr after sunrise
explanationEn: No prayer may ever be delayed past its valid boundary (Fajr for Isha); if traffic stalls until 4:00 AM, step aside safely or pray in the bus before Fajr enters.
reference: Fatawa Ibn Baz; Fatawa Ibn Uthaymeen

questionEn: Is there any restriction on spreading a thin sleeping mat or cardboard sheet on the ground in Muzdalifah while sleeping under the stars?
optionsEn: Yes, pilgrims must lie on bare gravel
No restriction—using a light sleeping mat, inflatable pad, and blanket (keeping a man's head uncovered) is completely permissible and keeps pilgrims comfortable
explanationEn: Muzdalifah has open paved/gravel zones with toilet and misting facilities; a simple mat protects your back from pebbles without violating Ihram.

questionEn: Why does sleeping under the open sky in Muzdalifah leave such a deep impression on pilgrims from all walks of life?
optionsEn: Because it is a camping contest
Because billionaires, scholars, and villagers lie side-by-side on simple mats under the same night sky—visibly stripping away ego before Allah
explanationEn: No VIP pavilions separate believers on the ground of Muzdalifah; every soul rests equally on the dust of the Haram.

questionEn: What is the minimum stay at Muzdalifah required if someone is NOT among the weak/excused, according to the Hanbali and Shafi'i vs Maliki/Hanafi schools?
optionsEn: Just driving past at 80 km/h without stopping

Majority (Shafi'i, Hanbali) require being present past midnight (at least a portion of the second half of the night); Hanafis specify standing between Fajr and sunrise; Malikis require descending long enough to pray and rest—so staying until after Fajr follows ALL schools safely!
explanationEn: Healthy pilgrims who pray Maghrib/Isha, sleep until Fajr, pray Fajr at Mash'ar al-Haram, and depart before sunrise fulfill the conditions of EVERY juristic school without exception.

questionEn: If a pilgrim is in a bus that drives straight through Muzdalifah without stopping at all because the driver lost his way or traffic didn't allow stopping, what is the ruling?
optionsEn: If they were healthy and able to stop or walk back yet left Muzdalifah completely without staying, a Dam applies according to the majority (unless genuinely forced/unable in a locked transit situation according to some scholars)
explanationEn: Because staying at Muzdalifah is Wajib (except for valid excuse/inability), pilgrims should coordinate with group guides so buses drop them inside Muzdalifah's marked perimeter.

questionEn: Can a pilgrim pray Witr in Muzdalifah on the night of the 9th–10th?
optionsEn: No, Witr is prohibited in Muzdalifah
Yes! The Prophet ﷺ never abandoned Witr while traveling; one may pray Witr right after combined Maghrib/Isha before sleeping, or right before Fajr
explanationEn: Praying 1 or 3 rakaat of Witr before sleeping (after combined Isha) secures your Witr cleanly before waking up for early Fajr.

questionEn: Which direction do pilgrims face when standing in supplication at Al-Mash'ar al-Haram after praying Fajr in Muzdalifah?
explanationEn: Jabir (RA) narrated: 'He rode Al-Qaswa' until he came to Al-Mash'ar al-Haram, faced the Qiblah, supplicated to Allah, proclaimed His greatness (Takbir), His Oneness (Tahlil), and stood until the sky was very bright.'

questionEn: Why must pilgrims be careful NOT to walk into traffic lanes or sleep right on paved bus roads in Muzdalifah?
optionsEn: Only cars may be in Muzdalifah
Because pebbles are prohibited near roads
Because thousands of buses enter and exit Muzdalifah in darkness; sleeping in designated pedestrian zones keeps everyone safe from fatal accidents
explanationEn: Preserving life is a sacred duty in Shariah; use designated fenced pedestrian areas and keep reflective/high-visibility bags tidy out of walkways.

questionEn: What is the approximate distance between Arafah and Muzdalifah?
explanationEn: Muzdalifah sits roughly halfway between Arafah (~8–10 km to its east) and Mina (~4–5 km to its west).

questionEn: If a pilgrim is walking from Arafah to Muzdalifah on the night of the 9th, how long does the walk typically take along the illuminated pedestrian pathway?
optionsEn: Around 2 to 3 hours at a steady, gentle pace (often faster than buses in heavy gridlock)
explanationEn: Many healthy pilgrims enjoy walking the wide, lit, mist-cooled pedestrian routes from Arafah to Muzdalifah while reciting Talbiyah together.

questionEn: What should a pilgrim do if they wake up in Muzdalifah and discover they slept past the Fajr Adhan by a few minutes (still well before sunrise)?
optionsEn: Make Wudu immediately, pray Fajr (2 rakaat), make dua at Mash'ar al-Haram until just before sunrise, and move calmly toward Mina
explanationEn: Any time between true Fajr and sunrise remains valid for Fajr prayer; simply pray calmly and do not forget your dua before sunrise.

questionEn: What if someone forgets to collect pebbles in Muzdalifah before boarding the metro/bus to Mina?
optionsEn: They must walk back to Arafah
No problem at all—simply pick up 7 clean small pebbles anywhere along the safe ground in Mina before reaching Jamrat al-Aqabah
explanationEn: Picking pebbles in Muzdalifah is a matter of convenience and following Ibn Abbas's example, not a condition for Rami's validity.

questionEn: How does Surah Al-Baqarah 2:198 remind pilgrims of their former state of ignorance when commanding remembrance at Al-Mash'ar al-Haram?
optionsEn: 'And remember Him as He has guided you, for indeed you were before that among those astray (ad-dallin)'
explanationEn: Gratitude for guidance ('kama hadakum') turns the dawn of Muzdalifah into a moment of deep thankfulness for Islam itself.

questionEn: When a pilgrim combines Maghrib and Isha in Muzdalifah, how many rakaat are prayed in total?
optionsEn: 5 rakaat total (3 for Maghrib + 2 shortened for Isha)
explanationEn: Maghrib is never shortened (always 3 rakaat), while Isha is shortened from 4 to 2 rakaat—totaling 5 rakaat across the two combined prayers.

questionEn: Who led the combined Maghrib and Isha in Muzdalifah when the Prophet ﷺ stopped there—did he wait for all stragglers or pray promptly upon arriving?
optionsEn: He prayed promptly upon dismounting at Muzdalifah so everyone could rest early
explanationEn: Praying without needless delay gives tired pilgrims maximum sleep before the strenuous day of Yawm al-Nahr.

questionEn: Which direction do pilgrims look to verify they are inside Muzdalifah's boundaries rather than still in Arafah or already inside Wadi Muhassir?
optionsEn: Check the tall boundary signs reading 'Start of Muzdalifah' and 'End of Muzdalifah' along every road and walkway
explanationEn: All three plains (Arafah, Muzdalifah, Mina) are clearly signposted at their borders so pilgrims never camp outside the intended zone by mistake.

questionEn: If an excused woman or elderly person leaves Muzdalifah after midnight, do they need to pay a Dam for departing before Fajr?
optionsEn: No Dam at all—the Prophet ﷺ explicitly permitted the weak, women, and caretakers to leave after half the night/moonset
explanationEn: Prophetic dispensation (rukhsah) removes both sin and financial penalty for excused pilgrims leaving after midnight.

questionEn: Can healthy, strong men who are NOT caring for weak, elderly, or female family members leave Muzdalifah before midnight without excuse?
optionsEn: Yes, leaving at 9:00 PM is better
No—healthy unexcused pilgrims should remain in Muzdalifah until after Fajr and Mash'ar al-Haram dua; leaving before midnight without excuse violates the Wajib Mabit
Only if they drive sports cars
explanationEn: Following the Prophet's ﷺ stay until bright dawn after Fajr preserves the full Sunnah and Wajib of Muzdalifah for able-bodied pilgrims.

questionEn: What is the Sunnah regarding the Adhan and Iqamah when praying Fajr in Muzdalifah?
optionsEn: One Adhan and one Iqamah (just like every normal Fajr prayer), prayed early as soon as true dawn clearly appears
explanationEn: Unlike the two Iqamahs of combined prayers, Fajr is an independent prayer offered with its regular Adhan and Iqamah.

questionEn: Can a pilgrim collect pebbles in a small clean cloth pouch or zip-bag in Muzdalifah to avoid losing them while walking to Mina?
optionsEn: No, bags are forbidden in Ihram
Pebbles must be held in the mouth
Yes, a small cloth drawstring pouch or plastic bag is practical and completely permitted
explanationEn: Keeping 7 or 49 pebbles neatly in a pouch prevents dropping them in crowds or spilling them in pockets.

questionEn: Why should pilgrims avoid gathering pebbles that are coated in asphalt, glass shards, or oversized stones?
optionsEn: Because small smooth natural pebbles (~chickpea/hazelnut size) match the Prophetic description and cannot injure fellow pilgrims at the Jamarat
explanationEn: Safety and adherence to the Sunnah size ('hasa al-khadhf') prevent dangerous projectiles at the Jamarat levels.

questionEn: What happens to the 3 daily habits during Muzdalifah's morning departure: should pilgrims rush ahead to beat crowds to the Jamarat, or walk steadily?
optionsEn: Walk steadily with patience and mercy, remembering Jamrat al-Aqabah's window remains open all day and night on the 10th
explanationEn: Knowing that stoning on the 10th is valid throughout the day (and night for those delayed) eliminates reckless rushing.

questionEn: Which Surah's story of 'The Companions of the Elephant' (Ashab al-Fil) occurred right next to Muzdalifah's border at Wadi Muhassir?
explanationEn: Abraha's elephant refused to advance toward the Kaaba near Wadi Muhassir between Mina and Muzdalifah, where birds carrying baked clay struck his army (Qur'an 105).

questionEn: When leaving Muzdalifah for Mina on the 10th, what is the Talbiyah status along the walk?
optionsEn: Continues right along the road through Wadi Muhassir until reaching Jamrat al-Aqabah and throwing the very first pebble
explanationEn: Al-Fadl ibn Abbas (RA) confirmed: 'The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not stop reciting the Talbiyah until he stoned Jamrat al-Aqabah.'

questionEn: What is the ruling if a pilgrim arrives at Muzdalifah very late at night and accidentally forgets to pray Maghrib/Isha before falling asleep until Fajr?
optionsEn: Upon waking, immediately pray the missed Maghrib (3) and Isha (2) in order, then pray Fajr (2), repenting for oversleeping without alarm/precaution
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ taught: 'Whoever forgets a prayer or sleeps through it, its expiation is to pray it as soon as he remembers it'—always maintaining the sequence Maghrib → Isha → Fajr.

questionEn: If a pilgrim is accompanying an elderly mother who leaves Muzdalifah after midnight, does the healthy caretaker owe a Dam for leaving early with her?
optionsEn: No! Caretakers and family members accompanying the weak/women/elderly share the exact same Prophetic dispensation—just as Ibn Abbas (RA) accompanied his mother and family
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) was young and strong, yet the Prophet ﷺ sent him ahead with the weak of his family so they would not be stranded alone.

questionEn: What special dua or dhikr is recorded at Al-Mash'ar al-Haram after Fajr in Muzdalifah?
optionsEn: Facing the Qiblah with raised hands, reciting Takbir ('Allahu Akbar'), Tahlil ('La ilaha illallah'), Tahmid ('Alhamdulillah'), and asking Allah for acceptance, forgiveness, and Jannah
explanationEn: Following Jabir's (RA) narration, standing humbly with raised hands after Fajr until golden daylight honors the command of Qur'an 2:198.

questionEn: Is there any restriction on eating breakfast or drinking tea/coffee in Muzdalifah after Fajr before walking to Mina?
optionsEn: Fasting is mandatory on the 10th morning
Eating a light breakfast after Fajr in Muzdalifah is completely lawful (and wise, since fasting on Eid al-Adha 10th Dhul-Hijjah is strictly forbidden!)
explanationEn: The 10th of Dhul-Hijjah is Eid al-Adha—a day on which fasting is forbidden in Islam; nourishing yourself before the long walk to Jamarat and Makkah prevents fainting.

questionEn: Why is the night of Muzdalifah NOT meant for staying up all night in supererogatory night prayers (Qiyam) at the expense of rest?
optionsEn: Because the Prophet ﷺ himself lay down and slept through the night until Fajr so he would have peak energy for Yawm al-Nahr's demanding rites
Because night prayer is haram in Muzdalifah
Because angels prohibit dhikr at night
explanationEn: Following the Prophet's ﷺ wisdom—resting through Muzdalifah's night after Isha/Witr—guards against exhaustion during stoning, Tawaf al-Ifadah, and Sa'i.

questionEn: What is the ruling if a pilgrim loses their group in the dark crowd of Muzdalifah?
optionsEn: Stay calmly in a well-lit pedestrian zone, use their Nusuk/group ID card or phone meeting point, pray Fajr at Mash'ar al-Haram, and rejoin the group at their Mina camp after sunrise
explanationEn: Since every pilgrim's Mina camp number is printed on their wristband/ID card, staying calm until morning makes rejoining straightforward.

questionEn: Did the Prophet ﷺ deliver a sermon (Khutbah) at Muzdalifah after Fajr?
optionsEn: No—after Fajr he went straight to standing in personal dua, Takbir, and Tahlil at Al-Mash'ar al-Haram until bright dawn, then rode on to Mina
He prayed Eid prayer at Muzdalifah
explanationEn: Also notable: pilgrims do NOT perform the two-rakaat Salat al-Eid on the 10th of Dhul-Hijjah; their morning begins with Fajr, Mash'ar al-Haram dua, and moving to Jamrat al-Aqabah.

questionEn: Do pilgrims performing Hajj pray the two-rakaat Eid al-Adha prayer (Salat al-Eid) in Mina or Muzdalifah on the morning of the 10th?
optionsEn: Yes, it is the main pillar of the 10th
Yes, at 7:00 AM inside Masjid al-Khayf
No! Following the Prophet's ﷺ Sunnah, pilgrims in Hajj do NOT pray Salat al-Eid on the 10th; they proceed directly to Jamrat al-Aqabah, Hady, Halq/Taqsir, and Tawaf al-Ifadah
explanationEn: Neither the Prophet ﷺ nor his Companions prayed Salat al-Eid during Hajj; instead, their Eid celebration consists of the noble rites of Yawm al-Nahr.

questionEn: If a pilgrim happens to be inside Masjid al-Haram early on the 10th morning and the Imam is leading Salat al-Eid there, may they join it?
optionsEn: Yes, joining an ongoing mosque Eid congregation if one happens to be in Makkah then is permissible as voluntary good, though pilgrims are not required to seek out Eid prayer
They must run out of the mosque
explanationEn: While Eid prayer is not prescribed for pilgrims in Mina/Muzdalifah, praying behind the Haram Imam if present at that moment is valid.

questionEn: What is the role of 'Masjid al-Mash'ar al-Haram' standing inside Muzdalifah today?
optionsEn: It marks the site of Arafah
It marks the historic Quzah mound inside Muzdalifah where the Prophet ﷺ prayed Fajr and stood in dawn dua
explanationEn: Built near the site of Quzah mound in central Muzdalifah, its towering minarets help pilgrims orient toward the Qiblah during dawn dua.

questionEn: Which of the three stations—Mina, Muzdalifah, or Arafah—has NO permanent tent city pitched over its open valley?
optionsEn: Muzdalifah, which remains an open valley plain where pilgrims rest under the night sky
All three are enclosed indoor stadiums
explanationEn: Mina has permanent fireproof white tents and Arafah has vast seasonal camps, while Muzdalifah preserves the simple open-air humility of resting beneath the stars.

questionEn: If a pilgrim is traveling on foot from Muzdalifah to Jamrat al-Aqabah on Eid morning, roughly how far is the walk?
optionsEn: About 4 to 7 kilometers depending on where one slept in Muzdalifah, reaching Jamrat al-Aqabah at the far western end of Mina
explanationEn: Remembering that Jamrat al-Aqabah sits at the western (Makkah-side) edge of Mina helps pilgrims pace their hydration and steps comfortably.

questionEn: When collecting pebbles in Muzdalifah, how can one tell if a small stone is too large?
optionsEn: If it is significantly bigger than a hazelnut/chickpea—closer to a golf ball or larger—discard it and pick smaller pebble-sized stones
Only stones over 500 grams are right
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) showed pebbles roughly the size of a date-stone or chickpea ('mithla hasa al-khadhf')—small enough to hold 7 easily in one closed palm.

questionEn: What is the ruling on picking pebbles from a decorative landscaped rock bed or breaking off chunks from concrete curbs in Muzdalifah?
optionsEn: Never damage public structures or paved curbs; simply gather natural loose pebbles off clean sandy/gravel ground
explanationEn: Destroying public infrastructure or breaking stones off walls is both unsafe and disrespectful to Allah's sanctuary; loose gravel is plentiful.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ say 'All of Jam' (Muzdalifah) is a place of standing, except Wadi Muhassir'?
optionsEn: Because Wadi Muhassir has no sky
Because Wadi Muhassir belongs to Madinah
So pilgrims wouldn't fight over crowding right onto the small mound of Quzah itself, while ensuring they stay inside Muzdalifah proper rather than Wadi Muhassir
explanationEn: Just like his words at Arafah ('All of Arafah is a standing place, stay clear of Uranah'), this Prophetic clarity eases crowding while preserving exact geographic boundaries.

questionEn: When a pilgrim combines Maghrib and Isha in Muzdalifah (Jam' Ta'khir), should they recite aloud (Jahri) in the first two rakaat of Maghrib and both rakaat of Isha?
optionsEn: Yes! When praying in congregation (or aloud individually), Maghrib's first 2 rakaat and Isha's 2 rakaat retain their normal audible Qur'an recitation
explanationEn: Shortening Isha to 2 rakaat and combining it with Maghrib keeps both prayers' nighttime audible recitation intact.

questionEn: What is the ruling if a pilgrim already prayed Maghrib on the road before reaching Muzdalifah because they feared missing its time or out of confusion, and then reaches Muzdalifah at Isha time?
optionsEn: Their Maghrib is valid; upon reaching Muzdalifah they simply pray shortened Isha (2 rakaat) and stay overnight in Muzdalifah with zero penalty
They must repeat Maghrib five times
explanationEn: Delaying Maghrib to combine at Muzdalifah is Sunnah, not a condition for Hajj validity; praying Maghrib earlier does not invalidate anything.

questionEn: Which pillar of Islam's daily discipline is beautifully highlighted in Muzdalifah when the Prophet ﷺ prayed Fajr at its earliest dawn light (Taghlis)?
optionsEn: Eagerness for Salah at the front of its prescribed window so worship flows cleanly into dawn remembrance
explanationEn: Praying Fajr right at its first clear dawn gave the Prophet ﷺ maximum time for heartfelt dua before sunrise.

questionEn: If a pilgrim is on medication that causes frequent urination during the night in Muzdalifah, how should they stay prepared for Fajr?
optionsEn: Locate the nearest restroom block upon arriving in Muzdalifah, carry a small personal water bottle for Wudu if queues are busy, or perform Tayammum only if genuinely unable to access water before sunrise
explanationEn: Carrying a bottle of clean water for Wudu in Muzdalifah saves waiting in long dawn bathroom queues right before Fajr.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ NOT light fires or turn Muzdalifah's night into a festival of speeches and entertainment?
optionsEn: Because after a spiritually exhausting day at Arafah, silent rest prepares the body and mind for the five intense obligations of Yawm al-Nahr
explanationEn: Islam honors both spiritual intensity and physical recovery; sleeping early at Muzdalifah reflects prophetic balance.

questionEn: What is the relationship between 'Al-Mash'ar al-Haram' in Qur'an 2:198 and the Haram boundaries of Makkah?
optionsEn: Al-Mash'ar al-Haram (Muzdalifah) lies INSIDE the sacred Haram sanctuary—giving it the name 'The Sacred Monument/Station'—unlike Arafah which lies just outside it
explanationEn: Entering Muzdalifah from Arafah means crossing back inside the Haram sanctuary boundaries of Makkah.

questionEn: Can a pilgrim bring extra food/water into Muzdalifah if they didn't pack enough from Arafah?
optionsEn: No, eating in Muzdalifah is prohibited
Yes, charitable stalls and water coolers operate throughout Muzdalifah, and pilgrims frequently share dates, bread, and water with neighbors
explanationEn: Generosity in sharing snacks and water on the cold/warm night of Muzdalifah strengthens brotherhood across nationalities.

questionEn: If a pilgrim is too sick to spend the night on the ground in Muzdalifah and is kept in a Mina/Makkah hospital overnight on the 9th–10th, do they owe a Dam?
optionsEn: Many scholars (including Ibn Taymiyyah and Hanbalis/Shafi'is for genuine incapacity or emergency hospital care) waive the Dam when staying is genuinely impossible due to hospitalization or medical rescue, though some schools require Dam
explanationEn: Just as the Prophet ﷺ excused shepherds and water-bearers from Mina Mabit, scholars apply mercy ('La yukallifullahu nafsan illa wus'aha') when hospitalization makes Mabit impossible.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say when someone reached him at Fajr in Muzdalifah asking if their Hajj counted after having arrived at Arafah late in the night?
optionsEn: 'Whoever joins this prayer of ours (Fajr at Muzdalifah) and stayed with us until we depart—having stood at Arafah before that by day or night—has completed his Hajj and fulfilled his rite!'
explanationEn: This magnificent Hadith of Urwah ibn Mudarris (RA) defines the exact outer limits of catching Arafah and Muzdalifah in time.

questionEn: When the Prophet ﷺ left Muzdalifah before sunrise on the 10th, what pace did he maintain until reaching Wadi Muhassir?
optionsEn: A calm, dignified pace (Al-Sakinah), only hastening briefly across Wadi Muhassir
A reckless sprint knocking people over
explanationEn: Calmness everywhere except a brief brisk crossing through Wadi Muhassir reflects deliberate prophetic poise.

questionEn: Why is it unwise to leave all personal valuables scattered loosely while sleeping outdoors in Muzdalifah?
optionsEn: Because pilgrims must throw away money
Because thousands walk past in the dark; keeping passport/cash/phone inside a zipped waist pouch or under your pillow keeps them safe without distraction
explanationEn: Tie your camel and trust Allah: securing essentials close to your body prevents frantic lost-item searches at Fajr.

questionEn: Does a pilgrim who stayed in Muzdalifah past midnight as an excused elderly person STILL have to make up a dawn standing at Al-Mash'ar al-Haram?
optionsEn: Yes, they must return before noon
No—they pray Fajr calmly once dawn breaks in Mina (or en route) and proceed with Rami without returning to Muzdalifah
explanationEn: The permission to leave after midnight naturally means they will be in Mina by Fajr time; no return or penalty is required.

questionEn: What is the rule regarding praying Sunnah prayers at Fajr in Muzdalifah?
optionsEn: Sunnah of Fajr is forbidden there
Pray the 2 regular Sunnah rakaat of Fajr quietly before the 2 Fard rakaat of Fajr, just as the Prophet ﷺ never omitted Sunnah of Fajr even on journeys
explanationEn: Aisha (RA) reported the Prophet ﷺ was never more diligent about any voluntary prayer than the two light rakaat before Fajr.

questionEn: If a pilgrim is driving or riding the Mashaaer Metro from Arafah to Muzdalifah after sunset, how should they handle the train's rapid transit?
optionsEn: Wait to exit at Muzdalifah station, find an open spot inside Muzdalifah's signs, pray Maghrib & Isha combined, and stay until after Fajr (or post-midnight if excused)
Stay on the train straight back to Mina without stepping into Muzdalifah
Pray Maghrib inside Arafah station first
explanationEn: Al-Mashaaer Metro stations drop pilgrims directly inside Muzdalifah's marked zones so they fulfill the Mabit comfortably.

questionEn: In Muzdalifah, if two pilgrims disagree whether dawn (Fajr) has actually entered yet because city floodlights brighten the sky, what should they do?
optionsEn: Pray two hours before Fajr time
Follow the verified Makkah Fajr prayer timetable and Masjid al-Mash'ar al-Haram's Adhan rather than guessing under stadium floodlights
explanationEn: Bright valley floodlights hide the faint natural dawn horizon; trusted Makkah astronomical schedules and mosque Adhans prevent praying Fajr prematurely.

questionEn: What special mercy did the Prophet ﷺ seek for his Ummah in Muzdalifah after having already asked for them at Arafah, according to Sahih narrations?
optionsEn: In the Hadith of Abbas ibn Mirdas (RA), the Prophet ﷺ prayed for forgiveness of his Ummah's wrongs—and at Muzdalifah Allah granted forgiveness even for injustices/wrongs among servants when Allah reconciles them!
explanationEn: In the famous narration of Abbas ibn Mirdas (RA) in Sunan Ibn Majah 3013, Allah answered the Prophet's ﷺ persistent pleading at Muzdalifah with vast mercy and reconciliation.

questionEn: Does a pilgrim remove their Ihram garments at Muzdalifah on the morning of the 10th before walking to Mina?
optionsEn: No! Ihram remains active all through Muzdalifah and the morning walk until completing stoning Jamrat al-Aqabah and shaving/trimming hair (Tahallul al-Awwal) in Mina on the 10th
explanationEn: Exiting Ihram prematurely before Rami/Halq on the 10th violates Ihram rules; patience until Mina on Eid morning keeps everything intact.

questionEn: When picking pebbles in Muzdalifah, how many pebbles should a pilgrim pick if they want all pebbles for ALL four days (10th, 11th, 12th, 13th) plus a few backups?
optionsEn: Around 70 pebbles plus ~5–10 extra backups (since 7 + 21 + 21 + 21 = 70), or 49 plus backups if planning Nafar Awwal on the 12th
explanationEn: Carrying a few extra spare pebbles avoids panic if one slips through your fingers in a crowd.

questionEn: If a pilgrim picked up 70 pebbles in Muzdalifah and left on the 12th (Nafar Awwal) using only 49, what should they do with the leftover 21 pebbles?
optionsEn: Throw them all at the Kaaba
Simply leave them cleanly on the ground anywhere outside walkways or dispose of them respectfully; they carry no sacred power of their own
explanationEn: Unused pebbles are ordinary natural stones; returning them cleanly to the earth harms nobody.

questionEn: Why does the Prophet ﷺ pray Fajr early at Muzdalifah and then wait until bright daylight (before sunrise) before walking to Mina?
optionsEn: To give time for deep, unhurried dua at Al-Mash'ar al-Haram AND allow clear visibility along the mountain valley path before sunrise
explanationEn: Praying at first light maximizes the quiet golden window for standing in supplication before setting out in good daylight.

questionEn: Can a pilgrim perform Tawaf al-Ifadah in Makkah during the night of Muzdalifah (after midnight) BEFORE going to Mina on the 10th?
optionsEn: No, Tawaf al-Ifadah is invalid until the 13th

Jurists (Shafi'i, Hanbali) permit performing Tawaf al-Ifadah after midnight on the night of Eid (10th) once Wuquf at Arafah is completed, especially for excused/weak pilgrims—though the Sunnah order is Rami → Hady → Halq → Tawaf al-Ifadah after sunrise
explanationEn: While following the Prophet's ﷺ sequence after dawn is clearly best, Shafi'is and Hanbalis permit Tawaf al-Ifadah after midnight of the 10th when travel/crowd needs press.

questionEn: When walking from Muzdalifah to Mina on the morning of the 10th, which side of the road should pilgrims avoid blocking?
optionsEn: Emergency vehicle lanes and bus corridors, sticking strictly to designated pedestrian avenues and shaded tunnels
explanationEn: Keeping ambulance and bus lanes unobstructed protects injured pilgrims and maintains orderly flow.

questionEn: If a pilgrim is in a wheelchair in Muzdalifah, how do they perform the standing dua at Al-Mash'ar al-Haram?
optionsEn: They must stand on one foot
Simply turn their wheelchair toward the Qiblah right where they are in Muzdalifah, raise their hands, and supplicate until just before sunrise
They must go back to Arafah
explanationEn: Standing physically on two feet is never required for those disabled; facing Qiblah seated fulfills the sunnah completely.

questionEn: What is the ruling on a pilgrim picking pebbles with their shoes on vs barefoot in Muzdalifah?
optionsEn: Wear shoes/sandals normally and pick clean pebbles easily by hand—no special footwear rule applies
Only pick with the left foot
explanationEn: Using open sandals protects feet from sharp stones or glass while gathering pebbles cleanly.

questionEn: In Muzdalifah, if a pilgrim feels too cold in their two thin white Ihram sheets, what is the Sunnah-compliant way to stay warm?
optionsEn: Put on a warm winter jacket and trousers
Wrap a thick blanket or shawl around shoulders and torso while sleeping/resting (leaving the head uncovered for men, and not wearing sleeves/tailored pants)
explanationEn: A warm blanket or sleeping bag kept below the neck keeps male pilgrims warm in cooler desert nights without violating the ban on tailored garments.

questionEn: Which verse in Surah Al-Baqarah specifically commands pilgrims to remember Allah at Al-Mash'ar al-Haram after departing Arafah?
explanationEn: Qur'an 2:198 explicitly pairs departing Arafah with remembering Allah at Al-Mash'ar al-Haram.

questionEn: What did Ibn Abbas (RA) narrate about the time he was sent ahead from Muzdalifah during the Farewell Pilgrimage?
optionsEn: He left at Dhuhr of the 9th

He left during the late night with the weak members of the Prophet's ﷺ household, and the Prophet ﷺ instructed them: 'Do not stone the Jamrah until the sun rises' (while Asma's narration shows leaving after moonset and stoning around pre-dawn/dawn was also practiced)
He stayed in Arafah for 3 days
explanationEn: Reconciling Ibn Abbas (RA) and Asma (RA), scholars explain the Sunnah preference is waiting for sunrise if safe, while leaving/stoning earlier around pre-dawn when crowding threatens weak pilgrims is permitted.

questionEn: When pilgrims move from Muzdalifah into Mina on the 10th morning, which Jamarat pillar do they encounter FIRST if coming from Muzdalifah?
optionsEn: Jamrat al-Aqabah is nearest to Muzdalifah
All three are in a triangle

Jamrat al-Sughra is nearest to Muzdalifah, then Al-Wusta, and Jamrat al-Aqabah is farthest west (nearest to Makkah)—so on the 10th they pass Sughra and Wusta WITHOUT throwing at them and go straight to Aqabah!
Only one pillar exists on the 10th
explanationEn: Because pilgrims walk west from Muzdalifah toward Makkah, they pass Al-Sughra and Al-Wusta first without stoning them on the 10th, heading directly to Jamrat al-Aqabah at the Makkah end of Mina.

questionEn: How does a pilgrim who is walking on the Jamarat multi-level pedestrian bridge on the 10th recognize Jamrat al-Aqabah?
optionsEn: It is the very first pillar entering from Muzdalifah
It is clearly labeled in Arabic/English/other languages ('Al-Jamrah Al-Kubra / Al-Aqabah') and is the third/final basin on the Makkah side (when arriving from Muzdalifah)
explanationEn: Large overhead electronic signs clearly identify Sughra (Small), Wusta (Middle), and Kubra/Aqabah (Big) on every bridge level.

questionEn: If a pilgrim is in Muzdalifah and hears the news of Eid al-Adha dawning across the Muslim world, how should they greet companions?
optionsEn: With joyful 'Taqabbalallahu minna wa minkum' / Eid Mubarak, gratitude to Allah, and renewed focus on the rites of Yawm al-Nahr
explanationEn: The 10th of Dhul-Hijjah is the greatest day in the sight of Allah (Sunan Abi Dawud 1765)—combining the joy of Eid with the pinnacle deeds of Hajj.

questionEn: According to Abdullah ibn Qurt (RA), what did the Prophet ﷺ say is the greatest day in the sight of Allah?
optionsEn: Yawm al-Nahr (the Day of Sacrifice, 10th Dhul-Hijjah), followed by Yawm al-Qarr (11th Dhul-Hijjah, when pilgrims settle in Mina)
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ declared: 'The greatest of days with Allah is the Day of Sacrifice (Yawm al-Nahr), then the Day of Settling (Yawm al-Qarr, 11th).'

questionEn: Why is the 11th of Dhul-Hijjah called 'Yawm al-Qarr' in Sunan Abi Dawud 1765?
optionsEn: Because after the exhausting travel between Arafah, Muzdalifah, and Tawaf al-Ifadah on the 10th, pilgrims finally settle down (yaqirruna) peacefully in their Mina tents on the 11th
explanationEn: Qarr comes from qarar (settling/resting): having accomplished the hardest stations, pilgrims dwell calmly in Mina remembering Allah.

questionEn: What spiritual lesson does moving from Arafah (daytime plea for forgiveness) to Muzdalifah (quiet night surrender) teach the believer?
optionsEn: That after pouring out one's heart in earnest dua, true faith rests securely in Allah's promise and wakes ready to act in obedience
explanationEn: Arafah represents ardent supplication; Muzdalifah represents tranquil trust (tawakkul); Yawm al-Nahr represents energetic action.

questionEn: If a pilgrim is elderly and takes the Mashaaer Metro straight from Muzdalifah to Mina Station 3 (near the Jamarat), is using the train instead of walking through Wadi Muhassir valid?
optionsEn: Completely valid and wise—taking modern transit preserves strength safely for stoning and Tawaf al-Ifadah
Invalid—walking barefoot through Muhassir is mandatory
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ himself rode Al-Qaswa' along the route; riding the elevated Mashaaer Metro is completely permissible.

questionEn: Before falling asleep in Muzdalifah, what short evening Sunnah remembrances can a weary pilgrim recite on their mat?
optionsEn: Ayat al-Kursi, the last two verses of Surah Al-Baqarah, the Three Quls (Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq, Al-Nas), and Tasbih Fatimah (33 Subhanallah, 33 Alhamdulillah, 34 Allahu Akbar)
explanationEn: Simple bedtime Prophetic adhkar guard the pilgrim through the night and turn even tired sleep into worship.

questionEn: If a pilgrim arrives at Muzdalifah and sees there is no space right beside Masjid al-Mash'ar al-Haram, may they camp near the eastern or northern edge of Muzdalifah?
optionsEn: No, only within 10 meters of the mosque
Yes! Any square meter inside Muzdalifah's marked valley boundaries (excluding Wadi Muhassir) fulfills Mabit equally
explanationEn: The Prophet's ﷺ assurance—'All of Jam' (Muzdalifah) is a place of standing'—makes every safe space within Muzdalifah's perimeter equally valid.

questionEn: What is the rule if a pilgrim is still in Muzdalifah AFTER sunrise on the 10th due to a missed bus or waking late?
optionsEn: They must go back to Arafah
No penalty—they immediately head toward Mina calmly to perform Jamrat al-Aqabah, whose stoning window lasts all day on the 10th
explanationEn: Departing Muzdalifah before sunrise is a Sunnah; leaving slightly after sunrise due to delay or sleeping incurs zero Dam.

questionEn: As pilgrims emerge from Muzdalifah onto the morning of the 10th of Dhul-Hijjah, what four great deeds await them on Yawm al-Nahr?
optionsEn: Stoning Jamrat al-Aqabah, offering Hady sacrifice, shaving/trimming hair (Halq/Taqsir), and performing Tawaf al-Ifadah (with Sa'i if due)
Fasting, sleeping, shopping, and traveling home
Standing at Arafah, combining Maghrib, visiting Taif, and Qasr
explanationEn: These four harmonious acts transform the pilgrim from Ihram back into ordinary life purified like a newborn.

questionEn: What is the exact Prophetic sequence of the four primary rituals performed on Yawm al-Nahr (10th Dhul-Hijjah)?
optionsEn: Rami of Jamrat al-Aqabah → Hady sacrifice → Halq/Taqsir (shaving/trimming hair) → Tawaf al-Ifadah (and Sa'i if due)
explanationEn: Jabir (RA) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ first stoned Jamrat al-Aqabah at forenoon, went to the slaughter area to offer his Hady, had his head shaved, and then rode to Makkah for Tawaf al-Ifadah.

questionEn: What merciful reply did the Prophet ﷺ give whenever pilgrims came on Yawm al-Nahr admitting they had shaved before sacrificing, or sacrificed before stoning, or performed Tawaf before stoning?
optionsEn: 'Your Hajj is ruined—repeat it next year'
'If'al wa la haraj' (Do it, there is no harm / no penalty)
explanationEn: Abdullah ibn 'Amr (RA) reported that the Prophet ﷺ was not asked about any of these acts done ahead or behind order on Yawm al-Nahr except that he replied: 'Do it, there is no harm!'

questionEn: Does doing the four rites of the 10th out of order (for instance, shaving after Rami when Hady is delayed via Adahi bank voucher, or doing Tawaf al-Ifadah before Hady) incur a Dam?
optionsEn: No penalty according to the Sunnah ('If'al wa la haraj'), as confirmed by Shafi'i, Hanbali, and many scholars—though Hanafis prefer respecting the sequence
explanationEn: Especially today when official Adahi slaughterhouses process sacrifices over hours, knowing that 'If'al wa la haraj' lifts guilt when shaving or doing Tawaf before confirmation arrives brings tremendous relief.

questionEn: On the 10th of Dhul-Hijjah, which Jamarat pillar is stoned, and how many pebbles are thrown at it?
optionsEn: Only Jamrat al-Aqabah (the Largest Pillar, nearest Makkah), with 7 pebbles thrown one by one
explanationEn: On Eid day, only Jamrat al-Aqabah is pelted with 7 single pebbles; pelting all three begins on the 11th of Dhul-Hijjah.

questionEn: What words did the Prophet ﷺ pronounce each time he threw one of the seven pebbles at the Jamrah?
explanationEn: Ibn Mas'ud and Jabir (RA) reported the Prophet ﷺ stood and threw each pebble individually, saying 'Allahu Akbar' upon each throw.

questionEn: How should a pilgrim position themselves relative to the Kaaba and Mina when stoning Jamrat al-Aqabah according to the classic narration of Ibn Mas'ud (RA)?
optionsEn: Facing east with Makkah behind them

With the Kaaba to their left and Mina to their right (when standing at ground level), facing the basin—while on today's circular bridge any direction throwing cleanly into the basin is completely valid
explanationEn: Ibn Mas'ud (RA) stood in the hollow with the House on his left and Mina on his right; today's oval walls let thousands approach calmly from all angles and land pebbles inside the basin.

questionEn: Should a pilgrim stop beside Jamrat al-Aqabah on the 10th to raise their hands and make a long dua after throwing the 7th pebble?
optionsEn: Yes, face the Kaaba right beside Aqabah and pray loudly
No! Unlike Jamrat al-Sughra and Jamrat al-Wusta (on 11th–13th), the Prophet ﷺ did NOT stop to make dua after stoning Jamrat al-Aqabah—he immediately turned and departed
explanationEn: Leaving immediately after stoning Jamrat al-Aqabah keeps pedestrian flow moving safely and strictly matches the Sunnah.

questionEn: What is required for a throw at the Jamrah to be legally valid?
optionsEn: Each of the 7 pebbles must be thrown individually and land inside the circular basin (hawd)—whether or not it hits the central wall/column directly
Each pebble must smash the stone pillar violently
All 7 pebbles must be thrown together in one fistful
explanationEn: Many pilgrims mistakenly think they must hit the central concrete wall with force; jurists clarify the target is the circular basin (hawd) around the pillar, and all 7 throws must be separate—throwing 7 at once counts as only 1!

questionEn: If a pilgrim throws a pebble at Jamrat al-Aqabah and it bounces off someone's shoulder and lands OUTSIDE the basin, does that throw count?
optionsEn: No, it does not count—so carrying a few spare pebbles lets you immediately throw another single pebble cleanly into the basin
explanationEn: Watching each pebble drop cleanly into the wide elliptical basin ensures all 7 throws are valid.

questionEn: Why do scholars firmly warn pilgrims NOT to call the Jamarat pillars 'the big devil' or shout curses and throw shoes at them?
optionsEn: Because Shaytan lives inside the Kaaba
Because Rami is an act of pure remembrance of Allah ('Iqamat dhikrillah') and dignified obedience, not venting rage or cursing—plus throwing shoes harms fellow believers
Because only stones from Madinah work
explanationEn: Aisha (RA) narrated the Prophet ﷺ said Tawaf, Sa'i, and stoning the Jamarat were ordained solely to establish the remembrance of Allah ('li-iqamati dhikriLlah').

questionEn: Until when does the valid time for stoning Jamrat al-Aqabah on Yawm al-Nahr extend if crowds are too dense in the morning?
optionsEn: The Sunnah preferred time is after sunrise (Duha) on the 10th, yet it remains valid through the afternoon, sunset, and all night until Fajr of the 11th without penalty
explanationEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari 1723, a man asked the Prophet ﷺ 'I stoned after evening fell' and he replied 'No harm!'—showing afternoon/evening stoning on the 10th avoids dangerous morning bottlenecks.

questionEn: When may someone appoint a proxy (Wakil) to stone the Jamarat on their behalf?
optionsEn: Only when genuinely unable due to severe illness, advanced frailty, pregnancy-related danger, or disability—not out of laziness or wanting to shop
Whenever one prefers sleeping in a hotel
Healthy men may always hire proxies
explanationEn: Jabir (RA) narrated: 'We performed Hajj with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and there were women and children with us, so we stoned on behalf of the children.' Likewise, disabled/frail pilgrims appoint a trustworthy pilgrim who stones for himself first and then for them.
reference: Sunan Ibn Majah 3038; Fatawa Ibn Baz

questionEn: How does a proxy (Wakil) stone a Jamrah for both himself and an incapacitated pilgrim?
optionsEn: Throw 7 pebbles individually for himself FIRST, and then (at the same pillar before moving on) throw 7 pebbles individually on behalf of the excused person
Throw for the other person first and skip himself
explanationEn: Finishing one's own 7 throws at a pillar before throwing the 7 proxy throws at that same pillar saves walking back through massive crowds.

questionEn: What does 'Hady' refer to on the 10th of Dhul-Hijjah, and who MUST offer it?
optionsEn: A gift of dates for Makkah police
The sacrificial animal offered in Makkah/Haram by Tamattu' and Qiran pilgrims (and optionally by Mufrids as gratitude)
explanationEn: Hady is the sacrificial livestock (sheep, goat, or 1/7th share of a camel/cow) slaughtered within the Haram boundaries; Tamattu' and Qiran pilgrims owe it per Qur'an 2:196.

questionEn: Which livestock animals are valid for Hady sacrifice during Hajj?
optionsEn: Camels, cattle (cows/buffalo), and sheep or goats (Al-An'am)
explanationEn: Sacrificial animals in Islam are restricted to domestic Bahimat al-An'am (camels, cattle, sheep, goats) meeting minimum age and health criteria.

questionEn: How many pilgrims may share in ONE camel (Badanah) or ONE cow (Baqarah) for their Hady sacrifice?
optionsEn: Up to 7 pilgrims sharing one-seventh each (whereas a sheep/goat suffices for only 1 pilgrim)
explanationEn: Jabir (RA) narrated: 'The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us to share seven persons in one camel and seven in one cow.'

questionEn: What are the minimum ages required for Hady animals according to the Prophet's ﷺ Hadith?
optionsEn: A sheep (Jadha'ah) at least 6 months old, a goat (Thaniyy) at least 1 full year, cattle at least 2 years, and a camel at least 5 years
All animals must be 10 years old
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ instructed: 'Do not slaughter except a mature animal (musinnah), unless it is difficult for you, in which case slaughter a jadha'ah (six-month-old) of sheep.'

questionEn: Which four physical defects render an animal UNFIT for Hady sacrifice according to Al-Bara' ibn 'Azib (RA)?
optionsEn: Having black wool, long ears, short tail, or missing a horn tip
Clearly one-eyed/blind, visibly sick, unmistakably lame, or extremely emaciated with no marrow
explanationEn: Al-Bara' (RA) narrated the Prophet ﷺ pointed with four fingers naming those exact four disqualifying defects, teaching believers to offer Allah healthy, wholesome animals.

questionEn: During which days is slaughtering Hady (and Udhiyah) valid?
optionsEn: On Yawm al-Nahr (10th) and the Days of Tashreeq (11th, 12th, and until sunset of the 13th of Dhul-Hijjah—4 days total, though Hanafis/Malikis limit Udhiyah/Hady to 10th–12th)
explanationEn: Jubayr ibn Mut'im (RA) narrated the Prophet ﷺ said: 'All the Days of Tashreeq are days of slaughter'—giving slaughterhouses ample safe time across 10th–13th.

questionEn: How many camels did the Prophet ﷺ bring and offer as Hady during the Farewell Pilgrimage, and who slaughtered the remaining ones?
optionsEn: 100 camels total: the Prophet ﷺ personally slaughtered 63 with his own hand (matching his age) and entrusted Ali (RA) to slaughter the remaining 37
explanationEn: Jabir (RA) recorded this astonishing generosity: the Prophet ﷺ even had a piece from every camel cooked into broth so he and Ali ate of it and distributed all meat and hides to the poor.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ forbid Ali (RA) from giving the butcher as wages out of the Hady sacrificial animals?
optionsEn: Giving any portion of the sacrificial meat, hide, or saddle-cloth as payment to the butcher—instead paying the butcher's fee separately so the entire animal goes to worship and charity
Paying the butcher in silver coins
explanationEn: Ali (RA) reported: 'The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered me to supervise his sacrificial camels, distribute their meat, hides, and coverings, and not give the butcher anything from them [as wages]; we pay him from our own money.'

questionEn: If a pilgrim is performing Hajj al-Tamattu' or Qiran and ALREADY offers a Hady in Makkah, must they ALSO offer a separate Udhiyah (Eid Qurbani) back home?
optionsEn: Yes, two separate sacrifices are mandatory on every pilgrim
No! A pilgrim in Hajj offers Hady rather than Udhiyah (unless they optionally choose to appoint family back home to sacrifice for household Sunnah—and the Prophet ﷺ offered Hady in Hajj)
explanationEn: Scholars clarify that the pilgrim's rite is Hady (not Udhiyah), while non-pilgrim households back home offer Udhiyah.

questionEn: After stoning Jamrat al-Aqabah and arranging Hady on the 10th, why did the Prophet ﷺ pray three times for 'Al-Muhalliqin' (those who shave their heads) and only once for 'Al-Muqassirin' (those who trim)?
optionsEn: Because barbers charged less for shaving
To show that completely shaving the head (Halq) for men carries much greater reward and humility than merely trimming (Taqsir), though both are valid
explanationEn: Ibn Umar (RA) narrated: 'O Allah, have mercy on those who shave!' Repeated thrice before finally adding 'And those who trim'—showing full surrender via Halq is superior for men.

questionEn: What is the exact ruling on hair removal for WOMEN after stoning Jamrat al-Aqabah on the 10th (or after Umrah)?
optionsEn: Women must shave their heads bald
Women cut half their hair off
Women do nothing to their hair
Women are strictly forbidden from shaving their heads; instead they gather their hair and trim ONLY the length of a fingertip (unmulah, ~1–2 cm) evenly from the ends
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) narrated the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Shaving is not required of women; rather, shortening (taqsir) is upon women'—trimming about a fingertip's length evenly.

questionEn: If a male pilgrim chooses Taqsir (trimming) rather than Halq (shaving) on the 10th, is cutting only 3 tiny hairs from one side sufficient?
optionsEn: No! Cutting a tiny snip from one spot is a common mistake; jurists emphasize trimming noticeably from ALL over the head (covering the entire scalp evenly)
explanationEn: The Qur'an says 'muhalliqina ru'usakum wa muqassirin' (shaving your HEADS and shortening [them])—applying to the whole head, not two stray strands!

questionEn: Which side of the head did the Prophet ﷺ offer to the barber (Ma'mar ibn Abdullah RA) first when shaving his head at Mina on Yawm al-Nahr?
optionsEn: The right side first (then the left side), distributing his blessed hair among his Companions like Khalid ibn al-Walid and Abu Talhah (RA)
explanationEn: Anas (RA) witnessed the barber shave the right side of the Prophet's ﷺ head first and then the left, blessing the Companions with tokens of his hair.

questionEn: What does 'Al-Tahallul al-Awwal' (or al-Asghar — First/Partial Release from Ihram) allow on the 10th of Dhul-Hijjah?
optionsEn: Once a pilgrim completes two of the three Mina/Makkah release acts (specifically Rami + Halq/Taqsir, or Rami + Tawaf al-Ifadah), ALL Ihram restrictions lift—wearing normal stitched clothes, perfume, nail clipping—EXCEPT marital intimacy
explanationEn: Aisha (RA) narrated: 'I used to perfume the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for his Ihram before he entered it, and for his exit from Ihram before he performed Tawaf around the House.'

questionEn: What completes 'Al-Tahallul al-Akbar' (Full Release from Ihram), making even marital relations between spouses lawful again?
optionsEn: Completing ALL three major release acts: (1) Rami of Jamrat al-Aqabah, (2) Halq or Taqsir, and (3) Tawaf al-Ifadah (along with Hajj Sa'i if not yet done)
explanationEn: Once Rami, Halq/Taqsir, and Tawaf al-Ifadah (+ Sa'i) are all complete, full Tahallul is achieved.

questionEn: When a male pilgrim takes off his Ihram sheets, showers, wears clean regular clothes, and puts on perfume BEFORE going to Makkah for Tawaf al-Ifadah (after Rami and Halq), should he perform Raml or Idtiba during Tawaf al-Ifadah?
optionsEn: No! Both Idtiba and Raml belong ONLY to the arrival Tawaf (Tawaf al-Qudum / Umrah Tawaf)—NOT to Tawaf al-Ifadah or Tawaf al-Wada'
Yes, mandatory Raml in all 7 circuits
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) and jurists agree there is no Idtiba and no Raml in Tawaf al-Ifadah because the pilgrim is already dressed in normal clothes after Tahallul al-Awwal.

questionEn: Why is 'Tawaf al-Ifadah' also called 'Tawaf al-Ziyarah' or 'Tawaf al-Fard'?
optionsEn: Because pilgrims 'pour forth' (yufiduna) from Mina back to visit the Kaaba, and it is an indispensable Rukn (pillar) without which Hajj cannot be completed
Because it is done in Madinah
Because it is done on the 7th
explanationEn: Unlike Tawaf al-Qudum (Sunnah) and Tawaf al-Wada' (Wajib), Tawaf al-Ifadah is a Rukn of Hajj (Qur'an 22:29) that cannot be compensated with any Dam.

questionEn: If a pilgrim is exhausted on the 10th of Dhul-Hijjah, may they delay Tawaf al-Ifadah until the 11th, 12th, or even after leaving Mina on the 13th?
optionsEn: No, it becomes invalid after Maghrib of the 10th
Yes, but they owe three camels
Yes! Performing Tawaf al-Ifadah on the 10th is best (Sunnah), yet delaying it to the Days of Tashreeq or before leaving Makkah is completely valid with zero penalty
They must wait until next year
explanationEn: Delaying Tawaf al-Ifadah until the 11th, 12th, or 13th relieves dangerous 10th-day congestion in Masjid al-Haram and avoids violating any pillar.

questionEn: What happens if a Tamattu' pilgrim finishes Tawaf al-Ifadah on the 10th or 11th—what must immediately follow it?
optionsEn: Nothing, Tamattu' has no second Sa'i
Performing Hajj's second Sa'i (7 laps between Safa and Marwah), since their earlier Sa'i was for Umrah only
explanationEn: Remember: Tamattu' has TWO Sa'is (one for Umrah, one for Hajj), whereas Ifrad/Qiran need only ONE Sa'i if already performed after Tawaf al-Qudum.

questionEn: What should a woman do if her menstrual period begins AFTER Arafah on the 10th BEFORE she has performed Tawaf al-Ifadah?
optionsEn: She completes Rami, trimming her fingertip-length hair, and Mina stays normally; she simply delays Tawaf al-Ifadah until she finishes menstruating and takes Ghusl (never entering Tawaf while menstruating)
She performs Tawaf al-Ifadah while menstruating
explanationEn: When Safiyyah bint Huyayy (RA) menstruated during Hajj, the Prophet ﷺ asked anxiously: 'Is she going to delay us?'—and rejoiced when told she had ALREADY performed Tawaf al-Ifadah beforehand! Otherwise, a pilgrim waits until pure to complete this Rukn.

questionEn: Which Mother of the Believers had already completed Tawaf al-Ifadah right before menstruating, sparing the Prophet's ﷺ caravan from waiting in Makkah—and leading to the dispensation exempting menstruating women from Tawaf al-Wada'?
explanationEn: Because Safiyyah (RA) had already completed Tawaf al-Ifadah (the Rukn), the Prophet ﷺ said 'Then let her depart!'—establishing that menstruating women are excused from the Farewell Tawaf (Wada').

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ deliver to the people in Mina on Yawm al-Nahr (10th Dhul-Hijjah), right in the middle of the Tashreeq rites?
optionsEn: A powerful sermon reiterating the sanctity of life, wealth, and honor, reminding them to convey his message ('Let the witness inform the absent'), and asking 'Have I conveyed?'
An order to tear down tents
explanationEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari 1741, Abu Bakrah (RA) narrated the Prophet's ﷺ moving Yawm al-Nahr sermon in Mina reiterating human sanctity and asking Allah to bear witness.

questionEn: After performing Tawaf al-Ifadah in Makkah on the 10th, where MUST the pilgrim return to spend the night of the 10th–11th?
optionsEn: Back to Mina! The Prophet ﷺ returned to Mina right after Tawaf al-Ifadah to spend the nights of Tashreeq there
explanationEn: Even if one stays briefly in a Makkah hotel to shower and change after Rami/Halq, pilgrims return to Mina for the nights of 11th and 12th.

questionEn: If a pilgrim is naturally bald (has zero hair on his head), how does he fulfill Halq/Taqsir on the 10th of Dhul-Hijjah?
optionsEn: By passing a razor blade gently over his bare scalp (imrar al-musa) symbolically without cutting skin—this fulfills the rite cleanly
By shaving his entire beard off
explanationEn: Jurists agree passing the razor lightly over a completely bald head fulfills Halq (and certainly one should NEVER shave off the beard, which is forbidden to shave!).

questionEn: May a pilgrim shave or trim their own hair (or have a friend/fellow pilgrim in Ihram trim it) BEFORE that friend has exited Ihram?
optionsEn: No, a Muhrim cutting another Muhrim's hair is strictly void
Yes! Once the time for Halq/Taqsir arrives (after Rami on the 10th), one pilgrim may lawfully shave/trim another pilgrim's hair or his own hair with zero penalty
explanationEn: Since trimming hair on the 10th is the prescribed act of exiting Ihram (not a forbidden violation), helping a companion cut their hair is fully permitted.

questionEn: What happens if a pilgrim buys a cheap razor or uses an unhygienic shared blade from a street barber at Mina?
optionsEn: It risks blood-borne diseases like Hepatitis B/C or HIV; pilgrims MUST insist on a brand-new sealed disposable blade or bring their own personal electric clipper/razor
Electric clippers are invalid for Halq
explanationEn: Public health agencies and scholars stress bringing your own sterilized razor/clipper or verifying a fresh sealed blade opened in front of you.
reference: Saudi Ministry of Health Hajj Guidelines

questionEn: Are electric hair clippers set to zero (close buzz/shave) valid for Halq or Taqsir?
optionsEn: No, only straight razors from Damascus count
Yes! Using clean electric clippers to buzz the whole head short counts as thorough Taqsir (or close shave if blade-level), while a razor blade gives full Halq
explanationEn: Whether using scissors or electric clippers evenly across the whole head, hair shortening is completely valid—and using a clean razor earns the supreme Halq reward.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ do with the Zamzam water right after completing Tawaf al-Ifadah on Yawm al-Nahr according to Ibn Abbas (RA)?
optionsEn: He came to Banu Abd al-Muttalib who were drawing Zamzam water, asked for a bucket from which people were drinking, and drank standing up while praising their noble service ('Were it not that people would overwhelm you, I would draw water with you!')
He bathed his camel in it
explanationEn: This touching scene shows the Prophet's ﷺ humility toward the humble water-servers of Zamzam and his encouragement of Siqayah service.

questionEn: What is the ruling on performing Tawaf al-Ifadah WITHOUT doing Rami al-Aqabah or Halq first, if someone arrives at Masjid al-Haram directly from Muzdalifah?
optionsEn: According to the Prophet's ﷺ 'Do it, no harm' ruling, Tawaf al-Ifadah is valid, though the pilgrim stays in partial/full Ihram until completing Rami and Halq/Taqsir
explanationEn: Remember: full Tahallul requires all three (Rami, Halq/Taqsir, Tawaf al-Ifadah); doing Tawaf first is valid, yet stitched clothes/marital release still depend on Rami and Halq.

questionEn: When a pilgrim achieves Tahallul al-Awwal (Rami + Halq/Taqsir), which ONE restriction remains prohibited until Tawaf al-Ifadah (+ due Sa'i) is completed?
optionsEn: Marital intimacy (intercourse and sexual foreplay between spouses)
explanationEn: Aisha (RA) confirmed she applied perfume to the Prophet ﷺ after Rami/Halq before he went down for Tawaf al-Ifadah; only marital relations await full Tahallul.

questionEn: What if a pilgrim offers their Tamattu' Hady through an agency, and the agency later informs them slaughter occurred on the 11th instead of the 10th—is that valid?
optionsEn: Invalid—must be before 10:00 AM on the 10th
Only sheep from Yemen are valid on the 11th
Completely valid! All Days of Tashreeq (10th, 11th, 12th, and 13th) are valid days for slaughtering Hady
explanationEn: Because slaughterhouses process hundreds of thousands of sacrifices safely under veterinary supervision across 10th–13th, Hady slaughtered on the 11th or 12th is completely sound.

questionEn: What does Surah Al-Hajj 22:28 instruct pilgrims to do with the meat of their Hady sacrificial animals?
optionsEn: 'Then eat from them and feed the miserable and poor (al-ba'isa al-faqir)'
explanationEn: Qur'an 22:28 balances gratitude (eating a portion joyfully as Allah's guests) with social compassion (feeding the impoverished worldwide).

questionEn: How does the modern Saudi Adahi / Islamic Development Bank sacrificial system distribute Hady meat from Mina?
optionsEn: Chills, packages, and distributes millions of portions to Makkah's needy and ships frozen meat to impoverished Muslim communities across dozens of countries
explanationEn: This global cold-chain charity fulfills Qur'an 22:28 on an unprecedented scale while keeping Mina hygienic.
reference: Saudi Project for Utilization of Hajj Meat (Adahi)

questionEn: If a pilgrim is unable to afford a Hady animal for Tamattu' or Qiran, what must they do instead according to Qur'an 2:196?
optionsEn: Fast 3 days during Hajj (even on 11th–13th Tashreeq if not done before Arafah) and 7 days after returning home
explanationEn: Qur'an 2:196 provides this clear financial mercy so no humble believer is burdened beyond their wallet.

questionEn: When a pilgrim fasts the 7 remaining days at home after returning from Hajj (for lacking Hady), must those 7 days be consecutive?
optionsEn: Yes, missing one day voids all 10
Preferable to fast consecutively, though scholars agree fasting them non-consecutively is also valid since Qur'an 2:196 does not stipulate consecutiveness
explanationEn: Keeping the obligation practical, Allah simply asked for 'seven when you have returned; those are ten complete.'

questionEn: Why does the Prophet ﷺ combine both Jamrat al-Aqabah stoning AND Hady sacrifice on the 10th of Dhul-Hijjah?
optionsEn: Both honor Prophet Ibrahim's (AS) total victory over Shaytan's temptations and readiness to offer his dearest possession for Allah's pleasure
explanationEn: On Yawm al-Nahr, outward action (pelting Shaytan's whispers + offering sacrifice + shedding old ego/hair) crowns the inward repentance of Arafah.

questionEn: If a pilgrim stones Jamrat al-Aqabah with ONLY 6 pebbles by miscounting, and realizes it before leaving Mina on the 10th, what should they do?
optionsEn: Simply throw 1 additional pebble into Jamrat al-Aqabah to complete the 7
explanationEn: Completing the missing pebble once noticed restores the exact count of 7 cleanly; carrying 2–3 spares in your pocket makes fixing a miscount instant.

questionEn: What is the ruling if a pilgrim throws pebbles using their LEFT hand instead of their RIGHT hand at the Jamarat?
optionsEn: The throw is valid (since the pebble entered the basin), though using the right hand is Sunnah unless injured
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ loved starting and performing honorable acts with his right hand; if someone's right arm is injured or bandaged, using the left hand is completely valid.

questionEn: How does the modern 5-level Jamarat Bridge complex prevent stampedes that used to occur decades ago?
optionsEn: By providing wide multi-story ramps, one-way pedestrian flow, misting fans, and large oval target basins capable of handling over 300,000 pilgrims per hour safely
explanationEn: All levels of the Jamarat bridge drop pebbles into the exact same vertical shaft/basin, so stoning on the 2nd, 3rd, or 4th level is 100% as valid as the ground level!
reference: Fatawa al-Lajnah al-Da'imah; Jamarat Engineering Guide

questionEn: Is stoning the Jamarat from the upper tiers (Level 2, 3, or 4) of the Jamarat Bridge just as valid as stoning on the ground floor?
optionsEn: Yes, 100% equally valid—every level opens directly onto the exact same target shaft/basin
No, upper levels count as zero
explanationEn: Choosing less crowded upper levels protects life and prevents crushing while fulfilling the exact rite.

questionEn: When a pilgrim completes Tawaf al-Ifadah on the 10th or 11th, where are the 2 rakaat after Tawaf prayed?
optionsEn: Behind Maqam Ibrahim (or anywhere inside Masjid al-Haram out of the Mataf walking path)
Skip the 2 rakaat for Tawaf al-Ifadah
explanationEn: Every 7-circuit Tawaf (Qudum, Umrah, Ifadah, Wada', or Nafl) is followed by praying 2 Sunnah rakaat inside Masjid al-Haram.

questionEn: What is the ruling if a pilgrim has ALREADY entered normal clothes after Rami + Halq, then performs Tawaf al-Ifadah, and realizes they forgot Wudu during Tawaf al-Ifadah?
optionsEn: Majority (Maliki, Shafi'i, Hanbali) require Wudu for Tawaf al-Ifadah's validity, so they renew Wudu and repeat Tawaf al-Ifadah cleanly (Hanafis treat Wudu in Tawaf as Wajib requiring Dam if omitted)
explanationEn: Double-checking Wudu before starting Tawaf al-Ifadah ensures this indispensable pillar of Hajj is accepted unanimously across all schools.

questionEn: If a pilgrim is in Makkah on the 10th for Tawaf al-Ifadah and it is crowded at ground level, what is the smart Sunnah-compliant option?
optionsEn: Shove women and elderly aside on the ground floor
Pay someone to do Tawaf al-Ifadah for them while healthy
Perform Tawaf al-Ifadah calmly on the upper floor or roof of Masjid al-Haram (or postpone it to the 11th/12th night when the Mataf is cooler and calmer)
explanationEn: Note: Unlike Rami for the disabled, no healthy or living able-bodied pilgrim can hire someone else to perform Tawaf al-Ifadah on their behalf; wheeling them or choosing quieter upper floors/nights keeps the pillar sound.

questionEn: Can a disabled pilgrim who cannot walk be pushed in a wheelchair or carried during Tawaf al-Ifadah and Sa'i?
optionsEn: Yes! Pushing/carrying a disabled pilgrim fulfills their Tawaf and Sa'i completely (just as Umm Salamah RA did Tawaf riding when ill, and the Prophet ﷺ rode his camel)
No, only walking on feet counts
explanationEn: Umm Salamah (RA) complained of illness to the Prophet ﷺ, and he told her: 'Perform Tawaf behind the people while riding' (Sahih al-Bukhari 1619).

questionEn: When a volunteer or relative pushes a disabled pilgrim in a wheelchair around the Kaaba for Tawaf al-Ifadah, does that single Tawaf count for BOTH of them if the pusher also intends their own Tawaf al-Ifadah?
optionsEn: Yes! According to scholarly consensus (Fatawa Ibn Baz / Ibn Uthaymeen), if the pusher also needs their own Tawaf al-Ifadah and forms intention for themselves while pushing, it counts for both—just like carrying a child!
explanationEn: Serving an elderly parent or disabled spouse while simultaneously performing one's own Tawaf and Sa'i brings double reward without doubling fatigue.
reference: Fatawa Ibn Baz; Fatawa Ibn Uthaymeen

questionEn: What is the ruling on performing 'Tawaf al-Ifadah' and 'Tawaf al-Wada'' together in ONE single Tawaf at the end of Hajj if a pilgrim delayed Tawaf al-Ifadah until right before departing Makkah?
optionsEn: Many scholars (including Hanbalis, Shafi'is, and Ibn Baz/Ibn Uthaymeen) rule that if Tawaf al-Ifadah (+ Sa'i) is performed as the very final act before leaving Makkah, it suffices for both Ifadah and Wada' (whereas if one stays longer in Makkah afterward, a separate Tawaf al-Wada' is due)
explanationEn: This especially helps menstruating women who wait until pure just before their flight: performing Tawaf al-Ifadah right before departure covers Wada' too without extra delay.

questionEn: What happens if a pilgrim performs Tawaf al-Ifadah BEFORE stoning Jamrat al-Aqabah on the 10th, and then returns to Mina to stone and shave—when do they exit Ihram?
optionsEn: First Tahallul only happens once TWO of the three acts (Rami, Halq, Tawaf) are done, and full Tahallul occurs once all three (+ Sa'i if due) are finished
explanationEn: Even when the sequence varies per 'If'al wa la haraj', the Ihram release stages still depend on completing the constituent rites.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Kawthar 108:2 ('Fa salli li-Rabbika wanhar'), what two acts of devotion are paired together on the Day of Eid al-Adha?
optionsEn: Prayer (Salah) and Sacrifice (Nahr)—done sincerely for Allah alone
explanationEn: Qur'an 108:2 crowns Yawm al-Nahr with exclusive worship: 'So pray to your Lord and sacrifice [to Him alone].'

questionEn: Why does the Prophet ﷺ forbid fasts on the 10th of Dhul-Hijjah (Eid al-Adha) for ALL Muslims—pilgrims and non-pilgrims alike?
optionsEn: Because Eid al-Adha and Eid al-Fitr are Allah's designated days of feasting, gratitude, and hospitality ('You may not fast on these two days')
explanationEn: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (RA) reported the Prophet ﷺ strictly forbade fasting on Eid al-Fitr and Yawm al-Nahr.

questionEn: What is the meaning of 'Yawm al-Nahr'?
optionsEn: Day of Sacrifice (specifically referring to slaughtering camels at the upper chest 'nahr', and livestock sacrifice generally)
explanationEn: 'Nahr' is the method of slaughtering camels standing with one foreleg tied; thus the 10th of Dhul-Hijjah bears the name Yawm al-Nahr.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Hajj 22:36, why does Allah describe camels (Al-Budn) as 'standing in line' (sawaff) when being sacrificed?
optionsEn: Because camels are slaughtered swiftly while standing (often with left foreleg hobbled, facing Qibla) while mentioning Allah's name over them
explanationEn: Ibn Umar (RA) saw a man slaughtering a camel kneeling and told him: 'Make it stand tied [on three legs]—this is the Sunnah of Muhammad ﷺ!'

questionEn: What words must be spoken over every Hady animal at the moment of slaughter?
optionsEn: 'Bismillahi Wallahu Akbar' (and 'Allahumma hadha minka wa lak')
explanationEn: Anas (RA) narrated the Prophet ﷺ said 'Bismillahi Wallahu Akbar' when sacrificing two horned rams with his own hand.

questionEn: Did the Prophet ﷺ sacrifice ONLY camels during the Farewell Hajj, or did he also sacrifice for his wives?
optionsEn: In addition to the 100 camels, Aisha (RA) reported the Prophet ﷺ sacrificed cattle (cows) on behalf of his wives!
He sacrificed nothing for his wives
explanationEn: Aisha (RA) narrated in Sahih al-Bukhari 1709: 'The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sacrificed cows on behalf of his wives during his Farewell Hajj.'

questionEn: What is the ruling if a pilgrim performing Hajj al-Tamattu' bought a sheep for Hady, and BEFORE reaching the slaughter place on the 10th the sheep died or was stolen through no fault of theirs?
optionsEn: They must replace an obligatory Tamattu'/Qiran Hady (or fast 10 days if genuinely unable financially); if it was a purely voluntary gifted Hady that died without negligence, they do not replace it
explanationEn: Because Tamattu' Hady is an obligation owed per Qur'an 2:196, losing an animal before slaughter means offering another (or fasting 3+7 days if financially unable); today's official voucher system eliminates this risk.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ tell Najiya al-Aslami (RA) to do if one of the voluntary Hady camels collapsed near death on the road before reaching the Haram?
optionsEn: Eat all of it himself and keep the rest for his family
Slaughter it, dip its sandal/garland marker in its blood on its side so needy travelers know it is charity, and NOT eat from it himself or let his caravan eat it—leaving it for poor passersby
explanationEn: This compassionate Hadith ensured poor desert travelers could benefit from a collapsed Hady animal without waste or suspicion of self-dealing.

questionEn: When a pilgrim completes Tawaf al-Ifadah and returns to Mina on the 10th, what clothes do they wear for the remaining Days of Tashreeq (11th–13th)?
optionsEn: They must put Ihram back on
Their normal clean, modest everyday clothes (shirts, thobes, trousers, abayas, hats/caps, perfume)—because once Rami and Halq are done, they are out of Ihram!
explanationEn: Many first-time pilgrims stay in white Ihram towels on the 11th–13th thinking Hajj requires it; in fact, wearing fresh clean regular clothes after Tahallul on the 10th follows the Sunnah.

questionEn: Should a pilgrim continue reciting the Talbiyah ('Labbayka Allahumma labbayk...') on the 11th, 12th, and 13th of Dhul-Hijjah?
optionsEn: No—the Talbiyah stops upon throwing the first pebble at Jamrat al-Aqabah on the 10th, and from Yawm al-Nahr onward pilgrims switch to Takbir ('Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, la ilaha illallah...')
explanationEn: Talbiyah belongs to the Ihram journey; once the first pebble hits Jamrat al-Aqabah, Takbirat al-Tashreeq take over through the 13th.

questionEn: What is the ruling if a pilgrim accidentally throws 8 pebbles instead of 7 at Jamrat al-Aqabah?
optionsEn: No harm at all—extra pebbles thrown by mistake do not hurt validity (just ensure at least 7 landed cleanly in the basin)
explanationEn: Adding an eighth accidentally out of doubt ensures the minimum seven are met; no penalty applies.

questionEn: Can a pilgrim who has a severe skin condition on their scalp (making razor shaving painful) perform Taqsir (trimming with scissors/clippers) instead of Halq?
optionsEn: No, bleeding with a razor is mandatory
They must wait until next year
Yes! Taqsir is completely valid for all men (and is the only option for women), especially when scalp irritation exists
They must pull hair by hand
explanationEn: While Halq earns triple the Prophetic supplication for mercy, Taqsir is explicitly endorsed in Qur'an 48:27 and Hadith as fully valid.

questionEn: If a pilgrim is in Hajj al-Ifrad (so they owe NO mandatory Hady), what is their sequence on Yawm al-Nahr (10th Dhul-Hijjah)?
optionsEn: They must still buy a sheep or Hajj is void
They perform: (1) Rami of Jamrat al-Aqabah, (2) Halq or Taqsir (unless offering a voluntary Hady first), and (3) Tawaf al-Ifadah (plus Sa'i if they didn't advance it after Tawaf al-Qudum)
explanationEn: Because Mufrids owe no mandatory Hady, their Eid morning progression goes straight from Rami to Halq/Taqsir to Tawaf al-Ifadah.

questionEn: What is the ruling if a pilgrim performs Sa'i between Safa and Marwah BEFORE Tawaf al-Ifadah on the 10th by mistake?
optionsEn: Opinions differ: the majority (Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi'i, Hanbali standard) require Sa'i to follow a valid Tawaf, while a notable Hadith in Sunan Abi Dawud (2015, 'I did Sa'i before Tawaf' — 'Do it, no harm') led Imam Ahmad in one narration and some scholars to excuse it out of ignorance/mistake—though repeating Sa'i after Tawaf is safest
explanationEn: To remain safely valid in all schools, perform Tawaf al-Ifadah first and then Sa'i (and if done in reverse by mistake, walk 7 quick Sa'i laps right after Tawaf if able).

questionEn: Why does the Prophet ﷺ pray Dhuhr in Mina on the 10th of Dhul-Hijjah according to Ibn Umar (RA), vs in Makkah according to Jabir (RA)? How do scholars harmonize both?
optionsEn: Both narrations are authentic: he went early to Makkah for Tawaf al-Ifadah, prayed Dhuhr in Makkah (Jabir), and returned to Mina where he led Dhuhr again for companions who stayed behind (Ibn Umar)—or prayed Dhuhr in one and repeated/returned before Dhuhr ended
There was no Dhuhr on the 10th
explanationEn: Imam al-Nawawi explained the Prophet ﷺ performed Tawaf al-Ifadah before Dhuhr, prayed Dhuhr in Makkah with those there, and upon returning swiftly to Mina led his Mina companions in Dhuhr (making it a Nafl for him while Fard for them, just as Mu'adh RA did).
reference: Sahih Muslim 1218; Sahih Muslim 1308; Sharh al-Nawawi

questionEn: When a pilgrim completes Rami al-Aqabah and shaves/trims on the 10th, may they trim their mustache and clip their fingernails right away?
optionsEn: No, nails remain banned until Muharram
Yes! Once Tahallul al-Awwal occurs (after Rami + Halq/Taqsir), cutting fingernails, trimming the mustache, bathing, putting on perfume, and wearing tailored clothes all become completely lawful
explanationEn: Taking a refreshing shower, clipping nails, putting on fresh clothes, and applying perfume before heading to Masjid al-Haram for Tawaf al-Ifadah feels deeply uplifting.

questionEn: What is the ruling if a pilgrim accidentally puts on normal clothes and perfume AFTER Rami al-Aqabah, forgetting to shave/trim their hair first?
optionsEn: They never need to cut hair

Because they have not yet performed Halq/Taqsir, they are still in Ihram—so they should remove stitched clothes/wash perfume immediately upon realizing, shave or trim their hair (with no Fidyah if genuinely forgetful), and then dress cleanly
explanationEn: Remember the pair required for Tahallul al-Awwal: Rami + Halq/Taqsir (or two of the three); skipping Halq leaves Ihram active.
