questionEn: Does a pilgrim who enters Masjid al-Haram for Tawaf al-Ifadah in regular clothes (after Tahallul al-Awwal) still cover both shoulders properly?
optionsEn: Yes—modest regular clothing covering the full 'awrah (including shoulders during Salah) is worn
No, men must still bare their right shoulder in a shirt
Shoes must be worn inside the Mataf
explanationEn: Normal modest attire (thobe, tunic, modest pants/shirt for men; modest abaya/dress for women) is completely proper for Tawaf al-Ifadah.

questionEn: If a pilgrim is in Hajj al-Qiran or Hajj al-Ifrad and did NOT do Sa'i after Tawaf al-Qudum, when MUST they perform their Hajj Sa'i?
optionsEn: Immediately after Tawaf al-Ifadah on or after the 10th of Dhul-Hijjah
Before standing at Arafah next year
explanationEn: Any pilgrim who postponed Sa'i (including all Tamattu' pilgrims and those Mufrids/Qarins who skipped it earlier) performs the 7 laps between Safa and Marwah right after Tawaf al-Ifadah.

questionEn: How does a pilgrim who has BOTH Tawaf al-Ifadah and Sa'i to do on the 10th manage their energy safely?
optionsEn: Hydrate with Zamzam after Tawaf, rest briefly between Tawaf's 2 rakaat and starting Sa'i if fatigued, and walk calmly rather than pushing in crowds
explanationEn: Drinking Zamzam after the 2 rakaat behind Maqam Ibrahim restores electrolytes and follows the exact Sunnah before walking over to Al-Safa.

questionEn: Can a pilgrim pray 'Tahiyyat al-Masjid' separately upon entering Masjid al-Haram if they are about to start Tawaf al-Ifadah?
optionsEn: No prayer is ever allowed in Masjid al-Haram
No—the greeting of Masjid al-Haram for one coming to circumambulate IS Tawaf itself (followed by its 2 Sunnah rakaat), unless an obligatory prayer congregation is already starting
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ began directly with Tawaf upon entering Masjid al-Haram, greeting the Sacred House before praying behind Maqam Ibrahim.

questionEn: What is the ruling on throwing pebbles at Jamrat al-Aqabah by standing on top of the wall or leaning dangerously over the railing?
optionsEn: Strictly unsafe and unnecessary—stand squarely behind the safety barrier, aim gently upward in a small arc so the pebble drops cleanly into the wide basin
explanationEn: The elliptic basin is very wide (~26+ meters across); even a gentle underhand toss from behind the barrier easily drops inside.

questionEn: If a pilgrim is in Mina on the 10th and wants to perform Hady themselves (not via electronic voucher), where must the slaughter take place?
optionsEn: Anywhere inside the Makkah Haram boundaries (including Mina's licensed slaughterhouses), following the Prophet's ﷺ words: 'I slaughtered here, and ALL of Mina is a place of slaughter, and all the alleys of Makkah are a place of slaughter'
explanationEn: Licensed municipal slaughterhouses in Al-Mu'aysim (Mina/Haram) ensure veterinary inspection, sanitation, and proper distribution within the Haram.

questionEn: In what case would a pilgrim owe TWO sacrifices in one Hajj?
optionsEn: For example, if a Tamattu' pilgrim owes their normal Tamattu' Hady AND also committed a separate penalty Dam (like crossing Miqat without Ihram or missing Mina Mabit without excuse)
explanationEn: Tamattu' Hady is a rite of gratitude (Nusuk), whereas a Dam for a missed Wajib is a separate expiation; each obligation stands on its own.

questionEn: If a pilgrim intends to offer a Hady animal that has a small slit or notch on its ear (as a branding mark), is it valid?
optionsEn: A minor ear nick/branding mark (less than half or majority of the ear) is disliked in Udhiyah/Hady by some, yet valid according to the majority if not severely mutilated, whereas missing an entire ear or one-eyedness disqualifies
explanationEn: In fact, the Prophet ﷺ himself marked (ish'ar) his Hady camels with a light mark on the hump so people knew they were dedicated to Allah.

questionEn: What is 'Al-Ish'ar' and 'Al-Taqlid' that the Prophet ﷺ practiced on his sacrificial camels when departing Madinah?
optionsEn: Marking the camel's right hump lightly and hanging a garland/sandal around its neck (Taqlid) to honor it publicly as an animal dedicated to the poor of the Haram
explanationEn: Aisha (RA) described weaving garlands for the Prophet's ﷺ Hady camels, visibly honoring Allah's symbols (22:32) along the journey.

questionEn: When a pilgrim completes Tawaf al-Ifadah on the 10th, what is the rule regarding praying inside the Hijr Isma'il (Hateem) afterward?
optionsEn: Praying inside Al-Hijr is a Rukn of Hajj

Praying voluntary rakaat inside Al-Hijr is blessed because Al-Hijr is part of the Kaaba—just as the Prophet ﷺ told Aisha (RA) 'Pray in Al-Hijr, for it is part of the House'—yet NEVER during peak crowding where it blocks or injures others
explanationEn: Aisha (RA) loved wishing to pray inside the Kaaba, so the Prophet ﷺ gave her that tender gift: praying inside Al-Hijr equals praying inside the Kaaba!

questionEn: What if a pilgrim loses Wudu while on the 4th lap of Sa'i after Tawaf al-Ifadah?
optionsEn: Continue and finish Sa'i cleanly! While having Wudu in Sa'i is Sunnah, Wudu is NOT a condition for Sa'i's validity
explanationEn: Knowing Wudu is required for Tawaf (around the Kaaba) but NOT for Sa'i saves tired pilgrims needless stress on crowded days.

questionEn: Why is it important for a pilgrim NOT to remove their Ihram BEFORE confirming their Adahi Hady slaughter if they wish to follow the safest scholarly opinion (or how do modern Hajj scholars advise)?
optionsEn: Must watch the sheep die personally

The Prophet ﷺ famously said 'If'al wa la haraj' when asked about shaving before slaughtering; so if Adahi confirms an approximate slaughter window (or even before exact SMS arrives), shaving after Rami is valid—though waiting for your slaughter slot when easy aligns with the ideal sequence
explanationEn: Both waiting briefly when convenient and relying on 'La haraj' when your group's schedule moves quickly are rooted cleanly in Prophetic precedent.

questionEn: What happens if a pilgrim performs Tawaf al-Ifadah, returns to Mina, and then realizes on the 11th they had only done 6 circuits of Tawaf instead of 7?
optionsEn: Majority (Shafi'i, Hanbali, Maliki) require repeating a full 7-circuit Tawaf al-Ifadah (since long interruption breaks continuity), whereas Hanafis allow completing 1 circuit if only 1 was missed (though repeating 7 circuits cleanly removes all doubt and keeps Hajj 100% sound!)
explanationEn: Counting carefully—tracking each circuit by lap landmarks or a simple counter—prevents ever miscounting this vital pillar.

questionEn: If a pilgrim is exhausted after Tawaf al-Ifadah on the 10th and misses the last bus back to Mina, spending the night in Makkah and returning to Mina early next morning, what is the ruling?
optionsEn: The night of the 10th–11th is NOT the night of Muzdalifah—it IS the first night of Tashreeq (night of the 11th)! Missing Mabit in Mina on the 11th night without excuse incurs a Dam/charity according to the majority, whereas genuine inability/traffic failure without negligence may excuse it
Staying in Makkah on the 10th night is preferred
explanationEn: Remember the calendar carefully: sunset after the 10th begins the night of the 11th of Dhul-Hijjah—the first night of Mina's Tashreeq stay!

questionEn: In Islamic Hijri timekeeping, when does the 'night of the 11th of Dhul-Hijjah' begin?
optionsEn: At sunset (Maghrib) of the 10th of Dhul-Hijjah, because the Islamic night always precedes its day
explanationEn: Understanding that the night of the 11th begins at Maghrib on the 10th ensures pilgrims return to Mina promptly on Eid evening rather than staying overnight in Makkah hotels.

questionEn: When a pilgrim returns to their Mina tent on the afternoon/evening of the 10th wearing clean ordinary clothes after Tahallul, what should fill their heart?
optionsEn: Relief that worship is over forever
Deep gratitude to Allah for carrying them safely through Arafah, Muzdalifah, and Tawaf al-Ifadah, ready to spend the peaceful Days of Tashreeq in dhikr
explanationEn: Eid in Mina celebrates forgiveness with Takbir, shared meals, and thankful remembrance.

questionEn: Is a pilgrim allowed to trim or shave his BEARD during Halq on the 10th of Dhul-Hijjah?
optionsEn: No—Halq applies strictly to the hair of the head, while letting the beard grow is an emphasized Prophetic Sunnah
Yes, shaving the beard is part of Halq
explanationEn: Qur'an 48:27 explicitly specifies 'muhalliqina ru'usakum' (shaving your HEADS); tell the barber clearly 'head only' before sitting in the chair.

questionEn: What is the ruling if a pilgrim is in Hajj al-Ifrad, performs Tawaf al-Qudum WITHOUT Sa'i on arrival, and then performs Tawaf al-Ifadah on the 10th?
optionsEn: They MUST perform Sa'i right after Tawaf al-Ifadah, because every Hajj requires at least one Hajj Sa'i
They pay a sheep instead of Sa'i
explanationEn: Sa'i is an obligatory pillar of Hajj (in Shafi'i/Maliki/Hanbali majority; Wajib in Hanafi); performing it either after Tawaf al-Qudum or after Tawaf al-Ifadah fulfills it.

questionEn: If a pilgrim in Hajj al-Tamattu' already performed Sa'i for their Umrah upon arrival, why can't that Umrah Sa'i count for their Hajj too?
optionsEn: Because in Tamattu', the Umrah and the Hajj are two completely separate acts of worship separated by exiting Ihram—each requiring its own Tawaf and Sa'i
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas and Aisha (RA) clearly narrated that Tamattu' pilgrims perform Sa'i for Umrah first and a second Sa'i for Hajj after Tawaf al-Ifadah.

questionEn: What is the rule regarding using scented soap or deodorant AFTER completing Rami al-Aqabah and Halq/Taqsir on the 10th?
optionsEn: Completely permissible! Applying perfume is explicitly confirmed by Aisha (RA) as lawful immediately upon achieving Tahallul al-Awwal before Tawaf al-Ifadah
explanationEn: Aisha (RA) specifically perfumed the Prophet ﷺ after he exited partial Ihram and before he entered Masjid al-Haram for Tawaf al-Ifadah.

questionEn: What happens if a pilgrim stays in their Makkah hotel on the 10th morning waiting for crowding to drop, and goes to stone Jamrat al-Aqabah at 4:30 PM instead of 8:00 AM?
optionsEn: Completely valid and wise—late afternoon stoning on the 10th avoids extreme heat and crowds with zero penalty
explanationEn: The Prophet's ﷺ own ruling ('I stoned after evening' — 'No harm!') validates afternoon and evening stoning on the 10th.

questionEn: How should a pilgrim who finds a stray lost wallet or phone on the crowded road between Mina and Masjid al-Haram on Yawm al-Nahr act?
optionsEn: Keep it as a Hajj souvenir

Because the Prophet ﷺ prohibited picking up lost property in Makkah except to announce/return it, hand it immediately to official Makkah Lost & Found security or leave it safely visible to authorities rather than keeping it
explanationEn: Makkah's sanctity includes heightened protection over lost property (luqatah); turning found items in immediately to official Haram lost-and-found offices helps stranded pilgrims recover passports and money.

questionEn: After completing all four rites of the 10th of Dhul-Hijjah—Rami, Hady, Halq, and Tawaf al-Ifadah—what remain as the final rites of Hajj?
optionsEn: Spending the Days of Tashreeq (11th–12th/13th) in Mina, stoning all 3 Jamarat daily after Zawal, and performing Tawaf al-Wada' (Farewell Tawaf) before leaving Makkah
Nothing—go straight to the airport from Arafah
explanationEn: With the Days of Tashreeq and Farewell Tawaf remaining, the pilgrim finishes Hajj smoothly in gratitude and remembrance.

questionEn: Why are the 11th, 12th, and 13th days of Dhul-Hijjah historically called 'Ayyam al-Tashreeq'?
optionsEn: Because pilgrims used to travel east to Iraq
Because pilgrims sliced and sun-dried (yusharriqun) the sacrificial meat in Mina's sunlight—or because Eid prayers/sacrifices took place after sunrise (shuruq)
explanationEn: Before refrigeration, pilgrims cured and dried strips of Hady meat in the bright sun at Mina so it could sustain them on their long caravan journeys home.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about the Days of Tashreeq regarding fasting and spiritual atmosphere?
optionsEn: 'The Days of Tashreeq are days of eating, drinking, and remembering Allah (dhikr)'
explanationEn: Nubayshah al-Hudhali (RA) narrated this joyful Hadith prohibiting voluntary fasting on the 11th, 12th, and 13th so believers celebrate Allah's hospitality with gratitude and Takbir.

questionEn: Who is the ONLY category of Muslim permitted by the Sunnah to fast during the Days of Tashreeq (11th–13th Dhul-Hijjah)?
optionsEn: A Tamattu' or Qiran pilgrim who cannot afford a Hady animal and could not complete their 3-day Hajj fast before Eid
explanationEn: Aisha and Ibn Umar (RA) explicitly reported: 'No concession was granted to fast during the Days of Tashreeq except for the pilgrim who did not find a Hady.'

questionEn: When does the valid daily time window for stoning the three Jamarat begin on the 11th, 12th, and 13th of Dhul-Hijjah?
optionsEn: After Zawal (solar zenith / Dhuhr time enters), extending through the afternoon and night until Fajr of the next morning
Only during the 15 minutes before Maghrib
explanationEn: Jabir (RA) narrated: 'The Prophet ﷺ stoned on Yawm al-Nahr at forenoon (Duha), and after that [on the Days of Tashreeq] after the sun passed its zenith (Zawal).' Throwing before Zawal on 11th–13th is invalid in the four schools.

questionEn: If a pilgrim is caught by crowds after Zawal on the 11th or 12th and finishes stoning the three Jamarat after Maghrib or at 10:00 PM at night, is their Rami valid?
optionsEn: No, night stoning on the 11th is invalid
Yes! The window that opens at Zawal on the 11th remains valid all afternoon and throughout the night until Fajr of the 12th (and likewise on the night of the 12th–13th if staying for Nafar Thani)
explanationEn: Stoning in the cooler evening after Maghrib or Isha on the 11th dramatically reduces heatstroke and congestion while remaining valid in the majority of juristic rulings.

questionEn: What happens if a pilgrim plans to leave Mina early on the 12th (Nafar Awwal)—can they stone the 3 Jamarat BEFORE Zawal on the 12th to catch an afternoon flight?
optionsEn: The four Sunni schools strictly require waiting until AFTER Zawal (Dhuhr) on the 12th; stoning before Zawal on the 12th is not valid in the four schools (though a minority opinion attributed to Ibn Abbas/Ata' allowed it in hardship—pilgrims should schedule flights late enough to stone cleanly after Dhuhr!)
explanationEn: Ibn Umar (RA) said: 'We used to wait for the sun to pass its zenith (Zawal), and then we would stone.' Scheduling flights on the 13th or late evening of the 12th avoids violating Zawal.

questionEn: When walking from Mina's tents toward the Jamarat on the 11th, 12th, and 13th, in which exact order are the three pillars stoned?
optionsEn: Al-Jamrat al-Sughra (First/Small, nearest Masjid al-Khayf) → Al-Wusta (Middle) → Al-Aqabah (Largest, nearest Makkah)
explanationEn: Pilgrims walk westward from Mina toward Makkah, encountering Small → Middle → Large naturally in sequence—throwing 7 single pebbles with 'Allahu Akbar' at each (21 pebbles per day).

questionEn: After throwing the 7th pebble at Jamrat al-Sughra (First Pillar) on the 11th, 12th, and 13th, what is the cherished Prophetic Sunnah?
optionsEn: Step forward/to the side out of the throwing lane, face the Qiblah, raise both hands, and stand for a long, heartfelt dua (around the length of Surah Al-Baqarah)
explanationEn: Ibn Umar (RA) narrated the Prophet ﷺ would step slightly ahead to a clear spot on the right, face Qibla, raise his hands, and make lengthy dua after both the Small and Middle Jamarat.

questionEn: After stoning Jamrat al-Wusta (the Middle Pillar) on the 11th–13th, what did the Prophet ﷺ do next?
optionsEn: Stepped slightly to the left (out of crowded throwing paths), faced the Qiblah, raised both hands, and stood for another lengthy dua before walking to Aqabah
explanationEn: Thus on each Tashreeq day, pilgrims pause twice for deep Qiblah-facing dua (after Sughra and after Wusta) and do NOT pause for dua after Aqabah.

questionEn: Why do pilgrims NOT stop to make dua after stoning Jamrat al-Aqabah on the 11th, 12th, and 13th (just as on the 10th)?
optionsEn: Because dua is banned in Makkah
Because the Prophet ﷺ himself never paused to make dua after Jamrat al-Aqabah—he turned and departed immediately—and following his exact Sunnah keeps exit ramps clear
explanationEn: Ibn Umar (RA) explicitly observed: 'Then he stoned Jamrat al-Aqabah... and departed without standing beside it.'

questionEn: If a pilgrim mistakenly stones Jamrat al-Aqabah FIRST and then goes back to Sughra and Wusta on the 11th, is the wrong order valid?
optionsEn: No—the Prophet's ﷺ sequence (Sughra → Wusta → Aqabah) is a condition for validity in the majority view; so they must re-stone Wusta and Aqabah in order after Sughra
explanationEn: Because the Jamarat bridge layout flows naturally from Sughra → Wusta → Aqabah, following the signs automatically preserves the exact order.

questionEn: How many total pebbles are thrown across ALL three pillars on a single day of Tashreeq (11th, 12th, or 13th)?
optionsEn: 21 pebbles per day (7 at Sughra + 7 at Wusta + 7 at Aqabah)
explanationEn: 7 pebbles at each of the three pillars equals 21 pebbles each day on the 11th, 12th, and (if staying) 13th.

questionEn: If a pilgrim misses stoning on the 11th of Dhul-Hijjah completely (e.g., hospitalized or forgot until the 12th after Zawal), how can they make it up?
optionsEn: They cannot make it up—Hajj is lost

According to the majority (Shafi'i, Hanbali, Maliki), on the 12th after Zawal they first stone the 3 Jamarat for the missed 11th (Sughra→Wusta→Aqabah), and then stone the 3 Jamarat for the 12th in order—with no Dam owed for making it up within the Days of Tashreeq!
They throw 21 pebbles into Aqabah alone
explanationEn: Making up missed Tashreeq stoning before sunset of the 13th (in day-by-day order after Zawal) leaves the pilgrimage completely intact.

questionEn: What is 'Mabit' in Mina during the nights of Tashreeq (night of the 11th and night of the 12th), and what is its juristic status?
optionsEn: Spending the majority (more than half) of each night inside Mina's boundaries—Wajib according to Maliki, Shafi'i, and Hanbali majority (Sunnah in Hanafi fiqh)
A pillar that voids Hajj if missed
explanationEn: Majority jurists treat spending the majority of the 11th and 12th nights in Mina as Wajib; staying cleanly in one's Mina tent satisfies every school.

questionEn: Which two professions/roles did the Prophet ﷺ explicitly grant exemption from sleeping overnight in Mina during the Days of Tashreeq?
optionsEn: Camel herders (shepherds tending flocks outside Mina) and the water-bearers of Zamzam (Al-'Abbas and Banu Abd al-Muttalib serving pilgrims in Makkah)
explanationEn: Ibn Umar (RA) narrated Al-Abbas (RA) asked permission to stay in Makkah during the nights of Mina for Zamzam water service (Siqayah), and the Prophet ﷺ permitted him—and likewise excused shepherds.

questionEn: How do contemporary scholars apply the Prophet's ﷺ exemption of Zamzam water-servers and herders to modern Hajj workers?
optionsEn: Doctors, paramedics, traffic police, rescue teams, bus drivers, and camp staff actively serving pilgrims overnight in Makkah are likewise excused from Mina Mabit with zero Dam
Tourists shopping at night are also excused
explanationEn: Essential medical and public-safety staff serve the same sacred communal need as Siqayah; ordinary pilgrims without duty must stay in Mina.

questionEn: If Mina tents are completely overflowing to capacity and official Hajj authorities assign a pilgrim's camp just beyond Mina's boundary (in adjacent Muzdalifah), does that pilgrim owe a Dam?
optionsEn: No! Scholars (Fatawa Ibn Baz / Ibn Uthaymeen / Lajnah) rule that when Mina has zero remaining space and a pilgrim camps at the nearest official overflow border, there is no sin and no Dam ('Allah burdens no soul beyond its capacity')
They must sleep on top of Jamarat
explanationEn: Just like praying outside a full mosque when rows connect, being placed in adjacent official overflow camps out of necessity carries zero penalty.

questionEn: What is the meaning of 'Nafar Awwal' (Early Departure) vs 'Nafar Thani' (Second/Full Departure) in Qur'an 2:203?
optionsEn: Leaving Arafah at noon vs evening
Nafar Awwal is departing Mina after stoning on the 12th of Dhul-Hijjah BEFORE sunset; Nafar Thani is staying the night of the 13th in Mina and departing after stoning all 3 Jamarat on the 13th
explanationEn: Qur'an 2:203 explicitly grants both options: 'Whoever hastens [his departure] in two days—there is no sin upon him; and whoever delays [until the third day]—there is no sin upon him, for him who fears Allah.'

questionEn: Which of the two—Nafar Awwal (leaving on 12th) or Nafar Thani (staying until 13th)—did the Prophet ﷺ himself perform, making it slightly more meritorious?
optionsEn: Nafar Thani—the Prophet ﷺ remained through the 13th of Dhul-Hijjah, stoned all 3 Jamarat after Zawal, and then descended to Al-Abtah
explanationEn: Staying for the 13th (Nafar Thani) also lets pilgrims avoid the intense rush of millions departing simultaneously on the 12th afternoon.

questionEn: If a pilgrim intends Nafar Awwal (early departure on the 12th), by what exact deadline MUST they exit the boundaries of Mina?
optionsEn: Before sunset (Maghrib) of the 12th of Dhul-Hijjah—if sunset catches them still inside Mina without having started departure/packed up, the majority (Umar, Ibn Umar, Malik, Shafi'i, Ahmad) rule they must stay for the night of the 13th and stone on the 13th
explanationEn: Once sunset of the 12th enters while the pilgrim is still settled in Mina, staying the night and stoning after Zawal on the 13th becomes binding (with minor leniency if already packed inside a traffic-jammed bus leaving Mina at sunset).

questionEn: What if a pilgrim intended Nafar Awwal on the 12th, stoned all 3 pillars after Zawal, boarded their departing bus BEFORE sunset, and the bus was delayed inside Mina traffic past sunset?
optionsEn: They must abandon the bus and walk back to tents

Scholars rule that since they had already packed, exited their tent, and began departing before sunset—being trapped solely by road congestion—they may continue leaving and do NOT owe staying for the 13th
explanationEn: Because they initiated Nafar Awwal prior to sunset rather than remaining settled in Mina, traffic gridlock does not compel them to stay an extra day.
reference: Fatawa Ibn Baz; Fatawa Ibn Uthaymeen

questionEn: Why does Qur'an 2:203 end the permission for leaving in two days or three with the words '...li-man ittaqa' (for whoever fears Allah)?
optionsEn: Because only scholars can choose Nafar Awwal
To remind pilgrims that whether they leave on the 12th or 13th, the true measure of Hajj is returning home with ongoing Taqwa (piety), not merely finishing rituals swiftly
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas and commentators note 'for him who fears Allah' teaches that Allah accepts both schedules from a heart committed to obedience after Hajj.

questionEn: After leaving Mina on the 12th or 13th, where did the Prophet ﷺ briefly alight and rest in Makkah's outskirts before performing Tawaf al-Wada'?
optionsEn: Al-Muhassab (Al-Abtah) valley just outside Makkah, where he prayed Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, and Isha and napped briefly before entering Makkah at pre-dawn for Tawaf al-Wada'
explanationEn: Note Aisha (RA) clarified that stopping at Al-Abtah was simply a convenient resting camp the Prophet ﷺ used for departure, NOT an obligatory Hajj rite (Sahih al-Bukhari 1766).

questionEn: What is 'Tawaf al-Wada'' (the Farewell Tawaf), and what is its juristic status?
optionsEn: The final 7-circuit Tawaf around the Kaaba before departing Makkah—Wajib (obligatory) for all non-Makkan pilgrims (except menstruating/postnatal women), incurring a Dam if omitted without excuse
A Rukn whose miss cancels Hajj completely
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) narrated: 'The people were commanded that their last covenant (time) should be with the House, except that a concession was granted to menstruating women.'

questionEn: Who is explicitly exempted from Tawaf al-Wada' without needing to pay any Dam or wait in Makkah?
optionsEn: Menstruating women (Ha'id) and women in postnatal bleeding (Nufasa')—provided they have already completed Tawaf al-Ifadah!
explanationEn: When Safiyyah (RA) menstruated after already completing Tawaf al-Ifadah, the Prophet ﷺ exempted her from Tawaf al-Wada' and permitted the whole caravan to depart immediately.

questionEn: Is there any Sa'i between Al-Safa and Al-Marwah after Tawaf al-Wada'?
optionsEn: No! Tawaf al-Wada' consists ONLY of 7 circuits around the Kaaba followed by 2 Sunnah rakaat behind Maqam Ibrahim and Zamzam/dua—there is NEVER a Sa'i after Tawaf al-Wada'
explanationEn: Sa'i belongs to Umrah and Hajj (after Qudum or Ifadah), never to the Farewell Tawaf.

questionEn: Should men perform Idtiba (baring the right shoulder) or Raml (brisk jogging) during Tawaf al-Wada'?
optionsEn: No—men wear regular clothes during Tawaf al-Wada' and walk at a normal, reverent pace with zero Raml or Idtiba
explanationEn: Both Idtiba and Raml are exclusively for the arrival Tawaf (Umrah / Tawaf al-Qudum), never for Ifadah or Wada'.

questionEn: If a pilgrim performs Tawaf al-Wada' and then stops for a few minutes to buy food for the road, pack suitcases at the hotel, or wait for their airport bus, is their Tawaf al-Wada' still valid?
optionsEn: Yes! Brief travel necessities—loading luggage, checking out, grabbing a meal for the journey, or waiting for the scheduled bus—do NOT invalidate Tawaf al-Wada' (though one shouldn't linger unnecessarily shopping for souvenirs or stay days afterward)
No, even buying a bottle of water cancels it
They must walk backwards out of Makkah
explanationEn: Making Tawaf al-Wada' the last worshipful act before departure allows practical checkout/transit tasks without unreasonable hardship.
reference: Fatawa Ibn Baz; Fatawa Ibn Uthaymeen

questionEn: What common mistake do some pilgrims make right after Tawaf al-Wada' when exiting Masjid al-Haram?
optionsEn: Walking BACKWARDS facing the Kaaba out the door—an unfounded custom with NO basis in the Sunnah (the Prophet ﷺ walked out normally facing forward)
explanationEn: Walking backwards in dense exit crowds risks tripping and injury and has zero prophetic origin; walk forward calmly while keeping heartfelt love for Allah's House.

questionEn: If a pilgrim stays in Makkah for two or three MORE days after performing Tawaf al-Wada' to rest or shop, must they repeat Tawaf al-Wada' right before actually leaving?
optionsEn: No, one from last week works
Only if they travel by camel
Yes, because Tawaf al-Wada' must be their final covenant with the Kaaba before departing Makkah
explanationEn: Delaying departure for a day or two after Tawaf al-Wada' breaks the rule of making it the last act; performing a fresh 7-circuit Farewell Tawaf before boarding the departing coach resolves it cleanly.

questionEn: What is the rule if a pilgrim is leaving Mina on the 12th or 13th and stops in Makkah ONLY for Tawaf al-Wada'—and also plans to visit Madinah afterward?
optionsEn: They skip Tawaf al-Wada' because Madinah is in Saudi Arabia
They do Tawaf al-Wada' in Madinah
Only international flights need Tawaf al-Wada'
They MUST perform Tawaf al-Wada' before leaving Makkah for Madinah (or Jeddah/home), because it is the farewell upon departing Makkah after Hajj
explanationEn: Any non-Makkan traveling past Qasr/Miqat distance—whether heading straight home or to Madinah first—performs Tawaf al-Wada' before leaving Makkah.

questionEn: If a permanent resident of Makkah performs Hajj, must they perform Tawaf al-Wada'?
optionsEn: No! Residents of Makkah are not departing the city, so Tawaf al-Wada' is NOT obligatory upon them (as the Prophet ﷺ instructed departing visitors: 'Let none depart until his last covenant is with the House')
explanationEn: Tawaf al-Wada' bids farewell to Makkah; those living permanently in Makkah remain at home.

questionEn: During the Days of Tashreeq in Mina, how should pilgrims pray the 5 daily prayers?
optionsEn: Shortened (Qasr: 2 rakaat for Dhuhr, Asr, Isha; 3 Maghrib; 2 Fajr) WITHOUT combining them—each prayer in its own proper time
explanationEn: Just as on the 8th, staying stationary in Mina during Tashreeq follows Qasr without Jam', uniting campmates in calm congregational prayer five times daily.

questionEn: What is the wording of the famous 'Takbirat al-Tashreeq' recited after obligatory prayers from Yawm al-Nahr through Asr of the 13th?
optionsEn: 'Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, la ilaha illallah, wallahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar wa lillahil-hamd'
explanationEn: Reciting these joyous Takbirs aloud in Mina tents, walkways, and after prayers embodies Qur'an 2:203: 'And remember Allah during [specific] numbered days.'
reference: Qur'an 2:203; Sahih al-Bukhari (Bab al-Takbir Ayyam Mina)

questionEn: Which great Companion and his son-in-law used to recite Takbir loudly inside their tent in Mina during Tashreeq until the whole valley echoed with Takbir?
optionsEn: Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) and Abu Hurayrah / Ibn Umar (RA)—Umar's Takbir in his leather tent caused Masjid al-Khayf and the markets of Mina to resound with Takbir!
explanationEn: Sahih al-Bukhari records how Umar (RA) initiated Takbir from his tent, inspiring everyone in the mosque and streets until all Mina shook with Allah's praise.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Kitab al-'Idayn, Bab al-Takbir Ayyam Mina)

questionEn: When do non-pilgrims start Takbir al-Muqayyad (post-prayer Takbir) in Dhul-Hijjah compared to pilgrims?
optionsEn: Non-pilgrims start after Fajr on the 9th (Day of Arafah) through Asr of the 13th; pilgrims switch from Talbiyah to Takbir once they stone Jamrat al-Aqabah on the 10th (continuing through Asr of the 13th)
Pilgrims start on the 1st of Muharram
explanationEn: Because pilgrims are still reciting the Talbiyah throughout the 9th until Jamrat al-Aqabah on the 10th, their Takbir takes over seamlessly right where Talbiyah ends.

questionEn: Can a pilgrim leave Mina during the daytime on the 11th or 12th to go to Makkah for Tawaf al-Ifadah (or to shower in a hotel) and then return to Mina before nightfall?
optionsEn: No, leaving Mina in the daytime cancels Hajj
Yes! Exiting Mina temporarily during the day—and returning to spend the majority of the night inside Mina and stone after Zawal—is completely permissible
explanationEn: What is Wajib on the nights of 11th and 12th is Mabit (overnight stay inside Mina) and stoning after Zawal; visiting Makkah in the daytime between rites is totally allowed.

questionEn: What is the minimum portion of the night that must be spent in Mina on the nights of the 11th and 12th to fulfill the Wajib of Mabit?
optionsEn: Every single second from sunset to sunrise with zero departure
More than half of the night (the majority of the hours between Maghrib and Fajr)
explanationEn: Majority jurists (Shafi'i, Hanbali, Maliki) define Mabit as staying in Mina for over half the night; settling in before midnight until Fajr fulfills it effortlessly.

questionEn: What if a healthy pilgrim deliberately skips spending the night in Mina on BOTH the 11th and 12th nights (sleeping in a luxury Makkah hotel instead without excuse)?
optionsEn: According to the majority of scholars, they have neglected a Wajib of Hajj and must offer a compensatory Dam (a sheep distributed to the poor of the Haram) and repent—while in Hanafi fiqh it is disliked without Dam
explanationEn: Sleeping in Makkah out of mere luxury when space exists in Mina contradicts the Prophetic Mabit and incurs Dam under the majority view.

questionEn: Is a pilgrim allowed to go to Al-Tan'im to perform an extra Umrah AFTER finishing Hajj (on the 13th or 14th) before flying home?
optionsEn: Doing an extra Umrah after Hajj is permissible (as Aisha RA did after Hajj because she had not completed a separate Umrah earlier), though scholars remind pilgrims that the Prophet ﷺ and the Companions who already completed Umrah did NOT add extra Umrahs after Hajj—focusing instead on Tawaf and prayer in Masjid al-Haram
explanationEn: Remember why Aisha (RA) cried and asked for Tan'im: her menses prevented her from doing a separate Umrah before Arafah (she had folded into Qiran), whereas her brother Abdur-Rahman did not make an extra Umrah for himself there.

questionEn: When stoning the three Jamarat on the 11th, 12th, and 13th, if a pilgrim drops one of their pebbles inside a crowded walkway, should they stop and bend down right in the moving crowd to look for it?
optionsEn: Yes, crawl between people's feet immediately
Never risk getting trampled in a dense walking stream! Simply move onward safely using your spare pebbles (that's why bringing 5–10 extra spare pebbles is so helpful)
explanationEn: Bending down in moving crowds is one of the main causes of falls and injuries; always carry spare pebbles in your pouch!

questionEn: What should a pilgrim say if they accidentally bump into someone while walking to or from the Jamarat?
optionsEn: Smile, gently say 'Afwan / forgive me, May Allah accept your Hajj,' and keep moving calmly
explanationEn: Gentleness (rifq) in crowded walkways preserves brotherhood and keeps the atmosphere of worship intact.

questionEn: How many total pebbles are thrown during the entire Hajj if a pilgrim departs early on the 12th (Nafar Awwal)?
optionsEn: 49 pebbles (7 on the 10th + 21 on the 11th + 21 on the 12th)
explanationEn: 7 + 21 + 21 = 49 pebbles for Nafar Awwal.

questionEn: How many total pebbles are thrown during the entire Hajj if a pilgrim stays for the 13th (Nafar Thani)?
optionsEn: 70 pebbles (7 on the 10th + 21 on the 11th + 21 on the 12th + 21 on the 13th)
explanationEn: 7 + 21 + 21 + 21 = 70 pebbles for completing all three Days of Tashreeq.

questionEn: If a pilgrim is in Mina on the 11th and notices the dua spot right next to Jamrat al-Sughra is packed, how should they perform the Sunnah dua after Sughra and Wusta?
optionsEn: Step forward/to the side well clear of the throwing zone, face the Qiblah, and make dua calmly without obstructing incoming pilgrims
explanationEn: Ibn Umar (RA) noted the Prophet ﷺ moved forward away from the pillar before pausing to supplicate—prioritizing unobstructed safety.

questionEn: What is the ruling on performing Tawaf al-Ifadah AFTER leaving Mina on the 12th or 13th—if someone postponed it due to crowds or menstruation?
optionsEn: Completely valid with zero Dam—Tawaf al-Ifadah has no narrow expiry deadline, though completing it promptly before leaving Makkah is essential (since marital intimacy remains unlawful until it is done)
explanationEn: Remember: a pilgrim cannot return home permanently without completing Tawaf al-Ifadah (a Rukn of Hajj)!

questionEn: What happens if someone mistakenly flies back to their home country WITHOUT performing Tawaf al-Ifadah (thinking Tawaf al-Qudum or Tawaf al-Wada' covered it)?
optionsEn: They must do two Umrahs at home
Because Tawaf al-Ifadah is a fundamental Rukn of Hajj, their Hajj remains incomplete and marital intimacy remains prohibited until they travel back to Makkah and perform Tawaf al-Ifadah!
explanationEn: Never confuse Tawaf al-Qudum (arrival), Tawaf al-Ifadah (the Hajj pillar), and Tawaf al-Wada' (farewell); confirming Tawaf al-Ifadah (+ due Sa'i) before leaving Makkah is vital.

questionEn: What if someone leaves Makkah forgetting Tawaf al-Wada' (after having completed Tawaf al-Ifadah) and remembers halfway to Jeddah airport or back home?
optionsEn: If still close enough to return easily before traveling Qasr distance, go back and perform Tawaf al-Wada'; if already far or boarded a flight home, Hajj remains valid and they send a Dam (one sheep slaughtered and distributed to the poor of Makkah's Haram)
explanationEn: This clearly illustrates the difference between a Rukn (Tawaf al-Ifadah, irreplaceable by Dam) and a Wajib (Tawaf al-Wada', reparable by Dam if unable to return).

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ do on the 11th and 12th days of Tashreeq in Mina besides stoning the Jamarat and leading prayers?
optionsEn: He stayed locked alone without speaking
He taught his Companions, answered pilgrims' questions ('Do it, no harm'), delivered reminders on Muslim brotherhood, and celebrated Allah's remembrance
explanationEn: Mina during Tashreeq functioned as the Prophet's ﷺ open-air academy of mercy, unity, and spiritual reflection.

questionEn: When the Prophet ﷺ spent the Tashreeq days in Mina, where did he settle—in a house, or in a tent?
optionsEn: In a simple tent pitched in Mina near Masjid al-Khayf, sharing the simplicity of every pilgrim
explanationEn: Aisha (RA) narrated that when she asked about building a house in Mina to shade him, he declined saying: 'Mina is the camping ground of whoever arrives first!'—preserving Mina as open public trust for all pilgrims.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ declare when asked if they should build a permanent private structure for him in Mina?
optionsEn: 'No! Mina is the resting place for whoever arrives first (Munakh man sabaq)'
explanationEn: Preserving Mina as communal public endowment (waqf) ensures every generation of pilgrims has a shared home during Tashreeq.

questionEn: If a pilgrim is praying in Masjid al-Khayf during the Days of Tashreeq, what should they avoid during the quiet afternoons?
optionsEn: Turning the mosque into noisy political debate or littering; instead devote quiet hours to Qur'an, dhikr, resting respectfully, and sharing knowledge gently
explanationEn: Masjid al-Khayf holds profound historic sanctity; treating it with reverence honors seventy prophets who prayed there.

questionEn: If a pilgrim performs Tawaf al-Wada' at 11:00 PM at night and their flight is at 8:00 AM the next morning, may they sleep a few hours at their Makkah hotel before heading straight to the airport?
optionsEn: No, sleeping even 10 minutes voids Tawaf al-Wada'

Scholars permit brief rest/packing directly connected to an imminent morning departure (if staying in Makkah only for departure logistics), though timing Tawaf al-Wada' right before leaving for the airport is cleaner and safest
They must sleep inside Masjid al-Haram
explanationEn: Whenever practical, perform Tawaf al-Wada' right before your final check-out and transfer to Jeddah airport so it is unmistakably your final act in Makkah.
reference: Fatawa Ibn Baz; Fatawa Ibn Uthaymeen

questionEn: What is the ruling if a pilgrim performs Tawaf al-Wada' and then joins ONE obligatory Fard prayer (like Fajr) in Masjid al-Haram right before walking out to the bus?
optionsEn: Completely valid and praiseworthy! Catching an obligatory prayer while walking out does not count as lingering for worldly stay
explanationEn: If the Adhan/Iqamah sounds as you finish your 2 rakaat of Wada', praying Fard with the congregation and departing immediately afterward is completely fine.

questionEn: Can a pilgrim who completed Hajj perform a voluntary Tawaf on behalf of a deceased parent during the Days of Tashreeq, or give charity?
optionsEn: Tawaf can be bought for cash

Offering voluntary Sadaqah, making heartfelt dua for parents at the Kaaba/Jamarat, and dedicating a whole Umrah/Hajj al-Badal (after one's own obligations) benefit parents; scholars differ on gifting solitary voluntary Tawaf, while dua and charity are unanimously agreed upon!
explanationEn: Making abundant dua for living and deceased parents during Hajj—at Arafah, Sughra, Wusta, and Tawaf—and giving charity on their behalf are universally agreed ways to honor them.

questionEn: What should a pilgrim do if they realize on the 13th (after stoning for the 13th) that they missed ONE stone at Jamrat al-Wusta on the 12th?
optionsEn: If still in Mina before sunset on the 13th, stone the missing day/pillar cleanly (or if already left Makkah/past Tashreeq, scholars rule missing 1–2 pebbles incurs a small charity/mudd of food rather than a full Dam, while missing a whole day's stoning incurs a Dam)
Repeat the entire Hajj next year
explanationEn: Islamic jurisprudence distinguishes proportionally between missing 1–2 pebbles versus neglecting an entire day's Rami.

questionEn: Which two Jamarat pillars are followed by raising hands in long dua on the 11th, 12th, and 13th?
explanationEn: Never forget: Dua after 1st (Sughra) ✓, Dua after 2nd (Wusta) ✓, NO dua after 3rd (Aqabah) ✗.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say when someone at Mina on the Days of Tashreeq asked about delaying stoning two days together to avoid daily trips?
optionsEn: Combining all 3 days on the 10th is Sunnah

Companions reported the Prophet ﷺ permitted camel herders to stone one day and skip the next (combining two days' stoning on the second day) out of genuine hardship, whereas ordinary pilgrims stone daily after Zawal
explanationEn: 'Asim ibn 'Adi (RA) narrated the Prophet ﷺ granted herders concession to combine two days' Rami on one day—showing Shariah flexibility for legitimate occupational hardship.

questionEn: What is the rule if a pilgrim is unable to stone on the 11th due to severe illness, recovers on the 12th, and is going to stone both the 11th and 12th after Zawal on the 12th—in what order do they throw?
optionsEn: Throw all 42 pebbles at Aqabah only
Complete the full round of the 11th (Sughra → Wusta → Aqabah) first, then start over from Sughra → Wusta → Aqabah for the 12th
explanationEn: Preserving both chronological order (11th before 12th) and spatial order (Sughra → Wusta → Aqabah) keeps missed stoning clean and valid.

questionEn: During the Days of Tashreeq in Mina, is there any restriction on visiting friends or scholars in neighboring camps?
optionsEn: No restriction at all—visiting brothers and sisters in faith, sharing meals, and attending beneficial reminders in Mina camps deepens Ummah bonds
explanationEn: After the intensity of Arafah and Eid morning, Tashreeq days allow Muslims from every continent to share stories, warmth, and Islamic brotherhood.

questionEn: What is the ruling on performing Tawaf al-Wada' by wheelchair or upper-floor Mataf if a pilgrim is tired after completing all Days of Tashreeq?
optionsEn: Upper-floor Tawaf does not count for Wada'
Completely valid and safe—choosing upper tiers or wheelchair assistance completes Tawaf al-Wada' cleanly without exhaustion or crowding risk
explanationEn: Protecting your health at the end of a strenuous 5-day Hajj while still honoring the Kaaba properly is wise and fully valid.

questionEn: What heartfelt supplications are ideal while performing Tawaf al-Wada' around the Kaaba for the last time?
optionsEn: Thanking Allah for inviting you to His House, asking Him to accept your Hajj, forgive shortcomings in the rites, keep you steadfast in Islam, and invite you and your family back again and again
explanationEn: Leaving the Sacred House with humble gratitude and longing to return embodies Allah's promise in 2:125 ('mathabatan lin-nas').

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ command: 'Let none of you depart until his last covenant is with the House' (Sahih Muslim 1327)?
optionsEn: So the pilgrim's final physical memory and farewell act in Makkah is intimate devotion around Allah's Sacred House, sealing the heart with reverence
explanationEn: Closing Hajj right where Ibrahim (AS) raised the Kaaba binds the pilgrim's heart permanently to the Qiblah.

questionEn: If a pilgrim visits Al-Masjid al-Haram after completing Tawaf al-Wada' ONLY because their spouse forgot a bag inside the mosque gate, must they repeat Tawaf al-Wada'?
optionsEn: No, stepping briefly to retrieve an item or help someone without intending to stay in Makkah does not cancel Tawaf al-Wada'
explanationEn: Intentional lingering in Makkah requires repeating Wada', whereas unintended brief delays or retrieving a lost item do not.

questionEn: What happens if a pilgrim completes Tawaf al-Ifadah on the 12th AFTER leaving Mina (having done Nafar Awwal) and then immediately leaves Makkah for Jeddah airport without doing a second Tawaf?
optionsEn: They owe a Dam for missing Tawaf al-Wada'
As affirmed by Ibn Baz, Ibn Uthaymeen, and Hanbali/Shafi'i rulings, Tawaf al-Ifadah performed right at departure fulfills BOTH Tawaf al-Ifadah AND Tawaf al-Wada' simultaneously!
explanationEn: Since Tawaf al-Ifadah WAS their very last act with the Kaaba before departing Makkah, the command of Sahih Muslim 1327 is automatically fulfilled.

questionEn: Should a pilgrim who performed Tawaf al-Ifadah on the 10th and then returned to Mina for Tashreeq ALSO rely on that 10th-day Tawaf as their Farewell Tawaf?
optionsEn: No! Because after the 10th they returned to Mina for 2–3 days before departing Makkah, they MUST perform a separate Tawaf al-Wada' after finishing Mina before leaving Makkah
Only if they stayed in Madinah
explanationEn: Tawaf al-Ifadah on the 10th was followed by days in Mina; therefore departing Makkah on the 12th/13th requires Tawaf al-Wada' afterward.

questionEn: When leaving Mina after the final stoning on the 12th or 13th, can a pilgrim stop at Masjid al-Haram directly with their backpack in a locker outside, perform Tawaf al-Wada', and head straight to Jeddah?
optionsEn: Only after sleeping 3 nights in Makkah
Yes! Doing Tawaf al-Wada' right after finishing Mina stoning and departing straight onward is smooth, clean, and mirrors the Prophet's ﷺ own swift departure
explanationEn: Just avoid bringing large rolling suitcases into the prayer mats/Mataf area; use hotel storage or mosque luggage lockers.

questionEn: Which two verses of Surah Al-Baqarah conclude the entire Qur'anic Hajj section right after discussing leaving Mina in two or three days?
optionsEn: Al-Baqarah 2:203 ('And remember Allah during [specific] numbered days... And fear Allah and know that to Him you will be gathered')
explanationEn: Notice how Qur'an 2:203 closes the Hajj legislation by lifting the pilgrim's gaze to the Final Gathering ('wa'lamu annakum ilayhi tuhsharun')—connecting the crowds of Mina to Judgment Day.

questionEn: On the 11th and 12th of Dhul-Hijjah, why is it important to avoid throwing pebbles from far away in a wild high arc over people's heads?
optionsEn: Throwing wildly from far back risks striking other pilgrims in the eye or head—walk calmly up to the front edge of the spacious circular wall and toss gently right into the basin
explanationEn: Every Jamarat bridge level gives ample circular perimeter right around the basin wall; stepping calmly near the rail prevents accidental eye injuries.

questionEn: What is the ruling if a pilgrim is in Mina on the 12th, stones all three pillars after Zawal, and is completely unsure whether they threw 6 or 7 pebbles at Jamrat al-Wusta?
optionsEn: Build upon the lower certain count (6) and throw 1 more pebble cleanly at Al-Wusta—and if already past Aqabah, also re-throw Aqabah's 7 if strictly maintaining sequence in Hanbali/Shafi'i view
explanationEn: When uncertain in worship, one builds on certainty (the lower count) and completes the remainder; counting each pebble quietly with 'Allahu Akbar' helps prevent doubt before stepping away.

questionEn: If a pilgrim gets separated from their tent group during Tashreeq nights in Mina and ends up sleeping in a hospitable stranger's tent (clearly inside Mina's boundaries), does that fulfill Mabit?
optionsEn: No, only your assigned camp number counts
Yes! Spending the night anywhere inside Mina's geographic boundaries fulfills Mabit completely regardless of tent number
explanationEn: God looks at presence inside sacred Mina, not tent barcodes; hospitality among strangers is part of Hajj's beauty.

questionEn: Can a pilgrim bring Zamzam water home in sealed airline-approved containers after completing Tawaf al-Wada'?
optionsEn: Yes! Sharing blessed Zamzam water with family and neighbors back home follows a beloved Sunnah practiced since Aisha (RA) carried Zamzam back to Madinah
No, taking Zamzam outside Makkah is haram
explanationEn: Aisha (RA) narrated that she used to carry Zamzam water in flasks, noting the Messenger of Allah ﷺ himself carried Zamzam back and sprinkled/gave it to the sick.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say regarding the spiritual state of a pilgrim returning home whose Hajj was accepted (Hajj Mabrur)?
optionsEn: They should boast of their title 'Al-Haji' proudly
They return purified of sin like a newborn—striving to protect that purity with steady Salah, humility, honesty in trade, and kindness at home
They no longer need to pray Fajr
explanationEn: Guarding the post-Hajj heart against pride ('I am Haji!') and returning to bad habits is the lifelong test of Hajj Mabrur.

questionEn: Which two prayers are recommended upon safely returning home from the Hajj journey?
optionsEn: Praying two light rakaat in the neighborhood mosque before entering home (the Prophet's ﷺ travel-return Sunnah), and reciting the arrival dhikr ('Ayibuna, ta'ibuna, 'abiduna, li-Rabbina hamidun')
Four rakaat at the airport runway
explanationEn: Ka'b ibn Malik and Ibn Umar (RA) transmitted both the Prophet's ﷺ custom of stopping by the local mosque to pray two rakaat upon returning from travel and the grateful chant 'Returning, repenting, worshipping, praising our Lord!'

questionEn: What is the complete Arabic wording and meaning of the Prophetic travel-return dhikr recited when coming home from Hajj?
optionsEn: 'La ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lah... Ayibuna, ta'ibuna, 'abiduna, li-Rabbina hamidun' (Returning, repentant, worshipping, praising our Lord)
explanationEn: Anas and Ibn Umar (RA) narrated the Prophet ﷺ repeated this humbled praise whenever returning from battle, Hajj, or Umrah.

questionEn: During the Days of Tashreeq in Mina, if a pilgrim hears news of a deceased Muslim and wishes to pray Janazah for them, where is Janazah most abundantly offered in Makkah?
optionsEn: After almost every obligatory prayer inside Al-Masjid al-Haram—offering huge reward for joining funeral prayers and reminding the heart of the Hereafter
explanationEn: Joining the frequent Janazah prayers in Masjid al-Haram earns qirats of reward like Mount Uhud while softening the soul.

questionEn: What is the ruling on a pilgrim throwing pebbles at the Jamarat while sitting in a wheelchair pushed by a companion?
optionsEn: Completely valid! Sitting in a wheelchair along the front edge of the Jamarat level and tossing 7 pebbles individually into the basin is totally sound
explanationEn: The Jamarat bridge has smooth wheelchair lanes; throwing directly yourself while seated is even better than delegating a proxy when you are able!

questionEn: If a pilgrim is in Mina on the 11th and 12th and forgets to say 'Allahu Akbar' out loud when throwing one or two pebbles, is their throw still valid?
optionsEn: Yes, the throw is valid because saying Takbir with each pebble is a Sunnah rather than a validity condition, though keeping 'Allahu Akbar' on the tongue is strongly recommended
explanationEn: Knowing Takbir is Sunnah prevents anxiety if one momentarily focuses on balance in a crowd, while remembering 'Allahu Akbar' keeps the heart centered.

questionEn: Why does the Prophet ﷺ warn pilgrims against lingering unnecessarily in Makkah after Hajj without performing Tawaf al-Wada'?
optionsEn: Because departing without farewell is rude to hotel staff
Because departing straight from a sacred sanctuary requires closing one's spiritual visit directly before the Lord of the House rather than drifting away distracted by markets
explanationEn: Ending Hajj in worship at the Kaaba anchors the entire pilgrimage in Allah's presence.

questionEn: What if a menstruating woman completed Tawaf al-Ifadah earlier, gets exempted from Tawaf al-Wada', and wishes to offer a heartfelt farewell to Makkah before boarding her bus?
optionsEn: She stands outside Masjid al-Haram (on the outer plazas/doors without entering the prayer sanctuary) or in her lodging facing the Qiblah, makes sincere dua and sends peace upon the Kaaba and Prophet ﷺ, and departs with zero guilt or penalty
explanationEn: Islam honors both her spiritual longing and her ritual exemption—making dua from outside the mosque lets her say goodbye with peace.

questionEn: During the Days of Tashreeq, why did the Prophet ﷺ deliver another brief address on the middle Tashreeq day (12th/11th) reminding the Companions about Qur'an and Sunnah?
optionsEn: To reinforce essential teachings while hearts were tender and gathered in Mina before tribes dispersed back across Arabia
explanationEn: Repeating core truths across Arafah (9th), Yawm al-Nahr (10th), and Mid-Tashreeq (11th/12th) ensured every delegation carried Islam's clarity home.

questionEn: What happens if a pilgrim does Nafar Awwal on the 12th BEFORE Zawal by mistake and boards a bus to Jeddah, realizing the error at the airport?
optionsEn: Since they left without valid stoning on the 12th after Zawal, if they can return before sunset of the 13th to stone cleanly, do so; otherwise they offer a Dam (for neglecting a Wajib day's Rami) and repent
They must do 3 Umrahs in Jeddah
explanationEn: Remember: never book departure out of Mina before Dhuhr/Zawal on the 12th so your 12th-day Rami is unambiguously valid in all schools.

questionEn: Can a pilgrim stay in Makkah for a week AFTER Hajj finishes to pray in Masjid al-Haram before doing Tawaf al-Wada' right before flying home?
optionsEn: No, every pilgrim must leave Makkah on the 13th
Only if they stay in Ihram
Yes! There is no limit on extending your peaceful stay in Makkah after Hajj ends—simply perform Tawaf al-Wada' as your very final act when actually departing Makkah
explanationEn: Many pilgrims enjoy serene post-Hajj days in Makkah once crowds clear before bidding farewell via Tawaf al-Wada'.

questionEn: Which pillar is STILL valid even if performed after the 13th of Dhul-Hijjah (e.g., on the 15th or 20th) for a woman who was waiting for menstruation to end?
optionsEn: Tawaf al-Ifadah (and its following Sa'i if due), because Tawaf al-Ifadah has no strict end-date cutting off validity
explanationEn: While Arafah ends at Fajr of the 10th and Tashreeq stoning ends at sunset of the 13th, Tawaf al-Ifadah remains open until completed—even days later once a woman becomes pure.

questionEn: If a pilgrim is in Mina on the 11th and wants to pray Jumu'ah if the 11th or 12th happens to fall on a Friday, what is the Sunnah?
optionsEn: Travelers in Mina follow the Prophetic practice: the Prophet ﷺ did NOT establish a separate Jumu'ah in Mina (though if Masjid al-Khayf holds Jumu'ah or one attends in Makkah, joining it is valid; otherwise pilgrims pray shortened Dhuhr 2 rakaat in Mina)
explanationEn: During the Farewell Hajj, the 9th (Arafah) was a Friday and the Prophet ﷺ prayed combined Dhuhr+Asr (not Jumu'ah) after a single Khutbah; travelers are not obliged to hold Jumu'ah unless following a settled city Jumu'ah congregation.

questionEn: What does the phrase 'Faman ta'ajjala fi yawmayn' ('Whoever hastens in two days') in Qur'an 2:203 count as the 'two days'?
optionsEn: The first TWO Days of Tashreeq (11th and 12th of Dhul-Hijjah), after Yawm al-Nahr (10th)
explanationEn: Yawm al-Nahr (10th) is Eid day; the 'two days' of hastening are the 11th and 12th, while delaying a third day is the 13th.

questionEn: Why do scholars discourage pilgrims from rushing to the airport immediately after Hajj without expressing gratitude and making dua for their Hajj group leaders, volunteers, and camp workers?
optionsEn: Because thanking people requires a Dam
Because the Prophet ﷺ taught: 'Whoever does not thank people does not thank Allah' (Sunan Abi Dawud 4811)—honoring cooks, cleaners, bus drivers, and guides completes Hajj's noble character
explanationEn: Recognizing the unseen labor of sanitation workers, tent staff, medical teams, and guides reflects true prophetic gratitude.

questionEn: When a pilgrim completes Hajj and visits Madinah afterward, what is the best way to spend time in Al-Masjid al-Nabawi?
optionsEn: Praying all five daily prayers in congregation (each worth 1,000 prayers), sending abundant Salawat and Salam respectfully at the Prophet's ﷺ grave and his two Companions, praying in Al-Rawdah, and visiting Masjid Quba
Performing another Tawaf around the Green Dome
explanationEn: Notice: Ihram is NEVER worn for visiting Madinah—Tawaf belongs solely to the Kaaba, and visiting Madinah honors the Prophet's ﷺ sanctuary with calm devotion.

questionEn: What is the ruling on performing 'Tawaf al-Wada'' at Masjid al-Haram BEFORE going to Mina on the 12th for final stoning, and then leaving straight from Mina to Jeddah?
optionsEn: Invalid as Tawaf al-Wada'! Because you must STILL return to Mina afterward to stone the 3 Jamarat, that Tawaf was NOT your final act before departing Makkah's boundaries—so you must perform Tawaf al-Wada' AFTER finishing Mina stoning (unless excused)
explanationEn: Wait until your final stoning in Mina is finished before performing Tawaf al-Wada' so it truly serves as your last act with the Kaaba.
reference: Fatawa Ibn Baz; Fatawa al-Lajnah al-Da'imah

questionEn: If a pilgrim is in Mina on the 12th and sees heavy rain pouring during the afternoon stoning, does rain excuse postponing stoning until later that evening?
optionsEn: No, must walk through flash floods
Yes! Stoning after Zawal extends all evening and night; waiting inside the tent until rain/flash flooding subsides protects life without any penalty
Must throw pebbles from inside the tent
explanationEn: Taking shelter during heavy storms and stoning calmly once skies clear avoids slip hazards along the bridge ramps.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about the virtue of throwing EVERY single pebble at the Jamarat on the Days of Tashreeq?
optionsEn: In a narration reported by Ibn Umar (RA), every pebble thrown at the Jamarat becomes light (Noor) for the believer on the Day of Judgment
explanationEn: Viewing each small pebble not as a mechanical chore but as obedient light for the Akhirah transforms the walk to the Jamarat.

questionEn: What is the rule if a pilgrim uses a walking cane or mobility walker while performing Tawaf al-Wada'?
optionsEn: Completely permissible and valid—just ensure the cane tip is clean and does not trip fellow pilgrims
explanationEn: Supporting elderly mobility with canes or walkers preserves independence safely.

questionEn: After Tawaf al-Wada', what should a pilgrim drink as a final blessing before leaving Masjid al-Haram?
optionsEn: Fresh Zamzam water, thanking Allah and asking Him for beneficial knowledge, abundant lawful provision, and healing from every ailment
explanationEn: Drinking Zamzam with Ibn Abbas's (RA) dua ('Allahumma inni as'aluka 'ilman nafi'an, wa rizqan wasi'an, wa shifa'an min kulli da'') closes the visit beautifully.

questionEn: If a pilgrim performed Hajj on behalf of a deceased parent (Hajj al-Badal), should they also perform Tawaf al-Wada' at the end of that Hajj?
optionsEn: No, proxy pilgrims skip Tawaf al-Wada'
Yes! A proxy performs every pillar and Wajib of that Hajj—including Tawaf al-Wada'—on the same Prophetic model
explanationEn: A proxy discharges the full Hajj seamlessly from Miqat Ihram through Tawaf al-Wada'.

questionEn: What if a pilgrim loses all their money or belongings during Tashreeq in Mina—how does Islam encourage fellow pilgrims to respond?
optionsEn: Generously share meals, shelter, and emergency funds—embodying the Brotherhood of Hajj and earning immense reward in Allah's sanctuary
explanationEn: Helping a distressed traveler (Ibn al-Sabil) is an explicit Qur'anic charity category (9:60)—even sweeter when done inside Mina.

questionEn: Why is it vital NOT to rush out of Mina on the 12th in panic without checking if everyone in your family/elderly group is accounted for?
optionsEn: Because abandoning vulnerable family members in exit crowds causes severe distress and violates caring leadership; always verify every group member's safety and ID
explanationEn: Calm group accountability reflects the Prophet's ﷺ own careful oversight of women and weaker Companions.

questionEn: When a pilgrim returns home and friends visit to congratulate them, what is the best way to speak about their Hajj experience?
optionsEn: Complain endlessly about hotel food and buses
Speak with gratitude for Allah's mercy, highlight the spiritual majesty of Arafah and unity of the Ummah, and hide minor logistical inconveniences so others long to visit Allah's House
explanationEn: Speaking gratefully of Makkah and Madinah inspires love for Allah's House in the hearts of young and old back home.

questionEn: What is the ruling on people calling a returning pilgrim 'Haji' or 'Hajjah'?
optionsEn: It is an obligatory pillar of Islam
It is a harmless cultural sign of respect in many communities, provided the pilgrim never demands the title out of vanity or expects superiority over fellow Muslims
Anyone not called Haji loses their Hajj
explanationEn: Humility stays silent when praised; early pious predecessors even disliked being singled out by religious titles lest pride enter their hearts.

questionEn: If a pilgrim made mistakes during Hajj (e.g., missed a Wajib and offered Dam, or got angry once), should they despair that their Hajj was rejected?
optionsEn: Yes, Allah never forgives Hajj errors
Never despair! Turn to Allah in sincere Istighfar, pay any required expiation, and trust His mercy—just as Ibrahim and Isma'il (AS) prayed while building the Kaaba: 'Rabbana taqabbal minna!'
explanationEn: Even after completing every ritual impeccably, true believers close with istighfar and Ibrahim's prayer for acceptance (2:127).

questionEn: Why does Qur'an 2:199 command 'And seek forgiveness of Allah (Wastaghfirullah); indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful' right at the culmination of the Hajj rites?
optionsEn: Because believers always conclude acts of worship with Istighfar—acknowledging that no human worship ever fully matches Allah's majesty without His pardon
explanationEn: Just as we say 'Astaghfirullah' thrice immediately after finishing every Salah, Hajj closes with humble repentance and hope in Al-Ghafur al-Rahim.

questionEn: In which Hijri year did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ perform his historic Farewell Pilgrimage (Hajjat al-Wada')?
optionsEn: 10 AH (roughly three months before his passing in Rabi' al-Awwal 11 AH)
explanationEn: After conquering Makkah in 8 AH and sending Abu Bakr (RA) in 9 AH, the Prophet ﷺ personally led the entire Ummah in Hajjat al-Wada' in Dhul-Hijjah 10 AH.

questionEn: On which exact date did the Prophet ﷺ depart Madinah toward Makkah for his Farewell Pilgrimage?
optionsEn: Around the 24th or 25th of Dhul-Qi'dah 10 AH (with four or five nights remaining in Dhul-Qi'dah), praying Dhuhr in Madinah and Asr at Dhul-Hulayfah
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) narrated the Prophet ﷺ set out from Madinah with five days left in Dhul-Qi'dah, bathed, oiled and combed his hair, put on his Izar and Rida, and camped overnight at Dhul-Hulayfah.

questionEn: Which great Companion authored the most complete, step-by-step eyewitness Hadith describing the entire Farewell Pilgrimage from Madinah to Tawaf al-Ifadah?
optionsEn: Jabir ibn Abdullah (RA), preserved in Sahih Muslim 1218
explanationEn: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq and Muhammad al-Baqir visited the aged blind Companion Jabir ibn Abdullah (RA), who recounted the entire Farewell Hajj in crystal detail.

questionEn: When Jabir (RA) described the sea of people surrounding the Prophet ﷺ at the start of the Farewell Pilgrimage, how far did the crowd extend?
optionsEn: 'I looked as far as my eye could see in front of him, behind him, to his right, and to his left—masses of riders and walkers'
explanationEn: More than 100,000 Muslims traveled with the Prophet ﷺ on his final pilgrimage, eager to learn every word and gesture.

questionEn: Why is the Farewell Pilgrimage also called 'Hajjat al-Balagh' and 'Hajjat al-Islam'?
optionsEn: Because it took place in Syria
Because it was the Prophet's ﷺ sole Hajj after Hijrah in which he conveyed (ballagha) the perfected laws of Islam and called Allah to witness
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ asked the huge crowd at Arafah: 'Have I conveyed the message?' and they roared 'We bear witness that you have conveyed, fulfilled, and advised sincerely!'

questionEn: After the crowd roared 'We bear witness that you have conveyed!', what unforgettable gesture did the Prophet ﷺ make toward the sky and the people?
optionsEn: He closed his eyes and slept
He threw stones into the air
He pointed his index finger upward to the sky and then downward toward the people, saying three times: 'Allahummash-had!' (O Allah, bear witness!)
explanationEn: Calling Allah as his Witness before over 100,000 Companions sealed the prophetic mission's completion with awe and tears.

questionEn: In his Farewell Sermon at Arafah, which pre-Islamic financial exploitation did the Prophet ﷺ formally abolish—beginning with his own uncle's wealth?
optionsEn: Riba (usury/interest), declaring: 'All Riba of Jahiliyyah is abolished under my feet, and the first Riba I abolish is that of my uncle Al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib—all of it is canceled!'
explanationEn: By canceling his own family's outstanding interest claims first, the Prophet ﷺ modeled absolute integrity in leadership.

questionEn: Which pre-Islamic cycle of tribal vengeance did the Prophet ﷺ abolish in the Farewell Sermon—again starting with his own clan?
optionsEn: Pre-Islamic blood feuds, declaring: 'All blood-claims of Jahiliyyah are abolished, and the first blood-claim I cancel is that of Ibn Rabi'ah ibn al-Harith' (his infant cousin killed during infancy)
explanationEn: Starting justice reform within Banu Hashim instantly dismantled tribal pride and generational cycles of revenge.

questionEn: What solemn charge did the Prophet ﷺ deliver specifically regarding WOMEN during the Farewell Sermon at Arafah?
optionsEn: 'Fear Allah concerning women! Verily you have taken them as a trust (amanah) from Allah, and made intimacy with them lawful by the word of Allah... treat them kindly!'
explanationEn: On the greatest gathering of human history in Arabia, the Prophet ﷺ enshrined marital dignity, financial maintenance, and compassionate treatment of wives as a sacred trust before Allah.

questionEn: What foundational declaration against racism and ethnic supremacy did the Prophet ﷺ proclaim during the Farewell Hajj sermons (recorded in Musnad Ahmad)?
optionsEn: 'O people, your Lord is One and your father [Adam] is one. An Arab has no superiority over a non-Arab, nor a non-Arab over an Arab, nor white over black, nor black over white—except by Taqwa (piety)'
explanationEn: Delivered in the middle of the Days of Tashreeq during the Farewell Hajj, this timeless proclamation remains Islam's charter of racial equality.

questionEn: What unbreakable anchor of guidance did the Prophet ﷺ tell the Ummah he was leaving behind with them at Arafah so they would never go astray?
optionsEn: 'I have left among you that which if you hold fast to it you will never go astray after me: the Book of Allah (the Qur'an)'—alongside his Sunnah/family teachings in complementary narrations
explanationEn: In Sahih Muslim 1218 he pointed directly to the Book of Allah, and in Al-Muwatta'/Al-Hakim paired it with his Prophetic Sunnah.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ warn his followers NOT to fall back into after his passing during the Farewell Sermon?
optionsEn: 'Do not revert after me into disbelievers striking one another's necks (shedding each other's blood)'
explanationEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari 1739 and 1741, Jarir and Abu Bakrah (RA) transmitted this urgent plea against sectarian bloodshed and infighting.

questionEn: On which exact date did the Prophet ﷺ enter Makkah during the Farewell Pilgrimage?
optionsEn: On Sunday morning, the 4th of Dhul-Hijjah 10 AH (entering from Kada' / Upper Makkah in daylight)
explanationEn: Jabir and Ibn Abbas (RA) narrated the Prophet ﷺ arrived in Makkah on Sunday morning the 4th of Dhul-Hijjah, giving him four full days in Al-Abtah before heading to Mina on Thursday the 8th.

questionEn: Where did the Prophet ﷺ stay in Makkah from the 4th until the morning of the 8th of Dhul-Hijjah during his Farewell Hajj?
optionsEn: In a tent pitched at Al-Abtah (outside the main houses of Makkah), praying Qasr (shortened prayers) until heading to Mina on the 8th
explanationEn: Staying humbly in a simple tent at Al-Abtah rather than reclaiming old properties emphasized his detachment and status as a traveler before Allah.

questionEn: What did Suraqah ibn Malik (RA) ask the Prophet ﷺ right at the base of Jamrat al-Aqabah when the Prophet ﷺ commanded the Companions to turn Hajj into Umrah (Tamattu')?
optionsEn: 'O Messenger of Allah, is this Umrah-into-Hajj (Tamattu') only for this year of ours, or forever?'—and the Prophet ﷺ interlaced his fingers saying: 'No, forever and ever!'
explanationEn: Suraqah's bold question secured explicit Prophetic confirmation that Tamattu' remains permanent for every generation until Judgment Day.

questionEn: Which two Companions came from Yemen during the Farewell Hajj bringing the Hady camels with Ali (RA) or meeting the Prophet ﷺ, and had different Ihram stories?
optionsEn: Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA)—who brought Hady from Yemen and stayed in Qiran with the Prophet ﷺ—and Abu Musa al-Ash'ari (RA), who did not bring Hady and was told to exit Ihram after Umrah
explanationEn: Both Ali and Abu Musa (RA) had said 'Labbayka bima ahalla bihi Rasulullahi ﷺ,' yet because Ali had driven sacrificial camels with him, he remained in Ihram alongside the Prophet ﷺ.

questionEn: What touching incident occurred between Ali (RA) and Fatimah (RA) in Makkah during the Farewell Hajj that shows how clearly the Prophet ﷺ settled misunderstandings?
optionsEn: When Ali returned from Yemen, he found Fatimah had exited Ihram (wearing dyed clothes and kohl) per the Prophet's ﷺ order; surprised, Ali went to ask the Prophet ﷺ, who smiled and confirmed: 'She spoke the truth—I commanded her to do that!'
explanationEn: Even the noblest household sought verification directly from the Prophet ﷺ rather than nursing suspicion.

questionEn: When Aisha (RA) cried at Sarif because her menses started right after entering Ihram for Umrah, how did the Prophet ﷺ comfort her?
optionsEn: He sent her back to Madinah
He tenderly told her: 'This is a matter Allah has decreed upon the daughters of Adam; so perform all the rites a pilgrim performs, except do not circumambulate the House until you are pure'
He told her to skip Arafah
explanationEn: This gentle, reassuring narration remains the bedrock of menstrual fiqh for millions of female pilgrims every year.

questionEn: Where did the Prophet ﷺ instruct Abdur-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr (RA) to take his sister Aisha (RA) after the Farewell Hajj rites concluded so her wish for an independent Umrah would be fulfilled?
optionsEn: All the way back to Madinah
To Al-Tan'im (just outside Makkah's Haram boundary), where she entered Ihram for Umrah on the night of Al-Hasbah (13th–14th Dhul-Hijjah)
explanationEn: Today 'Masjid Aisha' stands at Al-Tan'im honoring that tender moment of prophetic care for Aisha's (RA) heart.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about the sacred months and the abolition of 'Nasi'' (intercalation / postponing sacred months) during his Farewell Sermon at Mina?
optionsEn: 'Time has turned back to its original cycle as on the day Allah created the heavens and the earth: the year is twelve months, of which four are sacred—three consecutive (Dhul-Qi'dah, Dhul-Hijjah, Muharram) and Rajab of Mudar between Jumada and Sha'ban'
explanationEn: Pre-Islamic Arabs tampered with the lunar calendar (Qur'an 9:37) to manipulate war months; the Farewell Sermon permanently restored the pure 12-month lunar calendar.

questionEn: Which four months did the Prophet ﷺ reaffirm as the Four Sacred Months (Al-Ashhur al-Hurum) in his Farewell Hajj address?
optionsEn: Dhul-Qi'dah, Dhul-Hijjah, Muharram (three consecutive), and Rajab (standing alone between Jumada al-Akhirah and Sha'ban)
explanationEn: Notice that two of the four sacred months (Dhul-Qi'dah and Dhul-Hijjah) directly shelter the Hajj season!

questionEn: What famous warning about Shaytan did the Prophet ﷺ deliver during the Farewell Sermon at Arafah/Mina?
optionsEn: 'Shaytan has despaired of ever being worshipped in this land of yours, yet he will be pleased to be obeyed in lesser things that you deem trivial—so beware of him for your religion!'
explanationEn: Warning believers against belittling 'small' sins and everyday disobedience keeps the Ummah vigilant long after idols are gone.

questionEn: During the Farewell Sermon, what rule did the Prophet ﷺ clarify regarding trusts (Amanat) and borrowed items?
optionsEn: Borrowed things need never be returned
'Every trust must be returned to its rightful owner; a loaned item must be returned, a guarantee is liable, and a debt must be repaid'
explanationEn: Alongside worship and equality, the Farewell Sermon underscored strict honesty in financial trusts and debts.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ state in the Farewell Sermon regarding criminal accountability and inheriting guilt?
optionsEn: 'No soul commits a crime except upon itself—neither a father is held liable for his son's crime, nor a son for his father's crime!'
Entire tribes are punished for one man's sin
explanationEn: Echoing Qur'an 6:164 ('No bearer of burdens bears the burden of another'), this ended collective tribal blood-revenge forever.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ tell the Companions on the Day of Sacrifice in the Farewell Hajj: 'I do not know—perhaps I shall not meet you here again after this year of mine'?
optionsEn: He planned to retire in Yemen
He sensed his earthly mission was nearing its close—giving the pilgrimage the enduring name 'Hajjat al-Wada'' (the Farewell Pilgrimage)
He wanted them to stop Hajj
explanationEn: Just ~81 days after standing at Arafah, the Prophet ﷺ passed away in Madinah, making his every word and action in 10 AH a parting testament.

questionEn: What happened to the Prophet's ﷺ voice and physical frame when he heard the revelation of Qur'an 5:3 ('Today I have perfected your religion') at Arafah—and why did Umar (RA) weep when he heard it?
optionsEn: Umar wept because he realized that once a thing reaches perfection, its completion signals nothing remains except departure (the Prophet's ﷺ imminent passing)!
explanationEn: Umar's (RA) deep spiritual insight—realizing 'after perfection comes only decline/departure'—showed how intimately he understood the Prophet's ﷺ life.

questionEn: When the Prophet ﷺ prayed behind Maqam Ibrahim after his arrival Tawaf on the 4th of Dhul-Hijjah, which two Surahs did he recite?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Kafirun (109) in the first raka'ah and Surah Al-Ikhlas (112) in the second raka'ah—the two Surahs of pure Tawhid
explanationEn: Just as he opened his mornings in Sunnah Fajr with pure rejection of shirk (Al-Kafirun) and affirmation of Allah's Oneness (Al-Ikhlas), he sealed Tawaf with them.

questionEn: During the Farewell Hajj, how did the Prophet ﷺ explain the importance of listening to upright leadership even from the humblest background?
optionsEn: 'Even if a mutilated enslaved Abyssinian is appointed over you who leads you by the Book of Allah, listen to him and obey'
explanationEn: Preserved by Umm al-Husayn (RA) in Sahih Muslim 1298 from the Farewell Hajj, this crushed Arab aristocracy and grounded authority purely in fidelity to Allah's Book.

questionEn: Which female Companion held onto the Prophet's ﷺ mount or observed Bilal and Usamah shading him while riding toward Jamrat al-Aqabah on Yawm al-Nahr?
explanationEn: Umm al-Husayn (RA) witnessed Bilal holding the camel's halter and Usamah holding a garment over the Prophet's ﷺ head against the heat as he stoned Jamrat al-Aqabah.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ do with the Key of the Kaaba during his earlier entry vs the Farewell Hajj—confirming who held custody permanently?
optionsEn: He threw the key into the sea
He gave it to Persian governors

At the Conquest of Makkah (8 AH) he returned the key permanently to Uthman ibn Talhah (Banu Shaybah) saying: 'Take it eternally; none shall seize it from you except an oppressor'—honoring trusts (Qur'an 4:58)
He kept it locked in Madinah
explanationEn: Banu Shaybah continue to hold the honored custody (sidanah) of the Kaaba's key to this day.

questionEn: What remarkable scene occurred at the Farewell Hajj when Al-Abbas (RA) offered the Prophet ﷺ a cup of Nabidh (date-infused water) from the pilgrims' Siqayah basin?
optionsEn: When told hands had dipped into it, the Prophet ﷺ humbly said 'Give it to me!' and drank it—honoring the public service and showing graciousness toward the volunteers
explanationEn: Reported by Ibn Abbas (RA) in Sunan Abi Dawud/Musnad Ahmad, the Prophet ﷺ refused elitism and drank from the same communal basin serving ordinary pilgrims.

questionEn: In the Farewell Hajj, how did the Prophet ﷺ treat the man who kept asking 'I shaved before sacrificing' and others who erred in order?
optionsEn: With warm reassurance ('Do it, no harm!'), without shaming, scolding, or imposing harsh penalties on anxious pilgrims
explanationEn: Ease and mercy characterized his entire teaching style at Mina.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say in his Farewell Sermon about the duty of every listener to pass his teachings onward?
optionsEn: 'Let the one who is present convey it to the one who is absent; perhaps a person to whom it is conveyed will comprehend and preserve it better than the one who heard it directly'
explanationEn: Abu Bakrah (RA) transmitted this famous mandate fueling generations of accurate Hadith preservation across the globe.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ pause to spend one night at Dhu Tuwa (just outside Makkah) on Saturday night before entering Makkah on Sunday morning (4th Dhul-Hijjah)?
optionsEn: To bathe (take Ghusl), pray Fajr cleanly, and enter the Sacred City in full daylight with dignity and humility
explanationEn: Ibn Umar (RA) faithfully imitated this Sunnah of bathing at Dhu Tuwa before entering Makkah in daylight.

questionEn: How many Umrahs did the Prophet ﷺ perform in total during his lifetime, and when did they occur?
optionsEn: Four Umrahs—all in Dhul-Qi'dah (except the one combined with his Farewell Hajj in 10 AH): Hudaybiyyah (6 AH), Umrat al-Qada (7 AH), Ji'ranah (8 AH), and his Hajj Umrah (10 AH)
explanationEn: Anas (RA) recorded these exact four Umrahs in Sahih al-Bukhari 1778, showing the Prophet ﷺ prioritized quality over multiplying Umrahs.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ exit Makkah quickly after Tawaf al-Wada' at dawn rather than lingering days after Hajj?
optionsEn: To return swiftly to Madinah where his mosque, community, and responsibilities awaited—leaving Makkah while hearts were still glowing from worship
Because Makkah ran out of water
explanationEn: Having conquered Makkah in 8 AH, the Prophet ﷺ remained faithful to his promise to the Ansar never to abandon Madinah.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say when his she-camel Al-Qaswa' was driven onto the desert road back to Madinah after Hajj—how did he remember the Kaaba?
optionsEn: He had deep lifelong love for Makkah ('By Allah, you are the best of Allah's earth and the most beloved land of Allah to me'), while honoring his covenant with the Ansar in Madinah
explanationEn: Makkah and Madinah together form the twin beating heart of Islamic devotion.
